points.requirement: A natural cytokine binds a receptor and relays a signal that can influence gene activity; the pictured relay is a selected schematic, not a universal molecular pathway.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cytokines are signalling proteins whose binding to a suitable receptor changes signalling and gene expression in a receiving cell. Autocrine action is on the producing cell, paracrine action is on neighbours, and endocrine action is at a distance, for example after entry into the circulation. Distant action is possible rather than the default for every cytokine (British Society for Immunology, Cytokines: Introduction). Chemokines are a cytokine family involved in cell recruitment and can also affect leukocyte activation (NLM MeSH, Chemokines). The information-versus-fuel distinction is a reading rule: a measured amount of signalling protein does not measure the energy available to the cell, and a message without the relevant receptor and response machinery does not establish a response.
evidence.explanation: The receiving receptor and downstream gene/signaling response are explicit; the drawn relay remains schematic. Source/depth references: scientific-authoring-bodies-13-2026-11-13/source-group-register.json#cytokine-and-control. Specific synthetic inputs and designed responses, natural receptor signaling and distinct activity/elimination mechanisms. The complete product and withdrawn-input consequences remain separately measured. Fictional counts/volumes and simplified shapes/ordered gates are not measured outcomes, personal decisions or a validated clinical algorithm. Personal-case material is excluded.

points.requirement: A synthetic cytokine receptor can connect a selected input to a selected growth/survival/function response, whose effect depends on design and context.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A synthetic cytokine receptor is an engineered cell-surface protein that connects a specified input to intracellular signalling. It differs from engineering a soluble cytokine or simply administering a cytokine. Some designs require an externally supplied ligand; others generate ligand-independent signalling. The receptor domains, input, expression and cell type define the tested construct. A growth-supporting signal does not itself establish antigen recognition, entry into a tumour, completed killing or durable patient benefit.
evidence.explanation: Specified engineered inputs and design/context limits replace a universal growth claim. Source/depth references: scientific-authoring-bodies-13-2026-11-13/source-group-register.json#cytokine-and-control. Specific synthetic inputs and designed responses, natural receptor signaling and distinct activity/elimination mechanisms. The complete product and withdrawn-input consequences remain separately measured. Fictional counts/volumes and simplified shapes/ordered gates are not measured outcomes, personal decisions or a validated clinical algorithm. Personal-case material is excluded.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Engelowski and colleagues joined fluorescent-protein-binding nanobodies to selected cytokine-receptor membrane and intracellular domains. points.requirement: CAR target recognition and an added receptor that influences cell behavior are distinct jobs; neither job guarantees the other.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a 2010 human T-cell study, a chimeric receptor joined the IL-4 receptor binding region to an IL-2/IL-15 receptor signalling component. IL-4 supported expansion of the engineered cells, while a separate CAR specified the tumour target. The reported culture experiments distinguished expansion, cytokine dependence and target-cell killing; they were not patient efficacy results.
evidence.explanation: Added support and the separate CAR recognition route have different jobs. The complete product and withdrawn-input consequences remain separately measured. Fictional counts/volumes and simplified shapes/ordered gates are not measured outcomes, personal decisions or a validated clinical algorithm. Personal-case material is excluded.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Read each supportive feature as a testable hypothesis. A drug-triggered signal needs a baseline and a withdrawal test; an antigen-triggered signal needs testing after cells leave the priming site. Constitutive signalling raises different growth and cell-state questions, while a secreted payload can affect neighbouring cells or circulate. Orthogonal means sufficiently separate from natural partners under tested conditions, not selectivity established by its name. The supportive receptor does not specify the CAR target, and changing an internal signal is different from secreting a cytokine. An added support signal does not by itself demonstrate adequate oxygen, tissue access, recognition of an absent antigen or patient benefit.

points.requirement: DNA, mRNA and receptor proteins are different objects; transcription and translation are separate steps.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Replication makes DNA from DNA. Transcription uses a DNA template to make RNA. Translation reads the coding sequence of a message in three-base codons to build a polypeptide; the transcript and reading frame matter. Functional noncoding RNAs do not need to become protein. Reverse transcription copies RNA into DNA in relevant viral and retrotransposon contexts. This information-flow map is not a guarantee that every DNA change produces a measured RNA or protein change.

points.requirement: Reaching and entering tumour tissue is a separate barrier from antigen recognition.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rise in engineered cells in blood with few found in two tumour biopsies leaves distribution and infiltration unresolved. Blood abundance is not entry into a mass of tissue, and a biopsy represents its sampled place and time. If a receptor works in a simple culture but killing falls in a more complex model with the target still present, investigate access, cell state and the model’s other features with controlled perturbations. The contrast alone does not identify a macrophage, vessel or signalling pathway as the cause, or show that more expansion will solve it. Expression of PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3 or TIGIT, or a count of macrophages or suppressor cells, does not by itself establish which input caused the functional difference. Trafficking toward a site and infiltration into tissue are different steps, and vessel number does not measure perfusion. Chronic stimulation, low oxygen, limited nutrients and inhibitory signals are different hypotheses; exhaustion describes cell states rather than physical tiredness.

points.requirement: Tumour cells may differ in target expression; adding T cells does not replace a missing target.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional population of 100 cancer cells, 80 display target X and 20 do not. Killing the X-positive 80 leaves 20 survivors; ten times as many effector cells does not create X on them. For two targets, suppose 20 cells carry both X and Y, 60 carry X only, ten Y only and ten neither. An idealised either-target rule covers 90 cells, whereas a both-target rule covers 20. These are recognition-coverage calculations, not measured killing or healthy-tissue selectivity. Expression thresholds, tissue access and cell function still matter.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional receptor kills X-positive tumour cells and normal airway cells that also display X: that is the on-target, off-tumour problem. If it also recognises Y on an X-negative healthy cell, that is off-target cross-reactivity. Binding or surface contact does not itself measure injury. Record tissue, assay sensitivity, staining intensity, positive fraction or calibrated molecules per cell, binding specificity, and healthy-cell killing or cytokine release at a named time; viable-cell tests consume the sample. Clinical organ injury is a further outcome in the actual population and regimen. A staining ratio, one negative panel or a control switch does not establish safety everywhere or guarantee reversal of an injury already present.

points.requirement: RNA, DNA and an unspecified carrier cargo are not interchangeable labels; no integration or clinical effect is inferred from the schematic.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

points.requirement: An intended diagnostic use binds the assay, specimen, result rule and corresponding treatment/use.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: FDA describes companion diagnostics as devices that supply essential information for a corresponding treatment. Their roles can include identifying likely benefit, increased risk of serious adverse effects or a specified monitoring need. The treatment label and diagnostic labeling retain the relevant disease, specimen, biomarker and decision rule. Some devices have documented group labeling for specified oncology therapies. Similar analyte names do not establish assay interchangeability, and a label-matched result does not guarantee individual benefit or complete clinical suitability.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Three examples separate intended uses. Validated ER immunohistochemistry in invasive breast cancer, with appropriate tissue handling, tumour-nucleus scoring and controls, has a marker-specific pathology and endocrine-treatment assessment role; it does not validate a new RNA score as a substitute. In a wholly fictional second example, assay T version 1 detects alteration M in fixed tumour tissue under rule R, and Drug A requires exactly that result in setting S. The stipulated match supplies that requirement within the exercise, without promising benefit; another specimen, result type or setting needs evidence for the changed use. A third fictional score Q combines RNA, spatial neighbourhoods and a derived culture response to propose Drug A. Reproducibility and biological support can justify research, but do not establish that Q-guided care improves outcomes against an appropriate comparator. A laboratory certificate does not supply that missing evidence. Useful research and an established clinical use can appear on different parts of one report.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: G1 prepares the cell, S copies DNA, and G2 precedes the mitotic phase. Mitosis separates nuclear chromosomes; cytokinesis separates cytoplasm into daughter cells. G0 describes a noncycling state, which need not mean death or loss of function. Cyclins, CDKs and checkpoints regulate transitions, and their alteration can contribute to cancer without making every checkpoint absent or guaranteeing error-free division. Cell-cycle checkpoints and immune checkpoints describe different biological processes.

points.requirement: The schematic follows G1, S, G2 and M, with an optional G0 state and conditional return.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: G1 prepares the cell, S copies DNA, and G2 precedes the mitotic phase. Mitosis separates nuclear chromosomes; cytokinesis separates cytoplasm into daughter cells. Cyclins, CDKs and checkpoints regulate transitions, and their alteration can contribute to cancer without making every checkpoint absent or guaranteeing error-free division. Cell-cycle checkpoints and immune checkpoints describe different biological processes.

In five primary glioblastomas, Patel and colleagues profiled 430 cells and inferred broad chromosome alterations by averaging RNA expression along chromosomes against normal reference profiles. points.requirement: A generalized human-cell cutaway distinguishes cytosol from nucleus, ER/Golgi/vesicle/lysosome lumens and mitochondrial compartments; organelles are not one required transport sequence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The nucleus houses most cellular DNA; mitochondria have their own genome and participate in energy metabolism and other processes. Ribosomes make polypeptide chains. The endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi process and sort selected membrane or secreted cargo, while lysosomes degrade delivered material in an acidic compartment. That itinerary is not the route of every protein. Cytosol is the fluid outside membrane-bound organelle interiors; cytoplasm includes cytosol and structures outside the nucleus. A vesicle lumen is not cytosol.
evidence.explanation: Cytosol, membrane-enclosed interiors and organelle structure are distinguished. The selected secretion route is expressly not an obligatory sequence through every organelle or an inventory of every human-cell subtype. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A nucleus has an inner and an outer membrane, pores and DNA associated with proteins as chromatin. Rough endoplasmic reticulum forms a membrane network with a lumen; its membrane connects with the outer nuclear membrane. The Golgi consists of flattened membrane sacs, while a lysosome encloses material for breakdown. A mitochondrion has outer and inner membranes; folds of the inner membrane are cristae, and the matrix lies inside it. Its genome is distinct from nuclear chromatin. This general description is not an inventory of every human cell subtype, nor proof that DNA can never occur elsewhere.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: DNA methylation changes a base’s chemical state without substituting the underlying sequence letter. Much human methylation analysis concerns 5-methylcytosine at CpG sites. Histone modifications affect DNA-associated proteins and are distinct from marks on DNA itself. Promoter methylation can participate in reduced transcription, while patterns elsewhere need their own interpretation.

points.requirement: In the same specified internal protein-coding transcript window,5prime-to3prime coding DNA is partitioned from the same left edge. Substitution at reference position5 changes A to C while retaining triplet grouping; RNA/splicing/translation are assumed or unmeasured, not observed.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Consider an invented internal coding-DNA window, read from the 5-prime to the 3-prime end with the same left-hand frame: ATG GAA TCC GCT AAC GGT, 18 bases. Changing A to C at reference position 5 gives ATG GCA TCC GCT AAC GGT and preserves the grouping. Deleting positions 4 to 6, GAA, gives ATG TCC GCT AAC GGT, 15 bases. Deleting only G at position 4 instead gives ATG AAT CCG CTA ACG GT, 17 bases, with changed downstream grouping. The final GT is an incomplete part of a continuing window, not a stop codon. These predictions assume the specified coding transcript and unchanged splicing; neither RNA processing nor translation was measured.

points.requirement: A chemical methyl mark on C does not replace that base with T; a C-to-T substitution changes the sequence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In an invented sequence example, AACGT can carry a methyl group on its C while the underlying base order remains AACGT. Keep that biological comparison separate from an assay that chemically converts bases: standard bisulfite treatment can change the readout without establishing that the original DNA carried a C-to-T variant. Read the conversion chemistry, locus and cell context before interpreting a methylation call.

Promoter methylation can participate in reduced transcription, while patterns elsewhere need their own interpretation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:

Its target coverage, origin checks, sample requirements and calling rule determine the claim. Genotyping, residual-disease monitoring and screening have different intended uses; a method label does not validate every use or locate the source of a plasma signal.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Splicing processes an initial RNA transcript. Exons are retained in a specified product and may contain untranslated sequence; introns are removed. For many nuclear pre-mRNAs, a spliceosome made of RNA and proteins recognizes boundary and regulatory sequences. The donor site starts an intron and the acceptor site ends it. Alternative choices yield transcript isoforms; a variant can alter exon inclusion, intron retention or use of a cryptic site. Exon skipping is not automatically a frameshift: the coding sequence and resulting joins matter. An altered message may undergo nonsense-mediated decay or produce a changed protein, but neither outcome follows from a prediction alone.

Cancer-associated splicing changes can arise through altered RNA-processing factors or their expression. SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1 and ZRSR2 illustrate studied factors; AR-V7 and BCL2L1 illustrate named transcript contexts. The linked review describes disease-specific mechanisms and therapeutic research. An altered transcript alone does not establish an intact abnormal protein, immune presentation, a therapeutic dependency or patient benefit. points.requirement: The paired interior bases are distinct from the sugar/phosphate backbone; a label leader must identify the intended component.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: DNA contains nucleotide chains with a sugar–phosphate backbone and the bases A, T, C and G. Complementary A–T and C–G pairing joins antiparallel strands. Nuclear chromosomes contain DNA associated with proteins as chromatin; nucleosomes organize DNA around histones. Mitochondria carry a separate genome. A gene is a functional region within DNA, rather than an entire chromosome. Replication copies DNA, while transcription produces RNA from a selected template. Packaging and gene presence do not establish active transcription or a functional protein.
evidence.explanation: The reader separates bases from sugar-phosphate backbones. points.requirement: A partial agonist has a lower maximum in the stated system, which differs from a full agonist observed at a low concentration.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A full agonist can reach a system’s maximal measured response. A partial agonist has lower activating capacity; its observed maximum depends on receptor amount and amplification and is not defined by giving a smaller dose of a full agonist. Competing partial agonists can reduce a full agonist’s response when they replace it. A neutral antagonist opposes agonist action without changing agonist-independent baseline activity; an inverse agonist reduces that activity when it is measurable. Antagonism need not use the agonist’s binding site.

points.requirement: Separate estrogen/ER and progesterone/PR examples depict classical intracellular transcription regulation, not anER-PR complex.

points.requirement: The classical example does not mean all hormone effects require transcription, all genes increase or every receptor permanently resides in the nucleus.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Receptors can be on the surface or inside a cell. Ligand-gated ion channels regulate ion passage; G-protein-coupled receptors act through G proteins; enzyme-linked receptors can contain an enzyme or recruit a separate one. A surface signal can ultimately alter genes, while nuclear-receptor family membership does not fix every molecule permanently in the nucleus or require every effect to use new transcription.

points.requirement: A selected serine-site kinase reaction transfers phosphate from ATP to the same protein oxygen, producing ADP and modified site. P denotes a phosphate group; molecule drawings are not protein abundance measurements.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Protein kinases commonly transfer phosphate from ATP to a substrate, producing ADP. Protein phosphatases remove phosphate by hydrolysis without regenerating ATP. points.requirement: An in-situ component within an intact duct boundary can coexist with a separate invasive component in surrounding stroma at one time; no inevitable transition or hole in this particular intact duct is asserted.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Ductal carcinoma in situ describes malignant epithelial cells within the ductal tissue boundary, without invasion identified in that component. An invasive component can coexist in the same specimen. Reading DCIS present does not cancel a separately reported invasive diagnosis. DCIS may be called precancer, noninvasive breast cancer or stage 0 disease; these terms retain the anatomical distinction and do not guarantee that every lesion has the same future risk.

points.requirement: Myoepithelial cells are living nucleated cells; the extracellular basement membrane is distinct from those cells and from their plasma membranes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Typical normal breast ducts and acini have luminal epithelial cells facing the lumen, an outer living myoepithelial layer, extracellular basement membrane and then stroma. Myoepithelial cells have contractile features that help move milk; they are not the chest muscle. Basement membrane contains matrix proteins such as laminins and type IV collagen, not living cells.

points.requirement: The fictional stain belongs to normal myoepithelial cells around a benign duct in one region and labelled malignant cells in another; attribute the signal to the actual stained population.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cimino-Mathews and colleagues found SOX10 nuclear staining in normal myoepithelial cells and in a subset of selected triple-negative and metaplastic breast carcinomas. Their series had 100 invasive cancers, with 38 of 58 basal-like, unclassified TNBC or metaplastic cases staining, compared with two of 42 luminal/HER2 cases. These selected-series frequencies are not universal prevalence or diagnostic sensitivity. SOX10 also occurs in other tumours, including melanoma and peripheral nerve-sheath tumours. Positive staining alone does not prove breast origin, and a negative result does not exclude breast carcinoma.

points.requirement: SOX10 alone does not establish breast origin, an RNA subtype/BL1 assignment, ancestry, dependence or treatment benefit. The labelled patterns are invented examples, not a scoring standard.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Basal-marker immunohistochemistry provides contextual protein evidence, not a stand-alone subtype from ribonucleic acid (RNA) or an exact lineage trace. SOX10 is the gene symbol for SRY-box transcription factor 10; the encoded protein is a transcription factor whose tissue assay commonly assesses nuclear signal. CK5/6 denotes cytokeratins 5 and 6, epithelial structural proteins, while EGFR means epidermal growth factor receptor and is also called HER1. Nielsen and colleagues evaluated an ER, HER2, CK5/6 and EGFR protein surrogate against expression-defined basal-like cancers and in a historical tissue series. A specified research panel is not equivalent to one marker reproducing a full RNA classifier.

points.requirement: TNBCtype-4 has four refined labels BL1,BL2,M,LAR. The qualitative four-column/five-row illustration is not empirical expression data, cell morphology, lineage, a best/worst ranking or an added IM/MSL/fifth group.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Lehmann's original TNBCtype system described six expression groups: BL1, BL2, IM, M, MSL and LAR. The 2016 TNBCtype-4 refinement retained BL1, BL2, M and LAR as tumour-focused profiles after evaluating immune and stromal contributions to the IM and MSL signals. Removed-profile samples were reassigned to their second-highest correlated tumour-profile centroid, not automatically to M.

BL1 is associated with cell-cycle/DNA-damage-response programmes; BL2 with growth-factor and myoepithelial-associated expression; M with motility and differentiation; and LAR with luminal and androgen-related transcription. These are classifier associations, not proof of one cause, functional repair deficiency or dependence on an inhibitor.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
The 2011 TNBCtype system included a mesenchymal stem-like profile with lower proliferation-related expression and mesenchymal/stem-like programmes. In the 2016 study, paired laser-capture analyses of epithelial-enriched and stromal regions showed a strong stromal contribution to this signal.

TNBCtype-4 removed IM and MSL as separate tumour-focused labels and reassigned those samples to their second-highest correlated tumour-profile centroid. MSL was not simply renamed M, and a whole-tissue call does not prove that only stromal cells contributed. Immune and stromal signals remain useful context. Claudin-low is another phenotype with its own classifier and cannot be inferred from an MSL name alone.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cortazar and colleagues' CTNeoBC analysis pooled 11955 patients from 12 trials. In triple-negative disease, attaining ypT0/is ypN0 was associated with event-free-survival HR 0.24 and overall-survival HR 0.16 versus not attaining pCR. This patient-level association is not a guaranteed personal outcome. The 95% confidence intervals were 0.18 to 0.33 for the triple-negative EFS association and 0.11 to 0.25 for OS.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: KEYNOTE-522 separately demonstrated endpoint and survival results for the whole perioperative regimen in previously untreated stage II or III TNBC. In the 2020 primary pCR analysis of the first 602 randomised participants, pembrolizumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy yielded 64.8% pCR versus 51.2% with placebo plus chemotherapy (difference 13.6 percentage points, 95% CI 5.4 to 21.8). The final 2024 overall-survival report covered all 1,174 randomised participants, including postoperative pembrolizumab or placebo: at 60 months, overall survival was 86.6% versus 81.7% (P = 0.002; median follow-up 75.1 months). Survival was measured directly; the pCR gain did not mathematically predict it or isolate which perioperative component produced the benefit.

points.requirement: Fibrosis alone establishes neither drug-specific response nor absence of cancer; pathological viable appearance is not a culture viability assay. The drawing assigns no individual stage or score.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: After preoperative therapy, fibrosis, necrosis, inflammation and histiocytic aggregates can be response-related tissue changes. Residual viable carcinoma is a separate morphological assessment, not a culture test of every cell. Response changes and residual cancer can coexist; scarring alone does not establish that no cancer remains. Fibrosis means collagen-rich scarring, necrosis means dead tissue and histiocytes are tissue macrophages.
evidence.explanation: Existing text distinguishes response-related changes, viable-looking residual carcinoma and culture testing, and states that prior injury can also cause repair. No complete response or drug-specific effect follows from fibrosis alone. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Lines of therapy describe successive treatment strategies under a clinical record or study's stated counting rule. First-line is the initial strategy for the specified disease setting. A later strategy may follow because treatment does not work, stops working or causes intolerable harm. The setting and reason for change belong beside the number.

In an advanced-cancer trial, first-line can mean no earlier systemic treatment for advanced disease, while previous treatment around surgery remains part of the exposure history and eligibility assessment. Several medicines, repeating cycles and planned blocks can belong to one strategy. A line count does not measure remaining life or establish that treatment options are exhausted.

points.requirement: The historical KEYNOTE-522-type stage II-III TNBC strategy comprises paclitaxel/carboplatin, anthracycline/cyclophosphamide, surgery and assigned postoperative immune treatment/placebo, with no dose or appointment schedule supplied.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Design (NEJM 2020): 1,174 patients with untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer randomised 2 to 1 to pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo every 3 weeks with four cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin then four of doxorubicin or epirubicin with cyclophosphamide, surgery, then nine cycles of adjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: KEYNOTE-522 tested a selected high-risk, previously untreated early-TNBC population, with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab or placebo before surgery and pembrolizumab or placebo afterwards. Eight planned 3-week preoperative cycles and nine postoperative cycles correspond to about 24 and 27 weeks; delays and clinical decisions can alter actual timing. The U.S. label describes tumour-size and nodal eligibility and enrolment regardless of PD-L1 expression. A stage label alone is not a personal treatment instruction. The complete regimen comparison did not independently randomise its two phases.

points.requirement: Pembrolizumab/placebo assignment spans preoperative and postoperative phases with no separate postoperative randomization; the whole strategy comparison cannot isolate the postoperative component.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The study question concerns the whole assigned sequence in previously untreated, non-metastatic stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer: T1c with N1 or N2, or T2 to T4 with N0 to N2, and performance status 0 or 1. The registry excludes prior checkpoint therapy and active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in the preceding two years, among other criteria. There was one assignment of 784 people to pembrolizumab and 390 to placebo across preoperative chemotherapy, surgery and postoperative treatment, without a separate postoperative randomisation. Smaller node-negative tumours outside those entry criteria and metastatic disease are different settings. Entry did not require PD-L1 selection, and the high-risk early-stage indication in the prescribing information has no PD-L1 threshold.
evidence.explanation: The trial note explicitly states one assignment across both phases and no separate postoperative randomisation. Fresh2020abstract confirms the sequence; component isolation is limited by the actual trial design, not inferred from pCRsurrogacy. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Neoadjuvant treatment precedes the main treatment, usually surgery; adjuvant treatment follows the main treatment to reduce recurrence risk. Perioperative treatment spans the period around an operation. Neoadjuvant therapy can aim to reduce disease before an operation and provides response information from treated tissue. Adjuvant therapy aims to reduce risk from disease that may remain. A pathological response and a later clinical outcome are different endpoints.

Timing comparisons need the actual population, intervention and comparator. Liu’s two mouse breast-cancer models supported testing preoperative immunotherapy, not a universal human timing rule or proof that retained tumour antigen explains every clinical result. KEYNOTE-522 assigned a complete before-and-after pembrolizumab regimen against its comparator; that design does not independently randomize the two phases and cannot isolate each phase’s contribution.
evidence.explanation: The trial note explicitly states one assignment across both phases and no separate postoperative randomisation. Fresh2020abstract confirms the sequence; component isolation is limited by the actual trial design, not inferred from pCRsurrogacy. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional one-hour recycling-station comparison starts with 20 waiting bags in each station. A receives 30 and processes 30, leaving 20; B receives five and processes none, leaving 25. Equal initial piles, including a six-bag schematic snapshot, cannot identify the rate or the later outcome. Bags are not LC3 molecules or assay thresholds: real markers are produced and removed, cargos differ, and a perturbation can affect several steps. Measure completion over time with appropriate controls. Even verified flow does not establish survival dependence; after a specific perturbation, more death can support a protective role, less drug-induced death can support a contribution to that death response, and changed flow with similar survival leaves timing or compensation as possible limits.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Flux, selected-cargo clearance and survival dependence are different claims. NBR1 experiments identify selective ubiquitinated-cargo handling, not a universal LC3 cargo census. Use time courses, viable-cell normalisation, verified lysosomal inhibition and independent perturbations; autophagy proteins can have other functions. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional one-hour recycling-station comparison starts with 20 waiting bags in each station. A receives 30 and processes 30, leaving 20; B receives five and processes none, leaving 25. Equal initial piles, including a six-bag schematic snapshot, cannot identify the rate or the later outcome. Bags are not LC3 molecules or assay thresholds: real markers are produced and removed, cargos differ, and a perturbation can affect several steps. points.requirement: Locate damage to vulnerable membrane lipids as distinct from a generic ROS increase; oxidation alone does not diagnose ferroptotic cell death.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Ferroptosis involves iron-dependent membrane-lipid peroxidation causing death. Erastin experiments implicated cystine uptake through system xc-, connecting cysteine and glutathione supply to antioxidant defence. Vulnerable polyunsaturated lipid chains, iron availability and cellular conditions matter; general reactive-oxygen fluorescence does not establish this mechanism.
evidence.explanation: The current field places the relevant damage in membrane lipids and rejects general oxidation fluorescence as a diagnosis. The fresh Dixon, Yang, Yang and Bersuker abstracts preserve their experimental systems and support lipid/iron/death distinctions. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Assigning ferroptosis needs convergent measurements of death, lipid damage preceding death, iron dependence and appropriately controlled rescue. Independent genetic and chemical perturbations strengthen attribution; rescue alone is not complete proof. A lipid-probe ratio and death fraction are different outputs, with no universal diagnostic staining threshold. Live death and rescue tests consume viable model material. Specify lipid-probe oxidation ratios and independently measured death percentages over a stated interval; a marker snapshot does not reconstruct the full causal sequence.

points.requirement: Protein abundance reflects synthesis and removal. points.requirement: An altered base, a bulky adduct, a copying mismatch and a double-strand break are physically different lesions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A DNA lesion is a physical or chemical problem; a mutation is a lasting sequence change. Repair can remove damage before a mutation is fixed. Recognition and checkpoint signaling are responses to the problem, whereas successful repair, tolerated damage, arrest and death are separate outcomes. The lesson map therefore ends by measuring the outcome instead of assuming that the alarm completed the repair.

Selected repair jobs address different problems: base excision begins by removing a damaged base, nucleotide excision removes a lesion-containing stretch, and mismatch repair corrects copying mismatches. Lindahl purified an E. coli enzyme that released uracil without cutting the DNA backbone, a specific early base-excision step rather than proof of all human repair routes. Double-strand breaks can use matching-template homologous repair or end joining. These are selected jobs, not exclusive assignments of every lesion to one pathway.

Gamma-H2AX is histone H2AX phosphorylated at serine 139. Rogakou 1998 observed a rapid response after experimentally induced double-strand breaks in mammalian systems. A microscopy focus is a response around damage, not direct sequencing of a break or a universal repair-failure test. In a fictional culture with a bulky lesion and increased gamma-H2AX, measure lesion removal over time with suitable controls before claiming nucleotide-excision failure, homologous repair deficiency or drug sensitivity.

Platinum agents can form DNA crosslinks; interstrand links block strand separation and require coordinated repair machinery. The Fanconi pathway links DNA-processing activities, and homologous repair can contribute to resolving replication-associated damage. This does not mean every platinum lesion is an interstrand link or that every HR-deficient tumor responds. A repair mechanism, an observed drug effect and clinical benefit in a defined population need separate evidence.
evidence.explanation: The selected jobs retain damaged base, lesion-containing stretch, copying mismatch and double-strand break as distinct inputs. points.requirement: Gamma-H2AX does not alone establish HR deficiency or drug sensitivity.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A DNA lesion is a physical or chemical problem; a mutation is a lasting sequence change. Repair can remove damage before a mutation is fixed. Recognition and checkpoint signaling are responses to the problem, whereas successful repair, tolerated damage, arrest and death are separate outcomes. The lesson map therefore ends by measuring the outcome instead of assuming that the alarm completed the repair.

Selected repair jobs address different problems: base excision begins by removing a damaged base, nucleotide excision removes a lesion-containing stretch, and mismatch repair corrects copying mismatches. Lindahl purified an E. coli enzyme that released uracil without cutting the DNA backbone, a specific early base-excision step rather than proof of all human repair routes. Double-strand breaks can use matching-template homologous repair or end joining. These are selected jobs, not exclusive assignments of every lesion to one pathway.

Gamma-H2AX is histone H2AX phosphorylated at serine 139. Rogakou 1998 observed a rapid response after experimentally induced double-strand breaks in mammalian systems. A microscopy focus is a response around damage, not direct sequencing of a break or a universal repair-failure test. In a fictional culture with a bulky lesion and increased gamma-H2AX, measure lesion removal over time with suitable controls before claiming nucleotide-excision failure, homologous repair deficiency or drug sensitivity.

Platinum agents can form DNA crosslinks; interstrand links block strand separation and require coordinated repair machinery. The Fanconi pathway links DNA-processing activities, and homologous repair can contribute to resolving replication-associated damage. This does not mean every platinum lesion is an interstrand link or that every HR-deficient tumor responds. A repair mechanism, an observed drug effect and clinical benefit in a defined population need separate evidence.

points.requirement: The selected sister-template repair route is conditional on a suitable template after DNA copying, not every break or cell state.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Double-strand breaks can be repaired through matching-template homologous recombination or several end-joining routes. Homologous repair often uses the sister chromatid after DNA copying. The substrate, available template and cell-cycle state affect which route can operate.

Preparing a double-strand break for homologous repair includes DNA end resection in the 5′ to 3′ direction, leaving protruding 3′ single-stranded ends. RAD51 helps a prepared strand find and pair with a complementary strand in matching duplex DNA, displacing the other template strand into a D-loop. DNA synthesis can then extend the invading end using the template. Synthesis-dependent strand annealing can finish as a noncrossover repair: the extended strand leaves the template and pairs with the other broken end. Other homologous-repair routes can have crossover outcomes, so using an intact template does not mean every repair leaves donor and recipient arrangements unchanged. Purified bacterial RecA structures reveal strand-pairing intermediates; they are not direct measurements of human RAD51 repair in a tumour.

Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Microhomology-associated joining uses short matching sequences after end processing. Theta-mediated end joining names a POLQ-mediated mechanism; finding short matches alone does not identify that enzyme. These routes overlap in outcomes without becoming interchangeable definitions.

Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. Resection exposes single-stranded regions for alternative joining, where short matches can align and intervening sequence can be lost. Purified-factor experiments, defined chromosome-break reporters and controlled cellular studies test particular substrates and factor dependencies, not a universal menu for every break.

A fictional top-strand sequence CA-GAC-TT|AA-GAC-GT has 14 base pairs before joining. A selected short-match product CA-GAC-GT retains seven, losing the four-base TTAA interval and one three-base GAC repeat. For a selected alignment of GAC with its complementary CTG sequence, trimming the unmatched TT flaps leaves seven paired positions and two backbone nicks to seal, without a gap to fill. Other substrates can require synthesis; this arithmetic and schematic geometry are not measured repair frequencies.

Sequence a repaired junction and measure a defined repair reporter, then perturb the proposed factor with specificity controls and, where feasible, rescue. Repair fraction, junction distribution and cell survival are distinct outputs. A deletion with microhomology is compatible with a joining route, but does not demonstrate POLQ dependence, selective killing or benefit from a POLQ inhibitor in a patient. Viable-cell and purified-component studies have model-specific input and material costs.
evidence.explanation: A matching template and cell-cycle/substrate conditions qualify the selected sister-chromatid route. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. None of these observations alone is the probability of clinical benefit.

Homologous recombination uses sufficiently matching DNA, often the sister chromatid after copying, to repair certain breaks. BRCA1 helps coordinate repair; BRCA2 helps RAD51 assemble on prepared single-stranded DNA to search and pair with a template. Template availability and cell-cycle state matter. In a fictional model with both functional BRCA2 copies lost, template-guided repair is impaired and alternative joining can leave deletions and rearrangements, but the sequence of a scar does not uniquely identify the cause or every protein that acted.

A low RAD51-focus count is interpretable only with adequate tumor cells, an appropriate cycling population and evidence that the cells experienced damage. Cruz 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived models and retrospective tumor specimens. Fixed tissue can support this functional-surrogate approach; functional does not always mean live drug culture. An inadequate sample is uninformative, and a research assay needs analytical and clinical validation for its intended use.

Telli tested scar-score associations with response to platinum-containing chemotherapy before surgery in triple-negative breast cancer; that result does not establish a universal PARP-inhibitor cutoff. Farmer demonstrated sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cell models, a separate evidence setting. The U.S. olaparib early-breast-cancer label specifies deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA findings, HER2-negative high-risk disease, prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy and companion-diagnostic selection. A tumor-only result or high scar score does not replace those criteria.

points.requirement: An invading strand pairs with a complementary donor strand and displaces a connected donor strand while the other broken end remains distinct.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Double-strand breaks can be repaired through matching-template homologous recombination or several end-joining routes. Homologous repair often uses the sister chromatid after DNA copying. The substrate, available template and cell-cycle state affect which route can operate.

Preparing a double-strand break for homologous repair includes DNA end resection in the 5′ to 3′ direction, leaving protruding 3′ single-stranded ends. RAD51 helps a prepared strand find and pair with a complementary strand in matching duplex DNA, displacing the other template strand into a D-loop. DNA synthesis can then extend the invading end using the template. Synthesis-dependent strand annealing can finish as a noncrossover repair: the extended strand leaves the template and pairs with the other broken end. Other homologous-repair routes can have crossover outcomes, so using an intact template does not mean every repair leaves donor and recipient arrangements unchanged. Purified bacterial RecA structures reveal strand-pairing intermediates; they are not direct measurements of human RAD51 repair in a tumour.

Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Microhomology-associated joining uses short matching sequences after end processing. Theta-mediated end joining names a POLQ-mediated mechanism; finding short matches alone does not identify that enzyme. These routes overlap in outcomes without becoming interchangeable definitions.

Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. Resection exposes single-stranded regions for alternative joining, where short matches can align and intervening sequence can be lost. Purified-factor experiments, defined chromosome-break reporters and controlled cellular studies test particular substrates and factor dependencies, not a universal menu for every break.

A fictional top-strand sequence CA-GAC-TT|AA-GAC-GT has 14 base pairs before joining. A selected short-match product CA-GAC-GT retains seven, losing the four-base TTAA interval and one three-base GAC repeat. For a selected alignment of GAC with its complementary CTG sequence, trimming the unmatched TT flaps leaves seven paired positions and two backbone nicks to seal, without a gap to fill. Other substrates can require synthesis; this arithmetic and schematic geometry are not measured repair frequencies.

Sequence a repaired junction and measure a defined repair reporter, then perturb the proposed factor with specificity controls and, where feasible, rescue. Repair fraction, junction distribution and cell survival are distinct outputs. A deletion with microhomology is compatible with a joining route, but does not demonstrate POLQ dependence, selective killing or benefit from a POLQ inhibitor in a patient. Viable-cell and purified-component studies have model-specific input and material costs.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. A low RAD51-focus count is interpretable only with adequate tumor cells, an appropriate cycling population and evidence that the cells experienced damage. Fixed tissue can support this functional-surrogate approach; functional does not always mean live drug culture. An inadequate sample is uninformative, and a research assay needs analytical and clinical validation for its intended use.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Genomic scars are historical patterns in sampled tumor DNA. They can remain after a surviving population restores homologous repair, so a scar result is not a direct measurement of current function or a guarantee of drug benefit. DNA extraction consumes material; purity, ploidy estimation, segmentation, specimen quality and algorithm version affect the reported result. Counts are not percentages of cells whose repair has failed.

Loss of heterozygosity means losing one parental version, with or without a reduction in total copy number. Abkevich 2012 counted LOH regions longer than 15 megabases but shorter than a whole chromosome in epithelial ovarian cancer analyses. Birkbak counted imbalanced regions reaching a telomere without crossing the centromere. Popova studied transitions between adjacent regions at least 10 megabases long in basal-like breast carcinoma. The original LST method estimated counts separately within each chromosome arm, excluding centromeric breaks, after filtering and smoothing variations smaller than 3 megabases. Segment filters and clinical score cutoffs are different rules.

A composite score can sum different scar features. Telli 2016 used the unweighted sum of LOH, telomeric allelic imbalance and large-scale transitions, with a predefined high-score boundary reported as 42 in the abstract, or a deleterious BRCA1/2 finding, in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials. The training population used to choose a boundary, the treated population used to test response, the assay scale and the intended use are different facts. A number on another assay cannot be read against this threshold without validation; a response association is not an interchangeable treatment-selection rule.

In a fictional, already filtered within-arm profile, a 12-megabase segment next to an 8-megabase segment fails the requirement that both neighbors be at least 10 megabases. A 12-megabase segment next to a 14-megabase segment meets that size component. This tests counting, not a 10-megabase deletion rule, present repair function or a clinical response cutoff. The original algorithm filters and validation population still apply.

points.requirement: Compatible ligatable blunt ends can be joined without sequence loss; c-NHEJ is not always inaccurate.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Double-strand breaks can be repaired through matching-template homologous recombination or several end-joining routes. Homologous repair often uses the sister chromatid after DNA copying. The substrate, available template and cell-cycle state affect which route can operate.

Preparing a double-strand break for homologous repair includes DNA end resection in the 5′ to 3′ direction, leaving protruding 3′ single-stranded ends. RAD51 helps a prepared strand find and pair with a complementary strand in matching duplex DNA, displacing the other template strand into a D-loop. DNA synthesis can then extend the invading end using the template. Synthesis-dependent strand annealing can finish as a noncrossover repair: the extended strand leaves the template and pairs with the other broken end. Other homologous-repair routes can have crossover outcomes, so using an intact template does not mean every repair leaves donor and recipient arrangements unchanged. Purified bacterial RecA structures reveal strand-pairing intermediates; they are not direct measurements of human RAD51 repair in a tumour.

Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Microhomology-associated joining uses short matching sequences after end processing. Theta-mediated end joining names a POLQ-mediated mechanism; finding short matches alone does not identify that enzyme. These routes overlap in outcomes without becoming interchangeable definitions.

Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. Resection exposes single-stranded regions for alternative joining, where short matches can align and intervening sequence can be lost. Purified-factor experiments, defined chromosome-break reporters and controlled cellular studies test particular substrates and factor dependencies, not a universal menu for every break.

A fictional top-strand sequence CA-GAC-TT|AA-GAC-GT has 14 base pairs before joining. A selected short-match product CA-GAC-GT retains seven, losing the four-base TTAA interval and one three-base GAC repeat. For a selected alignment of GAC with its complementary CTG sequence, trimming the unmatched TT flaps leaves seven paired positions and two backbone nicks to seal, without a gap to fill. Other substrates can require synthesis; this arithmetic and schematic geometry are not measured repair frequencies.

Sequence a repaired junction and measure a defined repair reporter, then perturb the proposed factor with specificity controls and, where feasible, rescue. Repair fraction, junction distribution and cell survival are distinct outputs. A deletion with microhomology is compatible with a joining route, but does not demonstrate POLQ dependence, selective killing or benefit from a POLQ inhibitor in a patient. Viable-cell and purified-component studies have model-specific input and material costs.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In G1, ORC binds origins and with CDC6 and CDT1 loads double MCM2-7 hexamers (licensing). At S-phase entry CDK2 and DDK (CDC7) convert MCM into the active CMG helicase (with CDC45, GINS), recruiting polymerases: Pol α-primase starts, Pol ε (leading) and Pol δ (lagging) extend, with PCNA as clamp, RPA coating single strands, and Okazaki fragments joined by FEN1/LIG1. Re-licensing within one cycle is prevented by CDT1 degradation (CRL4-CDT2), geminin, and CDK activity. Oncogenes (MYC, cyclin E, RAS) shorten G1, fire excess and ectopic origins, and cause origin-fork collisions and dNTP exhaustion, the root of replication stress. Chemotherapy exploits this: antimetabolites deplete dNTPs (5-FU, methotrexate, pemetrexed, hydroxyurea inhibits RNR) or terminate chains (gemcitabine, cytarabine); topoisomerase I poisons (irinotecan, topotecan, ADC payloads SN-38, DXd, exatecan) trap the enzyme ahead of the fork; platinum crosslinks block polymerases. POLQ, POLA1 and CDC7 inhibitors are experimental.

points.requirement: Under stated IdU-then-CldU 30-minute pulses and 2 kb per micrometre calibration, fictional 15 and 7.5 micrometre second tracks yield 1 and 0.5 kb/min.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Replication stress concerns difficulty copying DNA, including slow or stalled forks. A stalled fork can be protected and restart; it is not automatically a broken chromosome. Checkpoint activation, recovery, incomplete copying, damage and death are separate stages and measurements. High checkpoint-gene RNA or rapid proliferation alone does not establish fork stress, dependence or drug sensitivity.

RPA coats exposed single-stranded DNA and helps recruit ATR through ATRIP, initiating checkpoint signaling in biochemical and cellular experiments. Activated H-Ras in normal human-cell models produced hyper-replication before damage signaling and senescence. Bester studied HPV E6/E7 or cyclin-E-driven models in which nucleotide limitation disturbed replication and nucleoside supplementation in culture improved dynamics. These experiments do not recommend supplements or predict the behavior of every oncogene-bearing tumor.

In a fictional DNA-combing exercise, live cells receive a 30-minute IdU pulse followed by a 30-minute CldU pulse. At the stated example stretching calibration of 2 kilobases per micrometre, a 7.5-micrometre second track represents 15 kilobases copied in 30 minutes, or 0.5 kilobases per minute; a 15-micrometre track gives 1 kilobase per minute. Bester used those pulse times and calibration, but these example lengths are not that study's results and the calibration is not universal.

DNA-fiber measurements require viable cells that incorporate labels; extraction destroys sampled cells. Ordinary fixed pathology cannot retrospectively supply live-label tracks. Document pulse timing, labeling, stretching, track selection, cell-cycle distribution, model and comparison group. A lower population S-phase fraction is distinct from the speed of one selected molecule. Track length alone establishes neither the cause, breaks, restart nor death; checkpoint dependence needs a targeted perturbation and a separate functional outcome, without a universal patient-positive cutoff.

points.requirement: Class I PI3K converts PIP2 to PIP3, opposed by PTEN; lipid phosphorylation and AKT/mTOR protein-substrate phosphorylation are distinct measurements.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Class I PI3K phosphorylates a membrane lipid, producing PIP3; PTEN removes its position-3 phosphate. AKT and mTOR are protein kinases. A PIP3 lipid result and an AKT1 Ser473 phosphosite result are therefore different molecular measurements. Document specimen preservation, cell mixture, protein site, timing, exposure, comparator and total-protein normalization before interpreting a change as activity or dependence.
evidence.explanation: The existing field explicitly distinguishes Class I PI3K/PTEN lipid chemistry from AKT/mTOR protein phosphorylation. The native PIP2/PIP3 symbols show two versus three phosphate marks as a schematic, not full chemical topology. Maehama’s abstract identifies removal of the position-three phosphate in its defined tests. points.requirement: PIP3-associated AKT recruitment, PDK1 Thr308 phosphorylation and mTORC2 Ser473 phosphorylation are separate steps; one universal linear route is not implied.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

points.requirement: An acetyl mark, its BET reader and a mark-writing process are distinct.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
BRD4 is a chromatin reader that recognizes acetylated histones and helps regulate transcription. Its recognition pockets and other protein interactions can contribute different functions.

Engaging an acetyl-recognition pocket and depleting a whole protein are different interventions. In selected TNBC models with acquired BET-inhibitor resistance, cells remained dependent on BRD4 through bromodomain-independent regulation. Verify pocket engagement and depletion independently before comparing growth outcomes. Neither operation alone establishes clinical benefit or a vulnerability caused by an uncharacterized BET-family variant.

BET proteins read acetylated lysine marks; they do not write the acetyl mark. The family includes BRD2, BRD3, BRD4 and BRDT, with two bromodomains and an extra-terminal interaction region. BRD4 can recruit transcription-elongation machinery, but other bromodomain proteins are not all BET proteins and family members are not functionally interchangeable. A schematic that retains the same histone mark during pocket occupation and protein depletion isolates two different interventions. The fixed mark is a drawing convention rather than a measured unchanged acetylation state; the state of the mark needs its own measurement. A representative pocket also does not make JQ1 specific to BD1.

In a fictional culture, an engaged BET pocket probe leaves growth unchanged while independently controlled BRD4 depletion impairs growth. The findings can coexist if the remaining protein supplies functions the probe does not block, as the resistant-model work illustrates. Binding assays, chromatin occupancy, early RNA changes, later growth and death, general transcription effects and appropriate restoration controls answer different questions. Lower MYC RNA alone does not attribute a later effect to MYC.

French identified a BRD4-NUT fusion in the defined carcinoma; a fusion is a different biological alteration from an ordinary sequence variant. Stathis reported four people with confirmed BRD4-NUT carcinomas treated with OTX015/MK-8628 in compassionate use: two had rapid regression, with no randomized comparison or established survival benefit. The report described thrombocytopenia, including reversible grade 3 events and a grade 4 event in one patient. This small selected series does not establish efficacy across BET-altered tumors.

points.requirement: The common ligand-dependent Notch route uses membrane-bound ligand on a sender contacting a receptor on a separate receiver membrane, not membrane fusion or a free secreted ligand.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A ligand-bearing sender, receptor amount, received signal and growth dependence are separate observations. Locate malignant, vessel and other neighboring cells before assigning a Notch mechanism. Ligand on a vessel is not evidence that the tumor received the signal, and total receptor is different from a released nuclear intracellular domain.

Common contact-dependent Notch signaling begins when Delta-like or Jagged ligand on one cell engages a receptor on a neighbor. Ligand-regulated extracellular cleavage permits subsequent gamma-secretase-mediated membrane cleavage; the released Notch intracellular domain, NICD, can enter the nucleus and work with transcriptional partners. This route differs from an RTK phosphorylation relay and omits receptor maturation and sender mechanics.

Weng found activating NOTCH1 changes in extracellular heterodimerization or PEST regions in more than half of the studied T-ALLs. Agrawal identified predicted inactivating alterations in head-and-neck squamous tumors, suggesting a tumor-suppressor role there. An uncharacterized allele inherits neither direction from the pathway name; tissue, cell identity and alteration effect matter.

A fictional T-ALL culture with high nuclear NICD without a ligand-bearing neighbor, and lower NICD after gamma-secretase blockade, supports a ligand-independent activation hypothesis. A contact-blocking experiment that lowers NICD without changing growth instead supports reduced received signaling without demonstrating a growth requirement. Control general toxicity, contact conditions, independent pathway perturbations and compensation. Gamma-secretase also processes other proteins; responsive HES/HEY RNA and nuclear staining need validated assays and are not universal eligibility cutoffs.
evidence.explanation: The common contact route names separate ligand-bearing sender and receptor-bearing neighbour; fusion and soluble-ligand routes are not stipulated. points.requirement: Under the same stipulated upstream secretion block, intact destruction control and a downstream escape can yield different canonical beta-catenin nuclear outputs.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Canonical pathway output, dependence on secreted Wnt, growth dependence and clinical response are separate claims. Nuclear beta-catenin can reflect pathway signaling, whereas total beta-catenin also includes adhesion functions. Lower AXIN2 RNA supports an output effect with suitable controls, not selective killing or patient benefit. Wnt routes that do not use beta-catenin are outside this canonical readout.

Canonical Wnt uses Frizzled with LRP5/6 co-receptor machinery. Without an effective signal, the Axin/APC-organized destruction machinery and sequential kinase steps promote beta-catenin degradation; signaling can change that control and allow nuclear regulation with partners. PORCN supplies a lipid modification required for proper Wnt secretion in the studied systems. Blocking that upstream step need not overcome a downstream escape from destruction control.

Two fictional cultures have nuclear beta-catenin. Secretion blockade reduces the nuclear signal in culture A but not in culture B, where downstream bypass is stipulated. A supports a ligand-dependent hypothesis; B illustrates how an upstream block can leave a downstream output intact. The symbols represent qualitative readouts, not protein counts or a real drug dataset. Neither pattern alone establishes selective killing; measure viability and control intervention specificity.

Assays can measure localization, AXIN2 RNA or a defined transcriptional reporter, before and after a specified perturbation. Preservation, composition, global transcription effects, model validation and tissue consumption matter; there is no universal Wnt-high treatment cutoff. In Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study of 94 people with advanced solid tumors, AXIN2 fell in many paired biopsies while no RECIST responses were observed. Target-related output and tumor response must therefore be reported separately, alongside safety rather than a claim of demonstrated benefit.

points.requirement: Distinguish fibroblast cells from the broader stromal compartment containing matrix, vessels and other cell populations; stromal signal is not automatically malignant-cell signal.

evidence.explanation: The exact reader paragraph carries this learning requirement at its stated model, sample, measurement or inference scope: Distinguish fibroblast cells from the broader stromal compartment containing matrix, vessels and other cell populations; stromal signal is not automatically malignant-cell signal.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fibroblasts are cells; stroma is a broader compartment that also includes extracellular matrix, vascular structures and other cells. Fibroblasts can produce and remodel matrix and exchange signals with neighbouring cells. In the solid-tumour settings discussed here, a stromal signal is not automatically a malignant-epithelial signal. Sahai and colleagues describe diverse origins and states, without one marker or one effect shared by every cancer-associated fibroblast.

review.auditor: Coordinator scoped source and canonical-field assessment
review.rationale: Three complete scientific prompt bodies (14,870 bytes), two assigned whole native PNGs and two associated whole native v2 PNGs were freshly read/viewed, with both complete pinned parent versions. Eighteen frozen units comprise 13 canonical teaching requirements (11 current root representations and2 actual unmerged definition dependencies) and 5 authored-convention checks without canonical-coverage credit. Two construction rows remain partial: the old wrong Target leaders in both legacy images and the distinct blank assay display not clearly visible in v2. The pinned parent uses v2, not either assigned legacy PNG. Eighteen exact excerpts occur in 4 actual root and 2 separate actual-peer EntityDetail renders. Five complete abstracts,6 selected FDA body pages and selected NCI paragraphs retain their actual depth; no whole-paper or whole-guidance claim. No canonical, component, alias, relation, reviewer-stamp or artwork edits. No independent, expert, owner, learner, native-language, hosted/browser, hydration or accessibility acceptance.

points.requirement: Recognition is one part of a therapeutic design; connected formats add separate actions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A recognition molecule can be used as one component of a larger therapeutic design. Its ability to bind is one property of that component.
evidence.explanation: The dedicated unmerged binder owner supplies the generic component definition; a modality record is not substituted for that owner. Watson is a complete abstract about designed protein binders; Eshhar is a complete abstract about an experimental scFv receptor in a T-cell hybridoma. The generic component definition is a scoped synthesis, not a new clinical result. The dedicated definition remains an actual unmerged PR373 dependency, not a root integration.

points.requirement: The binder and the molecular target it contacts are distinct objects; purple and blue are drawing conventions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The antibody recognizes an accessible antigen; the attachment chemistry and linker affect stability and release; the payload acts through its own molecular mechanism.
evidence.explanation: Recognition and the recognized antigen are separate objects in the current ADC mechanism. The purple/blue labels remain a separately checked drawing choice. The FDA ADC selected pages describe antibody/fragment, linker and payload in cytotoxic conjugates. They do not cover every therapeutic cargo. Purple and blue are authored identifiers, not molecular properties. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: An accessible intended target can occur on cancer and healthy cells; recognition alone gives no tumour exclusivity or safety conclusion.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Healthy tissues can carry either recognized target
evidence.explanation: The current bispecific owner explicitly carries recognized targets on healthy tissue, with no safety conclusion from specificity alone. The selected NCI paragraphs name CD20 on B cells and some cancer cells in its rituximab example. This supports possible shared recognition, not a statement that every cancer antigen is equally accessible on all healthy cells. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Linking chemical cargo to recognition does not by itself establish entry, processing or usable payload at its action site.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Binding can support delivery, but uptake, processing, access to the payload’s target and cellular response require separate evidence.
evidence.explanation: Binding, uptake, processing, action-site access and response remain separate. FDA ADC printed pages 1 to 3 describe distinct constituent parts, release mechanisms and exposure considerations. The separate-test reading rule does not assume that every conjugate follows one guaranteed route. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: The illustrated soluble T-cell engager has distinct target-recognition and CD3-recognition arms binding different features on separate cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: CD20/CD3 lymphoma engagers illustrate one bispecific format: CD20 recognition connects to T-cell recruitment through CD3.
evidence.explanation: The named CD20/CD3 example and two linked scFv architecture jointly carry the illustrated distinct binding functions. Mack is one experimental construct, not a universal topology for every engager. Mack describes two scFv fragments joined by a peptide linker, one directed at CD3 and the other at epithelial 17-1A. The NCI paragraph gives a separate named CD19/CD3 example. These are illustrative architectures, not all engager forms. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The Mack construct joined two single-chain Fv fragments with a peptide linker in one compact protein; this is different from an IgG architecture with an Fc region.
evidence.explanation: The named CD20/CD3 example and two linked scFv architecture jointly carry the illustrated distinct binding functions. Mack is one experimental construct, not a universal topology for every engager. Mack describes two scFv fragments joined by a peptide linker, one directed at CD3 and the other at epithelial 17-1A. The NCI paragraph gives a separate named CD19/CD3 example. These are illustrative architectures, not all engager forms. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Bridging contact alone is not evidence of productive activation or target killing.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: T-cell engagers are proteins that bind a specified target and recruit T cells, often through CD3. A binding bridge does not by itself establish completed killing.
evidence.explanation: The registered engager TLDR explicitly withholds completed killing from a binding bridge. Mack measured cytotoxicity separately from binding. Bluemel reports different lysis despite similar target affinity in engineered CHO systems. The no-guarantee reading rule is an inference about evidence, not a new failure frequency. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: The cell-receptor example spans the T-cell membrane and links extracellular recognition to an intracellular signalling design.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A common CAR presents a binder outside the cell and signaling domains inside it, connected through a spacer and transmembrane region.
evidence.explanation: The registered CAR principle carries external recognition, transmembrane linkage and internal signalling. Eshhar used anti-trinitrophenyl scFv linked to gamma or zeta signalling chains in a cytolytic T-cell hybridoma. The selected FDA CAR guidance concerns ex vivo manufactured products and separates recognition from signalling. Neither supplies a general clinical outcome. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: A living-cell receptor and a soluble bridging protein are different formats; a floating antibody is not itself a cell receptor.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A dosed T-cell engager supplies a protein connecting target recognition to an available T cell. It does not itself install receptor instructions or supply engineered living responders.
evidence.explanation: The protein engager and receptor-bearing living cell are explicitly different administered/design objects. Mack concerns an expressed soluble bispecific protein; Eshhar concerns functional surface receptors in a cellular model. The FDA guidance discusses a living, genetically modified cell product. These object distinctions do not establish comparative efficacy. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The receptor is a protein; its encoding instructions and the living cell carrying it are different objects.
evidence.explanation: The protein engager and receptor-bearing living cell are explicitly different administered/design objects. Mack concerns an expressed soluble bispecific protein; Eshhar concerns functional surface receptors in a cellular model. The FDA guidance discusses a living, genetically modified cell product. These object distinctions do not establish comparative efficacy. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Function of the assembled product needs testing; receptor anatomy or a signalling symbol is not a measured successful response.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Binding, surface CAR expression, activation, proliferation and completed target-cell killing are distinct readouts.
evidence.explanation: Readouts and the schematic response arrow are explicitly separated from demonstrated expression or completed killing. The FDA CAR construct section calls for supporting recognition and signalling functions and evaluating hinge/linker/transmembrane contributions. Eshhar measured IL2 secretion and lysis in a defined model. A drawn signalling ray is not one of these measurements. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In this schematic sequence, simplified shapes and an arrow from recognition toward a response do not show that every cell expressed the receptor or completed killing.
evidence.explanation: Readouts and the schematic response arrow are explicitly separated from demonstrated expression or completed killing. The FDA CAR construct section calls for supporting recognition and signalling functions and evaluating hinge/linker/transmembrane contributions. Eshhar measured IL2 secretion and lysis in a defined model. A drawn signalling ray is not one of these measurements. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Delivery, function, safety and patient benefit are distinct questions, without a binding-to-benefit progression.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Two specificities do not establish that both targets are reached together, that binding produces killing, or that a molecule improves on a comparison treatment. Function, exposure, manufacturing quality and harms need evidence for the actual product and indication. A class containing approved drugs does not make every bispecific design an approved therapy.
evidence.explanation: Delivery, function, harms and comparative treatment evidence belong to the finished product; the binding result does not supply these unmeasured results. FDA ADC selected pages keep constituent exposure and safety/efficacy questions separate. The selected CAR pages distinguish product characterisation, nonclinical assessment and clinical studies. The separate-question rule supplies no patient-benefit estimate. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: An antibody-drug conjugate links a target-binding antibody to an active drug. Binding, delivery, release and drug action each matter, and normal tissues can also be exposed.
evidence.explanation: Delivery, function, harms and comparative treatment evidence belong to the finished product; the binding result does not supply these unmeasured results. FDA ADC selected pages keep constituent exposure and safety/efficacy questions separate. The selected CAR pages distinguish product characterisation, nonclinical assessment and clinical studies. The separate-question rule supplies no patient-benefit estimate. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.
