review.auditor: Coordinator scoped source and canonical-field assessment
review.rationale: Three complete scientific prompt bodies (14,870 bytes), two assigned whole native PNGs and two associated whole native v2 PNGs were freshly read/viewed, with both complete pinned parent versions. Eighteen frozen units comprise 13 canonical teaching requirements (11 current root representations and2 actual unmerged definition dependencies) and 5 authored-convention checks without canonical-coverage credit. Two construction rows remain partial: the old wrong Target leaders in both legacy images and the distinct blank assay display not clearly visible in v2. The pinned parent uses v2, not either assigned legacy PNG. Eighteen exact excerpts occur in 4 actual root and 2 separate actual-peer EntityDetail renders. Five complete abstracts,6 selected FDA body pages and selected NCI paragraphs retain their actual depth; no whole-paper or whole-guidance claim. No canonical, component, alias, relation, reviewer-stamp or artwork edits. No independent, expert, owner, learner, native-language, hosted/browser, hydration or accessibility acceptance.

points.requirement: Recognition is one part of a therapeutic design; connected formats add separate actions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A recognition molecule can be used as one component of a larger therapeutic design. Its ability to bind is one property of that component.
evidence.explanation: The dedicated unmerged binder owner supplies the generic component definition; a modality record is not substituted for that owner. Watson is a complete abstract about designed protein binders; Eshhar is a complete abstract about an experimental scFv receptor in a T-cell hybridoma. The generic component definition is a scoped synthesis, not a new clinical result. The dedicated definition remains an actual unmerged PR373 dependency, not a root integration.

points.requirement: The binder and the molecular target it contacts are distinct objects; purple and blue are drawing conventions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The antibody recognizes an accessible antigen; the attachment chemistry and linker affect stability and release; the payload acts through its own molecular mechanism.
evidence.explanation: Recognition and the recognized antigen are separate objects in the current ADC mechanism. The purple/blue labels remain a separately checked drawing choice. The FDA ADC selected pages describe antibody/fragment, linker and payload in cytotoxic conjugates. They do not cover every therapeutic cargo. Purple and blue are authored identifiers, not molecular properties. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: An accessible intended target can occur on cancer and healthy cells; recognition alone gives no tumour exclusivity or safety conclusion.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Healthy tissues can carry either recognized target
evidence.explanation: The current bispecific owner explicitly carries recognized targets on healthy tissue, with no safety conclusion from specificity alone. The selected NCI paragraphs name CD20 on B cells and some cancer cells in its rituximab example. This supports possible shared recognition, not a statement that every cancer antigen is equally accessible on all healthy cells. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Linking chemical cargo to recognition does not by itself establish entry, processing or usable payload at its action site.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Binding can support delivery, but uptake, processing, access to the payload’s target and cellular response require separate evidence.
evidence.explanation: Binding, uptake, processing, action-site access and response remain separate. FDA ADC printed pages 1 to 3 describe distinct constituent parts, release mechanisms and exposure considerations. The separate-test reading rule does not assume that every conjugate follows one guaranteed route. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Internalisation is not a universal requirement shared by all of the illustrated formats.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A change of format is a new product hypothesis. If an ADC binds M but yields little active material after uptake, an M-directed engager might avoid that particular processing requirement.
evidence.explanation: The current format-switching example explains how an engager can avoid a particular conjugate-processing requirement. This is a format-scope inference, not a claim that every construct works without uptake. Mack describes one soluble CD3/17-1A single-chain construct redirecting human lymphocytes in cell experiments. Contrasting that mechanism with FDA cytotoxic-conjugate processing gives a format-scope inference; no universal uptake or benefit claim is made. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: The illustrated soluble T-cell engager has distinct target-recognition and CD3-recognition arms binding different features on separate cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: CD20/CD3 lymphoma engagers illustrate one bispecific format: CD20 recognition connects to T-cell recruitment through CD3.
evidence.explanation: The named CD20/CD3 example and two linked scFv architecture jointly carry the illustrated distinct binding functions. Mack is one experimental construct, not a universal topology for every engager. Mack describes two scFv fragments joined by a peptide linker, one directed at CD3 and the other at epithelial 17-1A. The NCI paragraph gives a separate named CD19/CD3 example. These are illustrative architectures, not all engager forms. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The Mack construct joined two single-chain Fv fragments with a peptide linker in one compact protein; this is different from an IgG architecture with an Fc region.
evidence.explanation: The named CD20/CD3 example and two linked scFv architecture jointly carry the illustrated distinct binding functions. Mack is one experimental construct, not a universal topology for every engager. Mack describes two scFv fragments joined by a peptide linker, one directed at CD3 and the other at epithelial 17-1A. The NCI paragraph gives a separate named CD19/CD3 example. These are illustrative architectures, not all engager forms. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Bridging contact alone is not evidence of productive activation or target killing.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: T-cell engagers are proteins that bind a specified target and recruit T cells, often through CD3. A binding bridge does not by itself establish completed killing.
evidence.explanation: The registered engager TLDR explicitly withholds completed killing from a binding bridge. Mack measured cytotoxicity separately from binding. Bluemel reports different lysis despite similar target affinity in engineered CHO systems. The no-guarantee reading rule is an inference about evidence, not a new failure frequency. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: The cell-receptor example spans the T-cell membrane and links extracellular recognition to an intracellular signalling design.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A common CAR presents a binder outside the cell and signaling domains inside it, connected through a spacer and transmembrane region.
evidence.explanation: The registered CAR principle carries external recognition, transmembrane linkage and internal signalling. Eshhar used anti-trinitrophenyl scFv linked to gamma or zeta signalling chains in a cytolytic T-cell hybridoma. The selected FDA CAR guidance concerns ex vivo manufactured products and separates recognition from signalling. Neither supplies a general clinical outcome. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: A living-cell receptor and a soluble bridging protein are different formats; a floating antibody is not itself a cell receptor.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A dosed T-cell engager supplies a protein connecting target recognition to an available T cell. It does not itself install receptor instructions or supply engineered living responders.
evidence.explanation: The protein engager and receptor-bearing living cell are explicitly different administered/design objects. Mack concerns an expressed soluble bispecific protein; Eshhar concerns functional surface receptors in a cellular model. The FDA guidance discusses a living, genetically modified cell product. These object distinctions do not establish comparative efficacy. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The receptor is a protein; its encoding instructions and the living cell carrying it are different objects.
evidence.explanation: The protein engager and receptor-bearing living cell are explicitly different administered/design objects. Mack concerns an expressed soluble bispecific protein; Eshhar concerns functional surface receptors in a cellular model. The FDA guidance discusses a living, genetically modified cell product. These object distinctions do not establish comparative efficacy. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Function of the assembled product needs testing; receptor anatomy or a signalling symbol is not a measured successful response.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Binding, surface CAR expression, activation, proliferation and completed target-cell killing are distinct readouts.
evidence.explanation: Readouts and the schematic response arrow are explicitly separated from demonstrated expression or completed killing. The FDA CAR construct section calls for supporting recognition and signalling functions and evaluating hinge/linker/transmembrane contributions. Eshhar measured IL2 secretion and lysis in a defined model. A drawn signalling ray is not one of these measurements. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In this schematic sequence, simplified shapes and an arrow from recognition toward a response do not show that every cell expressed the receptor or completed killing.
evidence.explanation: Readouts and the schematic response arrow are explicitly separated from demonstrated expression or completed killing. The FDA CAR construct section calls for supporting recognition and signalling functions and evaluating hinge/linker/transmembrane contributions. Eshhar measured IL2 secretion and lysis in a defined model. A drawn signalling ray is not one of these measurements. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Delivery, function, safety and patient benefit are distinct questions, without a binding-to-benefit progression.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Two specificities do not establish that both targets are reached together, that binding produces killing, or that a molecule improves on a comparison treatment. Function, exposure, manufacturing quality and harms need evidence for the actual product and indication. A class containing approved drugs does not make every bispecific design an approved therapy.
evidence.explanation: Delivery, function, harms and comparative treatment evidence belong to the finished product; the binding result does not supply these unmeasured results. FDA ADC selected pages keep constituent exposure and safety/efficacy questions separate. The selected CAR pages distinguish product characterisation, nonclinical assessment and clinical studies. The separate-question rule supplies no patient-benefit estimate. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: An antibody-drug conjugate links a target-binding antibody to an active drug. Binding, delivery, release and drug action each matter, and normal tissues can also be exposed.
evidence.explanation: Delivery, function, harms and comparative treatment evidence belong to the finished product; the binding result does not supply these unmeasured results. FDA ADC selected pages keep constituent exposure and safety/efficacy questions separate. The selected CAR pages distinguish product characterisation, nonclinical assessment and clinical studies. The separate-question rule supplies no patient-benefit estimate. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: A shared recognition idea does not prove identical module performance after reformatting; the complete product needs tests.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A change of format is a new product hypothesis. If an ADC binds M but yields little active material after uptake, an M-directed engager might avoid that particular processing requirement. It still needs its own binding and contact-geometry measurements, useful effector access and function, normal-tissue testing and clinical evidence. Earlier antibody or ADC tolerability does not establish the safety of a different action. Bystander delivery and two-address designs are possible responses to heterogeneous expression, not guaranteed coverage or an exhaustive list of solutions.
evidence.explanation: A changed format is explicitly a new product hypothesis, with construct, geometry, expression and cell preparation retained. Bluemel compared epitope distance and antigen size in transfected CHO cells and engineered surface targets, with different lysis despite similar affinity. The FDA CAR section says structural-region contributions should be evaluated. No format-wide ranking or guaranteed sequence portability follows. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The full binder, spacer, anchor, signaling arrangement and cell preparation still matter.
evidence.explanation: A changed format is explicitly a new product hypothesis, with construct, geometry, expression and cell preparation retained. Bluemel compared epitope distance and antigen size in transfected CHO cells and engineered surface targets, with different lysis despite similar affinity. The FDA CAR section says structural-region contributions should be evaluated. No format-wide ranking or guaranteed sequence portability follows. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Multivalent apparent cell binding is not automatically single-site affinity; target density, spacing and assay preparation matter.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Avidity is the combined strength of several contacts and depends on target density, spacing and the number of binding sites. A cell-binding result for a multivalent product is therefore not its single-site affinity; ask which assay was used and how many sites took part.

points.requirement: An scFv links VH and VL variable domains by a peptide linker in one protein chain; one chain is not one variable domain.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Definitions. A conventional antibody pairs heavy- and light-chain variable domains to form a binding site. A single-chain variable fragment (scFv) joins those two domains with a peptide linker in one polypeptide chain, so single-chain does not mean one variable domain (Huston et al., 1988, a 15-amino-acid linker).
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. Huston reports linked VH/VL, one chain and a tested anti-digoxin construct. A linked chain can contain two domains; no universal success for every linker is claimed. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

points.requirement: The illustrated VHH is one variable domain without a VL partner; an isolated VHH differs from a complete heavy-chain antibody.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: VHH is the binding domain of a camelid heavy-chain-only antibody (Hamers-Casterman et al., 1993), and an isolated VHH used as a binder is called a nanobody (Bathula et al., 2021).
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. Hamers describes complete camel heavy-chain dimers, whereas Desmyter studies an isolated camel VH/lysozyme complex. The illustrated VHH is a domain, not the complete heavy-chain antibody; later single-domain variants are not re-certified here. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Camel serum was found to contain IgG-like molecules of about 100 kDa made of heavy-chain dimers without light chains or CH1 (Hamers-Casterman et al., 1993).
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. Hamers describes complete camel heavy-chain dimers, whereas Desmyter studies an isolated camel VH/lysozyme complex. The illustrated VHH is a domain, not the complete heavy-chain antibody; later single-domain variants are not re-certified here. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fab, the arm with the binding site, and Fc, the stem, are separate parts: binding does not guarantee killing, and Fc effector contacts need compatible effector cells or complement.
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. points.requirement: Linked domains must fold and recover actual binding in the tested construct; architecture alone does not show every linker or sequence works.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The original single-chain Fv work linked antibody heavy- and light-chain variable regions and tested binding after expression and refolding. Camelid heavy-chain antibody studies established a different architecture without light chains, underlying VHH-derived formats. More recent engineered-cell comparisons test the behavior of particular fragments in particular constructs. Format names describe architecture; they do not by themselves establish stability, specificity or therapeutic superiority.
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. Huston tested a particular engineered and renatured anti-digoxin sFv. Its recovery of specificity and changed association constant do not validate every sequence, linker or final format. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The first single-chain Fv joined the heavy- and light-chain variable domains of an anti-digoxin antibody with a 15-amino-acid linker (relative molecular mass 26,354); after refolding it showed digoxin specificity like the Fab and an association constant (3.2 x 10^7 per molar) about six-fold below the Fab's (Huston et al., 1988).
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. Huston tested a particular engineered and renatured anti-digoxin sFv. Its recovery of specificity and changed association constant do not validate every sequence, linker or final format. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

points.requirement: The size or appearance of a soluble recognition module does not determine transport of a cell carrying it.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: These are properties of the soluble protein. A cell carrying a small binder does not penetrate tissue like a small soluble protein.
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. This is an object/scope inference: the soluble protein and a living cell carrying a receptor are different objects. No new tissue-penetration claim for whole cells is imported. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

points.requirement: Neither fragment architecture nor the schematic size establishes whole-product safety, useful function or comparative clinical performance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Inference lesson. Two binders that both bind a purified protein have been shown equivalent in that one interaction only. Surface expression, target-dependent signalling, unwanted activation, tumour killing and healthy-tissue recognition each need separate evidence. Format names describe architecture, not stability, specificity or superiority.
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. Architecture and schematic size do not supply functional, safety or clinical-comparison measurements. Existing model-specific CAR examples retain their earlier recorded reading depth. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

points.requirement: Incoming lentiviral vector RNA is reverse-transcribed into a DNA copy before the depicted nuclear insertion in an integrating design.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Three design labels are easy to confuse. Replication-defective means the delivered particle lacks the machinery to propagate as an ordinary virus, which does not replace testing: FDA guidance sets out testing of retroviral vector products, lentiviral ones included, for replication-competent virus during manufacture and in patient follow-up. Self-inactivating means regulatory sequences in the long terminal repeats are disabled: in the original design a 133 base-pair deletion in the U3 region of the 3' repeat was copied to the 5' repeat after reverse transcription and integration, and the vector still expressed from an internal promoter in rat brain and eye (Miyoshi and colleagues). It does not mean the cassette cannot integrate. Integration-deficient means integrase is mutated: with a class 1 integrase mutation, residual integration was lower than with intact integrase by a factor of 500 to 1,250, expression was transient in dividing cell lines and long-lived in non-dividing neural cultures and in mouse brain, consistent with an episomal genome (Philippe and colleagues). The name does not promise zero integration or lasting expression in dividing cells such as T cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Where particles go depends on formulation and route. In female BALB/c mice given luciferase-mRNA LNPs by intramuscular, subcutaneous or intravenous injection, some intramuscular particles reached the liver and spleen, smaller particles more than larger ones, bigger particles tended to stay at the injection site, and liver expression was the most prominent; exposure and expression were not linearly related (Di and colleagues). Mouse distribution is not another product's distribution in people, and local injection does not establish local delivery. Readouts answer different questions: particle size, RNA integrity and encapsulated fraction describe the product; a labelled lipid or labelled RNA shows where a label went, not that intact RNA arrived or was released; and protein per identified live cell shows expression. In the mouse study a lipid label (DiR or deuterium-labelled cholesterol) and luciferase activity were measured separately and did not track each other linearly, and every figure needs its denominator (all cells, live cells or expressing cells). Uptake and protein are different fractions: in the six-formulation study the formulation with the highest eGFP expression had only moderate uptake, so a formulation that takes up in more cells can still make protein in fewer. Message and effect also run on separate clocks: in cultured mouse T cells CAR expression from LNP mRNA peaked at 24 hours and fell over the next days (Rurik and colleagues), and the same RNA in particles of different size or by a different route distributed differently, so the same RNA is not the same product.

Uptake and protein are different fractions: in the six-formulation study the formulation with the highest eGFP expression had only moderate uptake, so a formulation that takes up in more cells can still make protein in fewer. In sequential muscle biopsies taken 3 and 12 months after an intramuscular AAV vector expressing alpha-1 antitrypsin, most vector DNA was double-stranded circular episomes, and clones recovered from the biopsies were transcriptionally active (Schnepp and colleagues; abstract read, full text not retrievable). points.requirement: The original and later packaging sentences are distinct: named viral-genome sizes and Wu's tested packaging result do not establish one universal payload limit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Immunity and capacity also limit what a lot can do. In a phase 1/2 study in seven people with severe haemophilia B, an AAV2 factor IX vector infused through the hepatic artery reached therapeutic levels at the highest dose but expression lasted about 8 weeks; the authors' further studies suggested that cell-mediated immunity against capsid antigens destroyed transduced hepatocytes (Manno and colleagues). Neutralising antibodies against the capsid are why re-dosing is hard: a review notes that systemic AAV dosing needs patient stratification by antibody level and that re-administration then becomes very difficult (Naso and colleagues), and a 2024 mouse study, which opens by noting that AAV typically induces long-lasting neutralising antibodies that prevent re-administration, found that transient B-cell depletion (anti-CD20 with anti-BAFF) before hepatic AAV8 delivery allowed effective re-administration (Rana and colleagues). Whether a given product can be given again is a product-specific question, and that mouse experiment does not establish a clinical re-dosing protocol. For packaging, the AAV2 genome is a single-stranded DNA of 4,675 nucleotides (Srivastava and colleagues) and the original self-complementary-vector experiment used an inverted repeat that could pair with itself, bypassing synthesis of the second strand (McCarty and colleagues, 2001). McCarty's later review describes the trade-off as losing half the coding capacity. Report the capsid, cassette configuration and length being measured with a capacity figure; a measured packaged-genome length and usable coding capacity answer different questions. In the study of plasmid-encoded vectors of 4.7 to 8.7 kb in AAV2, AAV5 and AAV8 capsids, packaged genomes never exceeded 5.2 kb; genomes from plasmids over 5 kb were heterogeneous and truncated at the 5' end, and reporter expression in cells at high multiplicity of infection was substantially lower than from genomes under 5 kb (Wu and colleagues). FDA follow-up guidance says vectors such as AAV that do not tend to integrate or reactivate generally carry a lower risk of delayed adverse events, while product-specific modifications may change that, so safety is assessed per product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Where particles go depends on formulation and route. In the mouse study a lipid label (DiR or deuterium-labelled cholesterol) and luciferase activity were measured separately and did not track each other linearly, and every figure needs its denominator (all cells, live cells or expressing cells). Uptake and protein are different fractions: in the six-formulation study the formulation with the highest eGFP expression had only moderate uptake, so a formulation that takes up in more cells can still make protein in fewer. Message and effect also run on separate clocks: in cultured mouse T cells CAR expression from LNP mRNA peaked at 24 hours and fell over the next days (Rurik and colleagues), and the same RNA in particles of different size or by a different route distributed differently, so the same RNA is not the same product.

points.requirement: Start context crosses the untranslated/coding boundary; it is not an extra inserted segment or a DNA transcription promoter. Untranslated regions can affect use of the message.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Start-codon context was tested by single-base substitutions around the AUG initiator in a cloned preproinsulin gene, where the best sequence identified changed proinsulin yield over a 20-fold range (Kozak). The interaction of the cap and the poly(A) tail was tested with luciferase mRNAs delivered by electroporation into tobacco protoplasts, Chinese hamster ovary cells and yeast, where the tail's effect depended on the cap (Gallie). A textbook describes the 5' cap, 5' and 3' untranslated regions that regulate translation initiation and mRNA stability, a poly-A tail of about 200 A residues added by poly-A polymerase to cellular mRNA, and a ribosome that moves from the cap to the AUG, with Kozak's rules describing the sequence around it (OpenStax Biology 2e). The cellular tail length is not a rule for engineered constructs: one dendritic-cell study found that a 120-nucleotide tail, an unmasked tail end and two 3' untranslated regions each improved stability and translation, and it measured transcript amount by RT-PCR, protein by eGFP, peptide-MHC density and T-cell stimulation separately (Holtkamp and colleagues), so a doubled reporter signal after a 3' change is one measurement, not a different antigen or a clinical benefit. These are tested constructs and cell systems, not one best sequence for a clinical product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A computational study of spacer design for class-I-restricted string-of-beads polypeptides reported a fivefold increase in predicted epitope recovery and a 44 per cent reduction in predicted neo-epitope immunogenicity compared with designs without spacers (Schubert and Kohlbacher); these are predictions, not measured protection. Combining an N-terminal leader peptide with an MHC class I trafficking signal at the C terminus improved presentation of class I and class II epitopes in human and mouse dendritic cells and expanded antigen-specific CD8 and CD4 T cells in vitro and in mice (Kreiter and colleagues). In a first-in-human RNA poly-neo-epitope melanoma study all patients developed T-cell responses against multiple vaccine neo-epitopes (Sahin and colleagues; abstract only), and each patient's vaccine in the Rojas pancreatic cancer trial used two uridine mRNA strands, each encoding up to 10 neoepitopes. Mass spectrometry can identify recovered HLA-bound peptides. Caron and colleagues' 2015 review describes class I peptides predominantly 9 to 12 amino acids long and reports that about 10 per cent of acquired spectra could be confidently assigned at a 1 per cent false discovery rate in the workflows discussed. It also describes evidence that mass spectrometry underestimates the self-HLA peptide repertoire, so non-detection does not prove absence. Prediction is not presentation: of more than 1,300 amino acid changes in two mouse tumour models about 13 per cent were predicted to bind MHC class I and a small fraction of those were confirmed by mass spectrometry (Yadav and colleagues). Because a single amino acid after an epitope changed its immunogenicity in a multiepitope DNA vaccine (Livingston and colleagues, already linked), a changed spacer is a changed construct that needs renewed processing and display evidence, while earlier evidence is retained for the parts that did not change.

points.requirement: A pairing-antibody assay detects structures within its characterised length/chemistry/matrix scope; a lower or undetected signal proves neither zero impurity nor all product-quality attributes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: One documented origin is T7 polymerase initiating transcription from a promoter-less DNA end, producing an antisense strand and long double-stranded RNA that activated the sensor MDA5 (Mu and colleagues). In purification studies, unmodified mRNAs were translated better after HPLC purification but still induced high levels of cytokine secretion (Karikó and colleagues). A cellulose method removed at least 90 per cent of double-stranded RNA with over 65 per cent recovery regardless of mRNA length, coding sequence or nucleoside composition and increased translation in mice, and agarose gels showed that the purified mRNA stayed intact, but it removed duplexes of 30 base pairs or longer efficiently while most of a 21 base-pair duplex remained (Baiersdörfer and colleagues). Detection has its own scope: that paper notes an earlier report that about 40 base pairs of duplex are needed for detection by the J2 antibody, and a review of mRNA analytics lists immunoblot or ELISA for double-stranded RNA alongside separate integrity assays (Losada and colleagues). A lower dsRNA signal with worse fragmentation or recovery therefore does not show a better product. Method performance in those systems is not a clinical impurity limit.

points.requirement: LoB concerns the background-response distribution at a specified probability, not itself a reliably detected amount; repeated representative blanks and conditions matter.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The limit of blank describes an upper background response at a specified probability. A limit of detection concerns an amount that can be detected under stated false-call and detection-probability conditions; LoD95 specifies 95 per cent detection in the tested workflow. It is not a line above which every repeat must be positive, nor 95 per cent certainty that a person has disease. A limit of quantitation requires stated quantitative accuracy, including bias and imprecision goals. The limits answer different questions and have no universal spacing; they may coincide under a particular method and its criteria.
evidence.explanation: Exact current field containment plus coordinator semantic assessment at the stated source depth. No independent acceptance. armbruster:17,18,24, clsi-terminology:3998-4039 Actual unmerged PR371 field; absent from registered root and generated root exports.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Evaluate repeated blanks and low-level specimens across the conditions the claim covers. Each finite set of repeats needs representative clinical specimens or suitably equivalent reference inputs. Record the analyte, amount or concentration units, specimen matrix, input, workflow boundary, assay version and acceptable false-positive, false-negative and quantitative-error rates. Matrix means the material surrounding the analyte; reference material with a known added analyte amount needs justified equivalence to the clinical specimen. A limit measured on purified material is not automatically a collection-to-report limit. Contamination, nonspecific signal, calibration bias, poor recovery, unrepresentative targets, different lots or operators and inadequate input can change performance. Calibration-slope sensitivity, analytical detection capability and clinical sensitivity are different uses of the same word.

points.requirement: Prognosis is an outcome association in specified marker/assay, specimen, population, timing, background care, endpoint and horizon; it does not automatically describe untreated natural history.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A prognostic marker is associated with a defined outcome under specified care in a defined population and time horizon. It is not automatically a description of untreated natural history. A predictive biomarker concerns the effect of a named treatment relative to a comparator: compare those treatment effects across marker groups, with an explicit effect scale and uncertainty. A marker can serve both roles. Prespecified groups and randomized treatment assignment support this comparison, although the actual design, missing specimens and applicability still matter. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Read the effect estimate and confidence interval together. Too few events can leave a study with low power and an interval compatible with meaningful benefit and harm. points.requirement: Absolute/relative comparisons use the same defined event, population, comparator and horizon; incomplete follow-up requires appropriate time-specific estimates.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Absolute risk is the chance of a defined event by a stated time. For an undesirable event, absolute risk reduction is control risk minus treatment risk, the risk ratio is treatment risk divided by control risk, and relative risk reduction is one minus that ratio. When the absolute reduction is positive, number needed to treat is its reciprocal, using a fraction rather than a percentage. Risks are percentages, absolute differences are percentage points, ratios have no units, and number needed to treat refers to people over the specified horizon. The population, comparator, event direction and time must match. With incomplete follow-up, suitable time-specific estimates are needed; dividing recorded events by enrolment may answer a different question.
evidence.explanation: Named current fields carry the scientific interpretation at the stated source scope; exact containment establishes location and the coordinator has assessed entailment. This is not independent acceptance. The Cook returned abstract and named Altman 1998/Altman-Andersen 1999 paragraphs support reciprocal and time-horizon interpretation. Numerical grids, interval examples and baseline contrasts are invented arithmetic, not clinical outcomes. Retained CHALLENGE/KEYNOTE-564 and median assertions in the untouched summary are outside this fresh source assessment. Current registered local root; not main/live or independent acceptance.

This is an average contrast between strategies; it does not mean every seventeenth person benefits. Harms require their own outcomes and calculations.

points.requirement: Frequentist confidence level concerns repeated valid method coverage under assumptions; the normal construction is approximate, and an observed interval is not a posterior probability or a range containing 95 percent of patients.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A frequentist confidence interval describes estimation precision using a procedure with a stated coverage rate under its assumptions. Across repeated valid applications, a 95% procedure would include the fixed true parameter in 95% of its intervals. This does not assign a 95% probability to that parameter being inside one interval after it has been calculated, or describe a range containing 95% of patients. The result depends on the data structure, estimator, confidence level, model and calculation method, including adjustment, missing-data handling and multiplicity. More observations often improve precision but do not remove biased measurement, confounding or a wrong model.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: For a fictional binary outcome in 50 of 100 independent people, the normal-approximation standard error is sqrt(0.50 × 0.50/100) = 0.05. The approximate 95% interval is 0.50 ± 1.96 × 0.05, or 40.2% to 59.8%. With 5,000 of 10,000 people, the proportion stays 50% but the standard error becomes 0.005 and the interval 49.02% to 50.98%. Small counts, proportions near zero or one, clustering and incomplete outcomes may require other methods. A hand-picked set of ten such intervals, nine containing a fixed 50% truth and one missing it, illustrates coverage but does not measure a procedure's coverage rate. A 95% method need not cover in exactly 95% of a small set. Narrower bounds indicate greater sampling precision, not less bias.

points.requirement: A p-value conditions on the null and other analysis assumptions; it is not the probability the null is true, an individual finding is false, or a clinically important benefit exists.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A p-value is calculated for a specified null hypothesis and analysis. Assuming that null model and the other analysis assumptions are true, it is the probability of a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed. A small value indicates poor fit to that model; it is not the probability that the hypothesis is true, that the result occurred “by chance”, or that the selected finding is false. In particular, p = 0.03 does not mean a 97% probability of benefit. Omics analyses may test thousands of genes or pathways, and reporting only the most striking result hides the search. A selected small value can generate a hypothesis without establishing a drug dependency or clinical benefit. Error control cannot repair biased measurement or an irrelevant comparison, and prespecification reduces analytical flexibility without guaranteeing a sound design.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A Kaplan-Meier curve estimates the probability of remaining free of a defined event from a stated starting time while accounting for incomplete follow-up. At each event time, the previous estimate is multiplied by the fraction of people still at risk just before that time who avoid the event. A censor tick is neither an event nor proof of permanent event freedom. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A five-year curve height is an estimate from its stated origin. A landmark analysis instead selects people meeting a condition at a later time, such as being observed and event-free at month 6, then evaluates subsequent outcomes. It changes the population and clock and handles early events differently from the original trial comparison. Classifying people by a later response can also bias survival comparisons if timing is mishandled. At-risk counts are changing denominators, not new enrolment; a flat late tail may rest on very few people and does not establish cure. Median survival is when the curve reaches 50%; “not reached” means it did not reach that level during observed follow-up. Median follow-up describes observation time. Neither statement implies there were no events. Curve height is not a hazard ratio, and curve separation needs a suitable study design for a causal interpretation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Treating deaths that occur before the recurrence of interest as censoring and calculating one minus Kaplan-Meier targets a different quantity from cumulative incidence and can overstate that real-world recurrence probability. Cumulative incidence addresses that competing-risk question. The nonparametric Aalen-Johansen estimator estimates state probabilities, including cumulative incidence as a competing-risk special case, under the relevant event, observation and censoring assumptions. Fine-Gray regression is a separate model for covariate effects on the subdistribution hazard. Austin and colleagues' 2016 tutorial supports the bias and hazard distinctions; Therneau, Crowson and Atkinson's September 2026 technical vignette separately supplies the Aalen-Johansen method name and its relationship to cumulative incidence. Neither estimator removes the need for an appropriate event definition and follow-up.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Among 1,000 fictional participants, suppose 50 first recurrences are recorded and 20 are assigned to site X, with some follow-up incomplete. The calculation 20/50 = 40% describes the share of recorded first recurrences assigned to X. The calculation 20/1,000 = 2% describes a crude fraction of enrolled participants with that recorded event. Neither supplies five-year risk. Death before recurrence prevents recurrence, and another first site prevents X from being the first site; later recurrence at X is a different endpoint. A cumulative-incidence analysis can account for follow-up and competing events under its assumptions. The nonparametric Aalen-Johansen estimator supplies that estimate, while Fine-Gray regression models covariate effects on the subdistribution hazard. The method-name attribution comes from Therneau, Crowson and Atkinson's technical vignette, separately from Austin's competing-risk discussion. Turning the 40% site share into everyone's five-year risk changes both denominator and horizon without a supporting analysis.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A surrogate is a measured outcome used in place of a direct clinical-benefit outcome, with evidence needed for that substitution in the intended setting. Two relationships must be separated: people with a favourable marker may have better outcomes, while treatments that improve that marker may or may not improve the outcome. The first is a prognostic association; the second concerns agreement between treatment effects across suitable randomised comparisons. A treatment can change another pathway, later disease or toxicity as well as the marker. Validation is specific to disease, treatment context and intended outcome. An early measure is not automatically validated, and regulatory acceptance in one programme does not transfer to another. “Validated” and “reasonably likely to predict benefit” carry different evidence claims. Yet trial-level R-squared was 0.03 for event-free survival (95% interval 0.00 to 0.25) and 0.24 for overall survival (0.00 to 0.70). Conforti and colleagues' analysis of 54 trials and 32,611 participants found R-squared 0.14 (95% interval 0.00 to 0.29) for disease-free and 0.08 (0.00 to 0.22) for overall survival. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional six-week symptom example: each treatment group contains 100 people. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. Slower growth, death and a molecular change require their own readouts; direct death or recovery measurements could address further questions. A real experimental response does not by itself establish the responsible target or clinical benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional forest example: five studies compare treatment A minus control on the same 0 to 100 symptom scale at day 30. Their effects are -8, -6, -4, -2 and 0 points, each with standard error 2 and weight 20 per cent, so the square areas are equal. The mean is -4.0 points. With a classical moment variance estimate, Q = 10, I-squared = 60 per cent and tau-squared = 6 squared score points. A normal 95 per cent mean interval is about -6.8 to -1.2; the stated 2009 prediction method, using a t distribution with three degrees of freedom, gives about -13.0 to +5.0. The study intervals, mean diamond and wider prediction interval answer different questions. Five studies are few and these intervals are approximate; a negative mean does not imply a negative effect in every setting.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A confidence interval for the mean effect differs from a prediction interval for an underlying effect in another comparable study under the model. Neither is a personal prognosis interval. I-squared estimates the proportion of variability in study estimates associated with heterogeneity rather than sampling error; it is neither the percentage of people helped nor the percentage of studies that are wrong. Tau-squared is between-study effect variance on the chosen scale, such as squared score points or squared log risk ratios. These estimates can be uncertain, especially with few studies, and no I-squared cutoff alone makes pooling safe.

points.requirement: Vehicle and untreated controls ask different questions when the carrier or solvent can affect the assay.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

points.requirement: I-squared describes estimated heterogeneity relative to sampling variation, not people helped or studies wrong. Tau-squared is a between-study variance on the named effect scale; both estimates can be uncertain with few studies.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A confidence interval for the mean effect differs from a prediction interval for an underlying effect in another comparable study under the model. Neither is a personal prognosis interval. I-squared estimates the proportion of variability in study estimates associated with heterogeneity rather than sampling error; it is neither the percentage of people helped nor the percentage of studies that are wrong. Tau-squared is between-study effect variance on the chosen scale, such as squared score points or squared log risk ratios. These estimates can be uncertain, especially with few studies, and no I-squared cutoff alone makes pooling safe.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional forest example: five studies compare treatment A minus control on the same 0 to 100 symptom scale at day 30. Their effects are -8, -6, -4, -2 and 0 points, each with standard error 2 and weight 20 per cent, so the square areas are equal. The mean is -4.0 points. With a classical moment variance estimate, Q = 10, I-squared = 60 per cent and tau-squared = 6 squared score points. A normal 95 per cent mean interval is about -6.8 to -1.2; the stated 2009 prediction method, using a t distribution with three degrees of freedom, gives about -13.0 to +5.0. Five studies are few and these intervals are approximate; a negative mean does not imply a negative effect in every setting.

points.requirement: Phases 1 to 4 describe development purposes, with overlap and actual protocol context. They are not a benefit ladder, fixed sample-size rule, guarantee of safety, efficacy or approval for every investigated use.

Phase 4 studies an approved treatment in broader use. Read the protocol because phases can overlap or be combined.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Specify the question, treatments, period lengths, assigned order, background care, units, observation times and analysis before interpreting results. Random order does not erase these problems. Choose timing and analysis for the actual design and missing observations; there is no universal washout duration.

points.requirement: Explain IFNg-receptor/JAK1/JAK2/STAT response and distinguish inducibility from baseline display.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Explain IFNg-receptor/JAK1/JAK2/STAT response and distinguish inducibility from baseline display.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: In Zaretsky’s selected four-person melanoma relapse series, two cases had JAK1 or JAK2 loss-of-function changes with loss of the normal allele and another had a truncating B2M change. The JAK2-deficient relapse cells failed to increase interferon-gamma signalling, PD-L1 and class I while retaining interferon-alfa/beta responsiveness. Engineered JAK1- or JAK2-deficient melanoma cells were still recognized by the tested NY-ESO-1-specific T cells. Baseline display, inducibility, recognition and killing are separate dependencies; neither a JAK variant nor detectable HLA alone answers all of them.

points.requirement: Carry the full labelled/unlabelled-binder visual: isotope, delivery, access, competition, clearance, retention, mass, activity and image time; the conceptual diagram supplies no uptake values.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Imagine sending a labelled binding tool into the body. Some remains in blood, some reaches accessible sites, and some fails to bind or clears. Delivery, access, target binding, competition, clearance and retention all affect the image. Therapeutic or unlabelled antibody can compete for the same target or alter distribution and background. A smaller signal after same-target treatment is therefore not, by itself, target loss. A conceptual labelled/unlabelled-binder drawing supplies these alternatives, not uptake values.

A prepared stained tissue section supplies a different, sampled observation.

points.requirement: A shared beta chain can hide different alpha chains (figure, common confusions)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: A shared beta chain can hide different alpha chains (figure, common confusions) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Beta match, alpha hidden, fictional: three cells carry beta chains B, B and C, so a bulk beta-chain view lists B, B, C and loses the alpha chains. The paired view keeps alpha X with beta B, alpha Y with beta B and alpha Z with beta C, so the shared beta B does not make alpha X and alpha Y equal. Single-cell methods that sequence the alpha and beta genes of individual T cells retain each pair and can be combined with function-related gene expression, and the same TCR sequence can sit in functionally different cells (Han 2014). A bulk method profiles a mixed sample, often one chain, whereas TIRTL-seq generates paired alpha and beta repertoire data at cohort scale and is distinguished from bulk single-chain data and from single-cell throughput limits (Pogorelyy 2026). Paired identity plus an expression program is more context and is still not evidence of the receptor's antigen.

points.requirement: Density separation, interface, incomplete recovery and contamination; PBMC label is not purity (figure)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Density separation, interface, incomplete recovery and contamination; PBMC label is not purity (figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: What the fraction is: peripheral blood mononuclear cells are circulating white blood cells with a single unsegmented nucleus, mainly lymphocytes and monocytes, with T, B and natural killer cells among them, isolated by layering anticoagulated blood over a density-separation medium and collecting the interface. Most conventional granulocytes and red cells separate elsewhere, but recovery is incomplete, so platelets, red cells or low-density granulocytes can contaminate a preparation, and the label PBMC does not guarantee purity. The classic density-gradient method dates from 1968 (Boyum 1968). Isolation selects a recoverable blood fraction and does not sample tumour or give a complete immune census.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Density separation, interface, incomplete recovery and contamination; PBMC label is not purity (figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The usable input for a downstream assay is the recovered viable cell preparation, not simply the volume of blood drawn. Fresh isolation, freezing, thawing, washing and any rest period define a sequence of selections, so record recovery, population composition and purity as well as viability. The Cytiva density-separation handbook describes the mononuclear interface, platelet carryover and possible immature-granulocyte contamination in pathological blood. That manufacturer method source does not validate every cancer assay, and an inadequate number of the relevant cells can make a rare-response experiment uninformative.

points.requirement: Multivalent avidity on a labelled scaffold (figure); tetramer as one format

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Multivalent avidity on a labelled scaffold (figure); tetramer as one format Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: What the evidence shows: in the original report, tetramers of HLA-A2 with two HIV-derived peptides or an influenza A matrix peptide bound peptide-specific cytotoxic T cells in vitro and T cells from the blood of HIV-infected people, and binding in general correlated well with cytotoxicity assays (Altman 1996). That is a correlation in those systems and not a rule that binding equals killing for an arbitrary tumour peptide. Tetramers are made by mixing biotinylated MHC with fluorescent streptavidin, and a later method made them with small-molecule fluorophores (Ramachandiran 2007), so reagent preparation is a source of variation. An observed stain shows binding under the tested conditions and does not show natural processing and display of that pair by a tumour.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Multivalent avidity on a labelled scaffold (figure); tetramer as one format Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Avidity describes the combined strength of multiple contacts. Multimerising peptide-HLA ligands can make binding detectable when an individual receptor-ligand contact is weak; the 2021 guidelines also caution that more multimerisation does not always improve detection. The measured output is a gate-defined binding fraction or, with a suitable counting method, a count. Reagent, viability and background controls support that binding measurement, which still requires separate validation before use for treatment selection.

points.requirement: Stimulus types, transport inhibition window, fixation and permeabilisation, viability stain before fixation (Mermaid, figure)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Stimulus types, transport inhibition window, fixation and permeabilisation, viability stain before fixation (Mermaid, figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: cytokines retained inside cells during a defined assay, so a response can be assigned to stained cell populations. How: cells get a defined stimulus, a protein-transport inhibitor is present for a stated window so newly made cytokines accumulate, the cells are fixed and made permeable, and flow cytometry reads cytokine stains beside population markers, with a viability stain applied before fixation. Input: viable blood or tissue cells, with separate aliquots per stimulus, and fixed cells cannot go on to living-cell assays. Output: percent cytokine-positive cells within a named parent population, or percent with stated cytokine combinations. Controls: unstimulated or vehicle, a positive stimulation, viability and recovery, single-stain and staining-boundary controls. It cannot tell natural tumour presentation, direct target-cell killing, receptor sequence identity or clinical benefit.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Stimulus types, transport inhibition window, fixation and permeabilisation, viability stain before fixation (Mermaid, figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The stimulus changes the question. Added peptide can bypass some processing steps; whole protein needs suitable antigen-presenting cells and processing, while broad stimulation tests responsiveness without identifying the intended antigen. The 2021 flow-cytometry guidelines describe brefeldin A and monensin as transport inhibitors and explain that their choice and exposure window can affect what is measured. Intracellular accumulation after inhibition is not a measurement of how much cytokine reached the surrounding medium.

points.requirement: Relative enrichment versus absolute expansion: 30 of 100 to 30 of 50 (figure); richness is not evenness; a shared sequence is not proven cancer specificity; one number is not the whole repertoire

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Relative enrichment versus absolute expansion: 30 of 100 to 30 of 50 (figure); richness is not evenness; a shared sequence is not proven cancer specificity; one number is not the whole repertoire Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Share against count, fictional: clonotype A is 30 of 100 measured molecules, 30%, and later 30 of 50, 60%. Its measured count did not rise, the total fell, and its relative frequency doubled, so relative enrichment is not absolute expansion and the molecule counts are not blood cell counts. In a published analysis pipeline, clonality was identified as a robust key metric and first choice for measuring TCR repertoire diversity, and in prostate cancer patients given sipuleucel-T the pipeline detected changes in sequence frequency and diversity in blood and prostate tissue (Zhang 2017); that is a methods and example study and sets no response threshold. A diversity-analysis software suite reports repertoire comparison and diversity outputs (Shugay 2015), and formulas, software settings and subsampling depth have to be stated.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Frequency arithmetic, fictional: clonotype A is 10 of 10,000 sampled receptor units at baseline (0.1%) and 20 of 1,000 later (2%). The measured relative frequency rose twentyfold, but these are sampled receptor units and not a census of cells, and other populations contracting, different sampling and method effects can change frequency. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A count is a recovery under rules: enrichment concentrates candidate cells before identification, and each method selects. One established epithelial method captures with EpCAM, then checks cell shape, a nucleus, cytokeratin and absence of CD45, which is one operational definition and not a universal rule for all circulating tumour cells or tumour types. Physical methods select by size or deformability and remove or retain different cells, so marker independence is not unbiased recovery. A negative capture, such as zero qualifying cells in 7.5 mL, does not show that no tumour cells circulate and does not predict a ctDNA result, because free DNA fragments are a separate analyte.

Protein staining, RNA or DNA analysis, and culture are separate downstream measurements with their own material requirements; a count does not automatically supply a genome, a viable culture, the lesion that shed the cell or evidence that changing treatment helps.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Attribution rule: matched white-blood-cell sequencing is the standard comparison, but its gene coverage, depth and detection rules matter, a clone below its sensitivity can stay unseen, and subtracting every blood match is not a complete method because a variant can be present in blood and tumour. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Design contract, from the FDA guidance of November 2024: a tumour-informed approach sequences the tumour and selects variants to follow. Its stated advantage is potentially higher specificity, and its limits include lag between tumour testing and panel creation, possible failure to detect mutations that emerge after tumour sampling or revert, and dependence on the number and reliability of selected targets, which may be better for tumours with higher mutation burden and well-characterised hotspot variants. A tumour-naive or tumour-agnostic panel is generic, with faster turnaround as its stated advantage and tumour biomarkers outside the panel as a limit. Both still meet the same finite plasma tube, background attribution and calling rules.

points.requirement: Top panel ten numbered tumours with A/AB/B/none badges; lower panel HSA 30%, Bliss 44%, observed 40% at one dose pair (A 20%, B 30%), 72 h, vehicle-normalised viable-cell endpoint, no uncertainty/test; Loewe needs dose-response curves.

evidence.explanation: The responder union is 6 of 10; the separate 72-hour viable-count example exceeds HSA but not Bliss and supplies no uncertainty or Loewe curves.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The two fictional comparisons use different units of inference. In a ten-tumour better-component model, A covers tumours 1 to 4 and B covers 3 to 6: 4 + 4 - 2 = 6 in the union, with four in neither group. There is no extra within-tumour interaction or added toxicity in that counting model. Separately, one cultured-cell experiment at 72 hours gives 20%, 30% and 40% inhibition for A, B and the pair at one fixed dose pair. Inhibition here is a reduction in vehicle-normalised viable-cell count, not a direct death measurement. HSA expects 30% and Bliss 44%, so 40% exceeds the first and falls below the second. Loewe needs single-drug dose-response curves; three numbers and no uncertainty estimate cannot establish a general synergy claim. In this model, greater overlap among responders reduces the union. Independent drug action does not require the two response groups to be statistically independent; shared resistance and response correlation matter to a population prediction.

points.requirement: Four panels: purified binding, engagement in relevant cell, effect measurement, benefit and harm evidence; reaching the compartment alone is insufficient; molecular shapes schematic.

evidence.explanation: Purified binding, relevant-system engagement, functional effects and clinical outcomes form separate evidence layers.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Target engagement and the evidence ladder. Target engagement asks whether a compound interacts with its intended target in the relevant system. Binding to a purified protein does not show that the compound enters the cell or reaches its target in a tumour, and engagement is also not a change in the target's function, a downstream effect or clinical benefit. Each question needs its own measurement: engagement first, then a measured biological effect, then a check of the causal explanation with controls, then clinical evidence.

evidence.explanation: Purified binding, relevant-system engagement, functional effects and clinical outcomes form separate evidence layers.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading a thermal-shift result. The cellular thermal shift assay was introduced to evaluate drug binding to target proteins in cells and tissue samples through ligand-induced thermal stabilisation (Martinez Molina et al. 2013). The readout is the soluble target signal remaining after heating, plotted either against temperature at a fixed compound concentration or against concentration at a fixed temperature, so degrees Celsius and concentration units sit on different axes and the two designs ask different bounded questions. A shift of the compound curve against a matched control supports engagement under those conditions; indirect stability or protein-complex effects can also change the signal, so it is not an inhibition or occupancy percentage, and no universal shift cut-off is given here. The heated aliquots are consumed, so a record should carry the compound, concentration, exposure time, temperature series, cell or tissue system and controls. In an isothermal-shift study with a pan-kinase inhibitor, a large share of non-kinase proteins shifted in cells, which the authors read as in-cell profiling being more likely than lysate profiling to identify indirect binding targets; they recommend lysate profiling to identify targets and in-cell profiling to verify intracellular engagement (Ball et al. 2020).

evidence.explanation: Purified binding, relevant-system engagement, functional effects and clinical outcomes form separate evidence layers.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The last step is clinical. Mechanistic plausibility does not show benefit, because the target may also be present in healthy tissue and the useful margin depends on achieved benefit and harm in a stated disease, treatment setting, product and outcome. The National Cancer Institute adds that cancer cells can become resistant to targeted therapy when the target itself changes so the drug can no longer interact with it, or when cells find new ways to grow that do not depend on the target.

The cellular thermal shift assay was introduced to evaluate drug binding to target proteins in cells and tissue samples through ligand-induced thermal stabilisation (Martinez Molina et al. 2013). The readout is the soluble target signal remaining after heating, plotted either against temperature at a fixed compound concentration or against concentration at a fixed temperature, so degrees Celsius and concentration units sit on different axes and the two designs ask different bounded questions. A shift of the compound curve against a matched control supports engagement under those conditions; indirect stability or protein-complex effects can also change the signal, so it is not an inhibition or occupancy percentage, and no universal shift cut-off is given here. The heated aliquots are consumed, so a record should carry the compound, concentration, exposure time, temperature series, cell or tissue system and controls. In an isothermal-shift study with a pan-kinase inhibitor, a large share of non-kinase proteins shifted in cells, which the authors read as in-cell profiling being more likely than lysate profiling to identify indirect binding targets; they recommend lysate profiling to identify targets and in-cell profiling to verify intracellular engagement (Ball et al. 2020).

evidence.explanation: Purified binding, relevant-system engagement, functional effects and clinical outcomes form separate evidence layers.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The last step is clinical. Mechanistic plausibility does not show benefit, because the target may also be present in healthy tissue and the useful margin depends on achieved benefit and harm in a stated disease, treatment setting, product and outcome. The National Cancer Institute adds that cancer cells can become resistant to targeted therapy when the target itself changes so the drug can no longer interact with it, or when cells find new ways to grow that do not depend on the target.

points.requirement: Read both complete antigen-acquisition/support-input figures: distinct jobs, an example sensor, possible action on different cells and a later priming encounter whose response needs testing.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A vaccine adjuvant is an ingredient intended to support an immune response to vaccine antigen. In a topic-and-teaching-context analogy, antigen supplies a possible target while the adjuvant changes the context; it does not choose a mature T cell's receptor specificity. Ingredients can affect recruitment, antigen availability, activation and supporting signals through different pathways. An antigen-acquisition diagram with one example sensor and a later priming encounter is simplified: antigen and context have distinct jobs, adjuvants can act on other cells, and a useful response still needs testing.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Checkpoint antibodies interrupt specified inhibitory contacts. PD-1 is a receptor with two partners, PD-L1 and PD-L2; PD-L1 is a distinct molecule found on cancer and non-cancer cells. The pembrolizumab label describes blockade of PD-1 binding to both ligands. Atezolizumab instead binds PD-L1 and blocks its PD-1 and B7.1 interactions; directly blocking PD-L1 does not directly block the separate PD-1/PD-L2 contact. These target-specific descriptions are more precise than treating all checkpoint drugs as one switch.

points.requirement: Read both complete receiver/exposure figures: the same cytokine can meet different receptors and states, and a local origin can yield distant exposure if signal reaches circulation and persists.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Circulating protein, local formulations and engineered cytokine-producing cells are different exposure strategies. A local origin does not guarantee local confinement: the signal can reach the circulation and persist elsewhere. In Zhang's 2015 dose-escalation study, 33 people with metastatic melanoma received transferred tumour-infiltrating cells engineered with inducible IL-12. Higher cell doses were associated with high serum IL-12 and interferon gamma and serious liver, fever and circulatory toxicities. The finding concerns that construct and regimen; it does not establish the safety or harm of every armoured cell product.
evidence.explanation: The receiver/state and local-origin/distant-exposure panels are represented together; secretion location is not evidence of confinement. Source scope: Source-backed teaching and explicitly limited reading inference Point C-005: The receiver/state and local-origin/distant-exposure panels are represented together; secretion location is not evidence of confinement.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A cytokine is a signalling protein, and cytokine treatment supplies the protein or causes cells to produce it. The response depends on the molecule, the receiving receptor system, the cell's previous state and its exposure. A neighbourhood-message analogy is useful only to this extent: receiving a signal does not give a cell the correct cancer target or a literal instruction to fight it. IL-2 can influence lymphocyte growth and activity; interferons have different receptors and effects, so one cytokine name cannot stand for every immune signal.
evidence.explanation: The receiver/state and local-origin/distant-exposure panels are represented together; secretion location is not evidence of confinement. Source scope: Background receptor/state explanation consistent with distinct cytokine functions and the selective IL-2-complex experiment Point C-005: The receiver/state and local-origin/distant-exposure panels are represented together; secretion location is not evidence of confinement.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: IL-2 can support regulatory T cells as well as other responding lymphocytes. Boyman and colleagues showed in mice that different IL-2-antibody complexes preferentially expanded different T-cell populations, including CD8 cells or CD4 regulatory T cells. The formulation changed the biological effect. Receptor composition, sensitivity and cell state therefore matter when studying a cytokine design; these mouse experiments do not establish human cancer benefit from every complex or from a larger dose.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Keep three measurements separate. Changes in size or tissue at the injected lesion show local observations. Report each component's route and serial injected and uninjected lesion results. An uninjected lesion can still receive systemic co-treatment, so it need not be untreated.

points.requirement: Interpret the selected-role diagram without treating it as an exhaustive job map: CDK4/6 and CDK2 around G1/DNA copying, CDK7 at initiation and activation of other CDKs, and CDK9 at elongation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: CDK4 and CDK6 help phosphorylate retinoblastoma protein, or RB, near the G1-to-S transition toward DNA copying. Their usual arrest mechanism depends on a functional RB restraint on cell-cycle transcription; detecting RB protein alone does not establish an intact circuit, and loss of RB1 can remove that route. CDK2 works with cyclins E and A in progression around DNA replication. These are selected overlapping roles, not exclusive assignments for every cell state. Cyclin E abundance by itself does not select a particular CDK2 inhibitor.
evidence.explanation: The text carries the selected CDK4/6, CDK2, CDK7 and CDK9 roles and explicitly rejects exclusive boxes. UniProt-CDK2: reviewed protein annotation, complete function comment; CDK2 subunit comment also read, underlying linked papers not independently read; NCI-palbociclib: official technical dictionary, complete raw definition, not linked trial or drug-summary pages

evidence.supportingExcerpt: CDK7 contributes to transcription initiation and also activates other CDKs. Larochelle and colleagues showed connected CDK7 and CDK9 functions in human cells: CDK7 helped establish and release promoter-proximal pausing, including activation of CDK9, while CDK9 supported productive RNA elongation. These jobs cannot be sealed into separate boxes. If a test reports a fall in a short-lived transcript after a transcription-directed intervention, that is an RNA-output observation to verify, not proof of the cell-cycle arrest associated with CDK4/6 inhibition. The exact transcript and its response need to be measured.
evidence.explanation: The text carries the selected CDK4/6, CDK2, CDK7 and CDK9 roles and explicitly rejects exclusive boxes. 23064645: primary research publication, complete abstract and targeted body paragraphs; NCI-samuraciclib: official technical dictionary, complete raw definition, not linked trial or drug-summary pages; NCI-cdk9: official technical dictionary, complete raw definition, not linked trial or drug-summary pages

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Trilaciclib uses a different purpose and schedule: short exposure before chemotherapy can transiently arrest susceptible blood-forming stem and progenitor cells to reduce myelosuppression. TRACES studied Chinese patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer, including an open safety part and a randomised placebo-controlled part. Duration of severe neutropenia in cycle one was the primary myeloprotection endpoint in the randomised part. Blood counts and days of severe neutropenia measure marrow effects. They are not tumour shrinkage, and this endpoint does not establish a survival benefit in another cancer.
evidence.explanation: RB presence, a working arrest pathway, reversible arrest, death, marrow protection and tumour control are contrasted across the connected paragraphs. 38224653: primary research publication, complete abstract only; NCI-trilaciclib: official technical dictionary, complete raw definition, not linked trial or drug-summary pages

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional culture that stops dividing during drug exposure and regrows after washout, the observed pattern supports reversible arrest. It does not establish selective killing or durable tumour control. Test attribution to the intended kinase, measure death and longer-term regrowth, and compare relevant control cells. A pause used to protect marrow and an intervention intended to control a tumour can involve related machinery while pursuing different outcomes.
evidence.explanation: RB presence, a working arrest pathway, reversible arrest, death, marrow protection and tumour control are contrasted across the connected paragraphs. 22430491: primary research publication, complete abstract and targeted body paragraphs; NCI-trilaciclib: official technical dictionary, complete raw definition, not linked trial or drug-summary pages

points.requirement: Interpret all three figure contacts: extracellular antibody, intracellular kinase inhibitor and payload delivery, with receptor arrangement/cargo processing schematic.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: EGFR, also called HER1 or ERBB1, is a receptor tyrosine kinase. Ligand binding outside the cell can change receptor arrangement and the activity of phosphate-transfer machinery inside. Cetuximab binds the extracellular region, whereas an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor acts at the intracellular kinase. An antibody conjugate instead adds a cargo-delivery job to target recognition. Its mechanism and evidence need separate assessment, including any antibody-mediated immune effects. A schematic contact or cargo arrow is not a molecular map of receptor processing, and delivery to a recognised target does not by itself establish dependence on the receptor kinase.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K, AKT and mTOR name different parts of a signalling network. AKT, also called protein kinase B, phosphorylates proteins, and its connection to mTORC1 includes intermediate regulators. mTOR participates in the distinct mTORC1 and mTORC2 complexes. A diagram showing this route leaves other branches out.
