evidence.explanation: Multicellular inflammatory signalling is interpreted through clinical attribution, competing causes, treated denominator and product-specific observation, not a cytokine curve.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cytokine release syndrome can follow activation by engineered immune cells or T-cell-engaging treatments. Signals from several cell types can contribute to fever, hypotension, hypoxia and other organ effects. Infection or other conditions can produce similar findings or coexist with the syndrome.

evidence.explanation: Multicellular inflammatory signalling is interpreted through clinical attribution, competing causes, treated denominator and product-specific observation, not a cytokine curve.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading CRS without over-reading a cytokine level. CRS is a clinical syndrome, graded from attributed findings and not from a cytokine concentration. In a mouse model of CD19 CAR T-cell CRS, severity was mediated not by CAR T-cell-derived cytokines but by IL-6, IL-1 and nitric oxide from the recipient's macrophages, and IL-1 blockade abated it (Giavridis et al.); that supports a multicell amplification mechanism and does not show the same sources or shares in every human product. Infection and other conditions can cause or accompany the same findings, so the cause of a fever cannot be read from timing alone. A comparable report gives its grading version, observation window and treated denominator, with onset, maximum grade, interventions and resolution. Safety belongs to the product, disease, tumour burden and preparation, so experience with one blood-cancer product does not supply a solid-tumour product's rate, and no severe CRS in a small early study does not rule out uncommon events. CRS is a different problem from injury to healthy tissue that carries the target (on-target, off-tumour) and from neurotoxicity (ICANS). The treatment need not carry a cytokine payload to trigger endogenous inflammatory signalling. Tumour response does not establish acceptable inflammatory risk, and mild CRS does not establish lack of anticancer activity. Stopping a treatment input does not guarantee immediate removal of released signals or established injury. In a fictional early study, no severe CRS and a modest cytokine rise would not make every fever harmless CRS: attribution, clinical findings, a named grading framework, treated denominator and observation window are still needed.

points.requirement: Three panels: gut-brain nerve signalling plus blood-borne and learned inputs; reporting windows 0-24 h and beyond 24 h with overlap; nausea and vomiting as separate outcomes; no vomiting does not establish no nausea.

evidence.explanation: Separate gut/brain and learned pathways support overlapping timing categories; nausea and vomiting remain distinct outcomes.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Nausea and vomiting are different outcomes. Nausea is the sensation and vomiting the expulsion; they often occur together but one can occur without the other. Serotonin acting at 5-HT3 receptors and substance P acting at NK1 receptors contribute with other transmitters, and in two phase II cisplatin studies serotonin appeared to dominate early vomiting and substance P the later phase, with overlap (Hesketh et al.), so acute and delayed are reporting windows and not sealed pathways. The NCI PDQ classes are acute (the first 24 hours after chemotherapy), delayed, anticipatory, breakthrough, refractory and chronic; anticipatory nausea was reported in about 29 per cent of patients and anticipatory vomiting in 11 per cent, with prevalence varying with definitions and methods. It lists other causes too, such as fluid and electrolyte imbalance including hypercalcaemia or volume depletion, and tells clinicians to consider all potential causes when people receive several treatments, so new nausea needs a cause assessment.

evidence.explanation: Separate gut/brain and learned pathways support overlapping timing categories; nausea and vomiting remain distinct outcomes.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Gut-to-brain nerve signalling, blood-borne inputs and learned associations can contribute, so one blocked route does not account for every symptom. The timing terms organise observations. Acute commonly refers to the first 24 hours, delayed to symptoms beyond 24 hours, anticipatory to symptoms before treatment associated with previous experiences, and breakthrough to symptoms despite prevention. Learned symptoms are real; delayed does not mean mild, and early and later responses can overlap with multiday treatment. Prevention and treatment of symptoms that have appeared are different questions. In a fictional trial, no vomiting and no rescue medicine can meet its complete-response endpoint while the participant still reports nausea. Relief of either symptom does not measure tumour response.

points.requirement: Sam: no vomiting, persistent nausea, met endpoint no vomiting/no rescue -> not "no symptoms"; report separately, check window; emetic-risk class != individual certainty.

evidence.explanation: The named Navari regimen and endpoint definitions show why no vomiting/no rescue does not mean no nausea; patient reporting and alternative causes remain visible.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading antiemetic trials. In Navari et al. (380 evaluable chemotherapy-naive adults given cisplatin at 70 mg per square metre or more, or cyclophosphamide-doxorubicin, all with dexamethasone, an NK1 antagonist and a 5-HT3 antagonist), nausea prevention was the primary endpoint and complete response (no emesis and no rescue medication) a secondary one. No nausea in the first 24 hours was 74 per cent with olanzapine against 45 per cent with placebo, while complete response was 86 per cent against 65 per cent, so a complete response does not mean no nausea, and a person with no vomiting can still have persistent nausea. MASCC and ESMO updated their regimen-specific guideline in 2023 (Herrstedt et al., published 2024). Read patient-reported nausea severity, vomiting episodes, rescue-medication use and the observation window together with the preventive regimen and adherence; symptoms that limit drinking or eating warrant prompt contact with the care team. This describes how to read endpoints, not a medicine schedule.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Gut-to-brain nerve signalling, blood-borne inputs and learned associations can contribute, so one blocked route does not account for every symptom. In a fictional trial, no vomiting and no rescue medicine can meet its complete-response endpoint while the participant still reports nausea. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading antiemetic trials. In Navari et al. evidence.explanation: Neurologic findings and their timing are assessed separately from CRS, with vascular associations scoped to the Gust cohort and competing causes retained.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, or ICANS, is a neurologic syndrome associated with immune-effector-cell therapy. Changes in language, attention, handwriting or awareness and more severe findings such as seizures need assessment against baseline and alternative explanations. An immune-marker plot does not establish the syndrome.

evidence.explanation: Neurologic findings and their timing are assessed separately from CRS, with vascular associations scoped to the Gust cohort and competing causes retained.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: What is known about mechanism, timing and attribution. In 133 adults given CD19 CAR T cells, Gust et al. found that those with severe neurotoxicity had endothelial activation (disseminated intravascular coagulation, capillary leak) and increased blood-brain barrier permeability, and that the permeable barrier failed to protect the cerebrospinal fluid from high systemic cytokine concentrations including interferon-gamma. Higher risk went with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, high marrow CD19-positive burden, high CAR T-cell dose, CRS and pre-existing neurological disease, and markers of endothelial activation before lymphodepletion were higher in people who later had grade 4 or worse neurotoxicity. That is an association in one product class and population, not a complete mechanism for every treatment. ICANS can accompany CRS or follow its own timetable, and neurotoxicity after CRS is scored separately, so recovery of blood pressure and oxygen does not show neurological recovery. If a person is confused while taking a sedating medicine and the ICE score falls, the grading rule requires that sedation be excluded, so the fall calls for clinical assessment, neither ignored nor diagnosed from the score alone. Clinical assessment also considers infection, metabolic disturbances, medicines and pre-existing neurologic disease. A safety report should retain onset, severity, attributed cause, interventions, duration, recovery and how many people were adequately observed. Separate fictional CRS and neurologic timelines can end at different times; they do not specify a typical order or duration. Stopping an engineered input does not guarantee immediate reversal of established neurologic injury.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: To attribute a malignancy after engineered-cell therapy, investigators ask whether the therapeutic sequence is present in the malignant cells, where the integrations are, whether they alter relevant genes, whether related clones were detectable earlier, and what prior therapy, underlying disease and pre-existing genetic changes contribute. Integration-site sequencing maps insertion locations, quantitative DNA assays estimate vector copies per cell, and flow cytometry, gene-expression measurement and pathology answer different questions about identity, function and malignancy; the sample is consumed by testing. This record gives no copy-number or clone-frequency threshold because none of the sources read sets one. An insertion that leaves no demonstrated gene effect, one that interrupts a gene and one that alters nearby regulation are different possibilities; none of those schematic locations assigns an incidence or time to cancer. evidence.explanation: Site, vector-copy, expression and pathology measurements have sampling limits; the fictional expanding clone does not itself establish cancer.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

points.requirement: 2000 WBC/uL x 20% = 400; 500 x 40% = 200 lymphocytes/uL: fraction doubles, count halves; no tumour kill measurement.

evidence.explanation: Serial absolute counts, fraction denominators, protocol context and harms are separate from cell-product or tumour-response outcomes; 400 versus 200 cells illustrates the distinction.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Counts need their denominators. A percentage of white cells is not an absolute count: with invented numbers, 20 per cent of 2,000 white cells per microlitre is 400 lymphocytes, and a later 40 per cent of 500 is 200, so the fraction doubled while the count halved. Lymphocyte and neutrophil counts are separate measurements, cytopenia means a low count of any blood cell type, and none of these measures tumour killing.

evidence.explanation: Serial absolute counts, fraction denominators, protocol context and harms are separate from cell-product or tumour-response outcomes; 400 versus 200 cells illustrates the distinction.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Lymphocytes include T cells, B cells and natural killer cells. Preparation can affect competition, regulation and, for donor products, host rejection; it can also act on cancer directly. It does not create a missing tumour antigen or guarantee that transferred cells enter a solid tumour. The need for preparation and its recovery criteria belong to the named protocol, rather than to every cell therapy. Serial blood counts consume blood samples rather than tumour tissue. Report absolute lymphocytes and neutrophils with units, sampling time and reference ranges, and measure transferred-cell number, location and function separately from the counts. More depletion is not automatically more benefit. Nonmyeloablative describes a regimen not intended to eliminate marrow blood production completely, rather than a promise of mild count suppression. Report severity, duration, recovery, infections, organ harms and relevant support with the regimen. More transferred cells, more depletion and more tumour killing are separate propositions.

points.requirement: Two fictional ANC curves share day 3 = 0.5 x10^9/L; A brief dip, B days 2-4 at 0.5; no infection probability or G-CSF threshold; same number does not establish same risk.

evidence.explanation: ANC units, depth, duration, timing and fever definition are retained; equal day-three values do not give equal course or infection probability.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading a neutrophil count. The absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is the number of neutrophils per volume of blood, written as cells per microlitre or as times 10 to the ninth per litre; it is more specific than the total white cell count, which includes other cell types. One ANC is a snapshot. Two invented curves make the point: both read 0.5 times 10 to the ninth per litre on day 3, but in one the count dips briefly and recovers, while in the other it stays at that level from day 2 to day 4. The matching number does not mean matching risk, because depth, duration and trend matter, and a count alone neither establishes nor excludes infection. Keep the sampling date, units, the laboratory's reference range and the place in the treatment cycle with the number. NCI patient guidance lists a temperature of 38 degrees Celsius or higher among the signs of infection to report promptly, whatever an earlier count showed. Better counts and fewer infections are related but separate outcomes, and neither is tumour response.

evidence.explanation: ANC units, depth, duration, timing and fever definition are retained; equal day-three values do not give equal course or infection probability.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: For a prevention study, retain the actual anticancer regimen, risk factors, comparator, fever-and-count definition and observation window. A toxicity report needs its count threshold and grading version. The same ANC on one date can conceal different durations of low counts, and an earlier reassuring count does not dismiss new fever or other infection symptoms. Supportive-care benefit, such as fewer infections, is distinct from cancer control.

evidence.explanation: ANC units, depth, duration, timing and fever definition are retained; equal day-three values do not give equal course or infection probability.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fever with neutropenia is defined by a stated temperature and a stated neutrophil threshold, which a trial or guideline should name. A low count alone does not establish infection, and infection can occur without neutropenia, so the count and the fever are separate findings that together define the syndrome and prompt assessment before any source of infection is found.

points.requirement: Purification and impurity assays distinguish unwanted double-stranded RNA, DNA, enzymes and the desired RNA; a cartoon column does not establish complete removal.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Two details matter when reading a product description. First, double-stranded RNA can arise from the transcription step itself: in one study T7 polymerase started transcription from a promoter-less DNA end and made an antisense strand that paired with the intended RNA and stimulated the innate sensor MDA5, and the effect fell with modified nucleotides or a lower magnesium concentration (Mu and colleagues). Purification was tested separately: HPLC removed contaminants including double-stranded RNA from nucleoside-modified transcripts and raised translation 10 to 1,000-fold in primary cells (Karikó and colleagues), and a cellulose method removed at least 90 per cent of double-stranded RNA with over 65 per cent recovery, taking out duplexes of 30 base pairs or longer while most of a 21 base-pair duplex remained (Baiersdörfer and colleagues). Second, a lipid nanoparticle is not the only formulation in use: in the pancreatic cancer phase I trial of autogene cevumeran each patient's vaccine held two uridine mRNA strands, each encoding up to 10 neoepitopes, formulated as lipoplex nanoparticles of about 400 nm made from the cationic lipid DOTMA and the phospholipid DOPE and given intravenously (Rojas and colleagues). Release testing is layered: a review of mRNA analytics lists identity and modification analysis, poly(A) tail, RNA content and integrity, double-stranded RNA and residual DNA as separate attributes, and a review of mRNA manufacturing cites a regulator-recommended residual DNA limit of 10 ng per dose (Losada and colleagues; Nowak and colleagues). Particle size and composition measurements do not by themselves show that usable RNA reaches the cytosol of the intended cell.

points.requirement: Purification and impurity assays distinguish unwanted double-stranded RNA, DNA, enzymes and the desired RNA; a cartoon column does not establish complete removal.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Two details matter when reading a product description. First, double-stranded RNA can arise from the transcription step itself: in one study T7 polymerase started transcription from a promoter-less DNA end and made an antisense strand that paired with the intended RNA and stimulated the innate sensor MDA5, and the effect fell with modified nucleotides or a lower magnesium concentration (Mu and colleagues). Purification was tested separately: HPLC removed contaminants including double-stranded RNA from nucleoside-modified transcripts and raised translation 10 to 1,000-fold in primary cells (Karikó and colleagues), and a cellulose method removed at least 90 per cent of double-stranded RNA with over 65 per cent recovery, taking out duplexes of 30 base pairs or longer while most of a 21 base-pair duplex remained (Baiersdörfer and colleagues). Second, a lipid nanoparticle is not the only formulation in use: in the pancreatic cancer phase I trial of autogene cevumeran each patient's vaccine held two uridine mRNA strands, each encoding up to 10 neoepitopes, formulated as lipoplex nanoparticles of about 400 nm made from the cationic lipid DOTMA and the phospholipid DOPE and given intravenously (Rojas and colleagues). Release testing is layered: a review of mRNA analytics lists identity and modification analysis, poly(A) tail, RNA content and integrity, double-stranded RNA and residual DNA as separate attributes, and a review of mRNA manufacturing cites a regulator-recommended residual DNA limit of 10 ng per dose (Losada and colleagues; Nowak and colleagues). Particle size and composition measurements do not by themselves show that usable RNA reaches the cytosol of the intended cell.

review.rationale: Amount, rate, cargo, biological function, controlled model response and clinical benefit remain different observations. Schematic geometry and stipulated examples are qualified in reader prose; no image is itself empirical efficacy evidence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Hoslett and colleagues' 2026 preclinical study investigated selective disposal of trapped PARP1 involving TEX264, the protein-remodelling enzyme p97 and LC3-associated lysosomal handling. Autophagic handling of nuclear material is called nucleophagy. Perturbing the machinery increased chromatin-associated PARP1 and PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the studied systems; complementation and cargo-recognition experiments supported the proposed route. Some trapping experiments also supplied the DNA-damaging agent MMS, so their conditions are not every drug-alone exposure. The authors left the exact export or packaging of nuclear cargo, and macroautophagy versus direct microautophagy, unresolved. A clearance cartoon is therefore a mechanistic model, not established compartment geometry. Expression-survival associations do not validate TEX264 expression as a treatment-response test.
evidence.explanation: All four figure ideas and nucleophagy/clearance definition are represented; nuclear packaging is a proposed route, not settled geometry. complete raw Europe PMC abstract read

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional culture, more death with a PARP inhibitor plus a lysosomal drug fits several explanations: reduced clearance of trapped PARP, toxicity from the second drug itself, or another altered stress response. Measure chromatin-bound PARP1 over the relevant interval, include both single-drug conditions, and test the proposed clearance machinery with suitable independent perturbation and restoration. Unchanged trapped cargo despite more death argues against that particular clearance explanation. TEX264 or p97 perturbation is complementary evidence, not automatically perfectly selective, because proteins can have other functions. Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine alter lysosomal processes broadly. Survival alone, high recycling RNA or a broad lysosomal effect does not identify selective trapped-PARP disposal or establish patient benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: binding of cells to a specified peptide held by a specified HLA allele, under the staining conditions. points.requirement: Target death under one tested condition does not establish universal target specificity, natural presentation, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Scope of the methods: a flow-based assay labels targets with a dye, adds a dead-cell stain and analyses released nuclei, which lowers errors from target-effector aggregates, and it reported four nuclear staining patterns separating target and effector nuclei and live and dead cells (Rabinovich 2019). A peptide-pulsed target assay compares CFSE-low peptide-loaded and CFSE-high unloaded CD4 T-cell targets and calculates lytic units from specific lysis at several ratios (Noto 2013), so its result belongs to that artificial peptide loading, which can bypass the tumour's own processing. Degranulation (CD107 exposure) preceded cytolysis and was concordant with interferon gamma in the original report, and is distinct from completed target death (Betts 2003). Model-specific killing does not show trafficking, persistence, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit.
evidence.explanation: Artificial loading, target identity, preparation and model-dependent killing do not establish universal natural display, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A trial defines primary, secondary and exploratory outcomes and how they are measured and analysed. points.requirement: The conventional multimer example tests a paired peptide-HLA reagent binding a receptor under assay conditions. It is not direct loose-peptide/TCR binding or proof of natural tumour display.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The original peptide-MHC tetramer study made soluble multimeric peptide-display complexes to identify antigen-specific T cells. Binding correlated with cytotoxicity in the tested systems, but those observations are different measurements. The chosen peptide and HLA molecule define which interaction is tested. Detecting multimer-binding cells does not by itself establish natural display of that peptide by a tumor, successful target-cell killing or a clinical treatment effect.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: binding of cells to a specified peptide held by a specified HLA allele, under the staining conditions. How: HLA molecules are assembled with the selected peptide and several copies are attached to a labelled scaffold (a tetramer is one format), cells are exposed and analysed, usually by flow cytometry, with viable-cell and gate selection. Input: blood or tissue cells, where staining uses a defined aliquot and compatibility with later living-cell assays depends on the preparation, and the reagent must match both peptide and allele. Thresholds: gate and positivity rules need background and reagent controls, and no universal percentage shows efficacy. Failure modes: nonspecific binding, weak binding, dead cells, a wrong or poorly formed reagent, chain differences or sampling loss. It cannot tell cytokine response, tumour-cell killing, healthy-tissue specificity or benefit.

points.requirement: Reagent binding, receptor identity/abundance and effector function are separate observations, with assay-specific preparation and analysed-cell denominators.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Denominators, fictional arithmetic: 100 stained cells among 10,000 gated CD8 T cells is 1%, and the same 100 among 40,000 viable acquired cells is 0.25%. Both are correct and answer different denominator questions, and neither is a body-wide census or a killing rate. A tetramer-negative result is not a census of every possible relevant receptor, because some receptors bind too weakly for a given staining method, and HLA restriction belongs to the peptide-HLA pair and not the peptide alone.

points.requirement: A stimulated secretion assay captures a selected secreted molecule on the assay surface under its conditions; it does not directly measure target-cell death.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: cells that secrete a chosen molecule, most often interferon gamma, under defined stimulation, counted as spots on an antibody-coated membrane. How: capture antibodies hold the released molecule near the cell, the cells are removed and detection reagents make localised spots visible. Input: viable cells, often PBMCs, allocated to the test. Prior culture expansion changes the measured population, and the cells are removed before the membrane spots are read. Output: spot-forming units per stated number of input cells, with background handling stated. Thresholds: response and quality rules fixed in advance for that assay and study, so one paper's positivity rule is not imported into another laboratory's report. Failure modes: high background, dead cells, weak stimulation, merged spots, inconsistent counting or failed controls. It cannot tell each receptor's target, natural tumour recognition, safety in healthy tissue or clinical benefit.

points.requirement: A killing assay needs identifiable targets, a target-only baseline and an effector-plus-target condition, with suitable recognition/HLA and viability controls for its claim.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: whether specified effector cells cause death of specified target cells under controlled laboratory conditions, at a stated effector-to-target ratio and time. Readouts: flow cytometry that separates labelled targets from effectors and uses death-associated staining, release assays, or imaging over time. A fall in a metabolic or growth signal can reflect slowed growth and not death, so it needs validation as evidence of killing. Controls: target-only survival wells, effector identification and viability, a positive-control response, irrelevant or antigen-negative targets and suitable antigen or presentation perturbations, plus maximum release where relevant. Failure modes: high spontaneous death, mistaken target identity, aggregates, dye transfer, artificial loading, mismatched ratios or a readout that mainly measures growth.
evidence.explanation: Target-only baseline and effector-plus-target comparisons retain identified cells, ratios, timing and specificity controls; detail beyond the fresh abstract retains the source-depth limitation. points.requirement: Target death under one tested condition does not establish universal target specificity, natural presentation, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Scope of the methods: a flow-based assay labels targets with a dye, adds a dead-cell stain and analyses released nuclei, which lowers errors from target-effector aggregates, and it reported four nuclear staining patterns separating target and effector nuclei and live and dead cells (Rabinovich 2019). A peptide-pulsed target assay compares CFSE-low peptide-loaded and CFSE-high unloaded CD4 T-cell targets and calculates lytic units from specific lysis at several ratios (Noto 2013), so its result belongs to that artificial peptide loading, which can bypass the tumour's own processing. Degranulation (CD107 exposure) preceded cytolysis and was concordant with interferon gamma in the original report, and is distinct from completed target death (Betts 2003). Model-specific killing does not show trafficking, persistence, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit.
evidence.explanation: Artificial loading, target identity, preparation and model-dependent killing do not establish universal natural display, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Keep the identities and preparation of both effector and target cells, whether a cell line, engineered target or patient-derived preparation, together with medium, effector-to-target ratio and exposure time. Reproducibility and biological specificity need checking for the specimen, model and intended claim.

points.requirement: Clinical outcomes require separate evidence in a defined study population, comparator and endpoint; the schematic does not claim every clinical comparison is randomized.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A trial defines primary, secondary and exploratory outcomes and how they are measured and analysed. The primary question informs design, sample size and testing; having a secondary endpoint does not by itself establish whether it was adequately powered or met a prespecified testing rule. Overall survival concerns death from any cause, while response, progression, symptoms and quality of life answer different questions. A composite endpoint combines specified events, so its definition and starting time matter. FDA's December 2018 nonbinding oncology-endpoint guidance distinguishes direct clinical benefit and context-dependent surrogate evidence; use in an approval does not make an endpoint interchangeable with survival in every setting.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional two-drug table normalises remaining viability to vehicle at 100 per cent: A leaves 70, B leaves 80, and combination examples leave 56 or 30. Highest single agent uses the better single-drug effect, a 70 per cent remaining-viability reference here. Bliss independence predicts 0.70 times 0.80 = 0.56, or 56 per cent. Both combinations exceed the HSA effect; 56 matches Bliss while 30 exceeds it at that dose pair. A further combination leaving 65 exceeds HSA but not Bliss. Loewe additivity instead needs equivalent-dose information from suitable individual dose-response curves; this one-point table cannot establish it. Report the model, dose-pair pattern, uncertainty and schedule. Interaction relative to a reference does not identify a biological mechanism, tolerable human exposure or a treatment choice.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Consider a fictional trial in operable cancer with one random assignment to study drug plus common chemotherapy, surgery and study drug afterwards, or placebo on the same sequence. Comparing the whole assigned strategies does not isolate starting the drug only after surgery, because there is no second postoperative assignment. From the common randomisation origin, a recurrence in someone still alive and a death without earlier recurrence both count in a recurrence-or-death composite; only the death counts in overall survival. An improvement in a composite need not mean that every component improved. This is a reasoning example, with no dosing schedule or effect size.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional two-drug table normalises remaining viability to vehicle at 100 per cent: A leaves 70, B leaves 80, and combination examples leave 56 or 30. Highest single agent uses the better single-drug effect, a 70 per cent remaining-viability reference here. Bliss independence predicts 0.70 times 0.80 = 0.56, or 56 per cent. Both combinations exceed the HSA effect; 56 matches Bliss while 30 exceeds it at that dose pair. A further combination leaving 65 exceeds HSA but not Bliss. Loewe additivity instead needs equivalent-dose information from suitable individual dose-response curves; this one-point table cannot establish it. Report the model, dose-pair pattern, uncertainty and schedule. Interaction relative to a reference does not identify a biological mechanism, tolerable human exposure or a treatment choice.

Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A completed macroautophagosome has separate inner and outer membranes, with space between them. A direct-fusion sketch omits intermediate endosomal interactions described in multicellular organisms; it is not the complete route taken by every compartment.

points.requirement: Ubiquitin tagging and proteasomal degradation are distinct steps, and not every ubiquitin linkage or tagged protein has the same degradative fate.

A protein can fall because synthesis changes, cells are lost or degradation increases, so abundance alone does not identify the route. Proteasome inhibitors and recruited-degradation strategies intervene at different steps; mechanistic measurements do not by themselves establish clinical benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) system, with two main classes of peptide-display molecule. Classical class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) has a heavy chain, beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a bound peptide, is found on most nucleated cells, usually displays peptides from proteins made inside the cell and is read by CD8 T cells. Class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) has alpha and beta chains with a bound peptide, is mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (expression can be induced elsewhere), usually displays proteins processed in vesicles, often acquired from outside, and is read by CD4 T cells. These are common routes, not exclusive lists: cross-presentation puts externally acquired antigen on class I without making it class II, and a CD4 response is not proof of matching class I tumour display. CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors and usual recognition partners, not guarantees of cell function. Structural work shows the T-cell receptor lying across the peptide and HLA together (Garboczi et al., 1996), CD8 contacting the class I alpha2 and alpha3 domains and B2M (Gao et al., 1997) and CD4 engaging a separate class II region (Yin et al., 2012); these constructs do not define universal angles or functions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. CDR3 is an informative variable region, but neither a beta-chain sequence nor CDR3 alone specifies the complete paired receptor or its function.

Particular receptors can cross-react across peptide and HLA contexts; that does not establish a universal cross-reactivity rate. Paired receptor identity, binding, activation, target-cell death and clinical benefit require different evidence. A response by one reconstructed pair to peptide-loaded cells does not establish that another alpha-chain pairing recognises the same target, or that either kills naturally presenting tumour cells. Use irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls. Peptide loading can bypass natural processing, and contact diagrams are not healthy-tissue safety tests.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is DNA outside intact cells in a specimen. Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) is the tumour-derived part of the plasma DNA mixture, rather than a different material competing with cfDNA. DNA from non-tumour tissues can contribute much of that mixture, as illustrated by Moss and colleagues' methylation-atlas study. Total extracted DNA is therefore not a tumour measurement. A finite evaluated aliquot can contain no qualifying tumour signal even when disease exists elsewhere.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The two-window comparison is about scope. A finite plasma aliquot contains extracellular DNA, of which tumour-derived fragments may be one part; breast MRI observes regional, sequence-dependent features rather than individual cancer cells. Contrast enhancement reflects vascular and contrast-delivery behaviour as well as the acquisition protocol; it is not a one-to-one viable-cell count. In the 84-person I-SPY2 MRI pilot, functional tumour volume summed voxels meeting 70% enhancement about two and a half minutes after contrast, inside a manually drawn box around the lesion. A camera-and-stream analogy illustrates those two sampled views without promising that every tumour sheds DNA. Keep the imaging method visible: mammography uses X-rays, ultrasound uses sound, and PET/CT combines tracer-distribution images with anatomical CT images. A formal response category needs its framework, comparison timepoint and findings outside a selected lesion measurement. None of these measurements is an interchangeable all-body tumour-cell number.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Spatial transcriptomics measures RNA signals while retaining information about where they came from in a tissue section. Sequencing capture and imaging-based detection use different measurement units. A third approach, region-of-interest profiling such as digital spatial profiling, releases oligonucleotide tags only from regions an operator chooses; the method paper describes regions covering 1 to about 5,000 cells and panels of up to 44 proteins, or 1,412 genes with sequencing readout, on formalin-fixed tissue (Merritt and colleagues, 2020), so the result depends on how the regions were selected. The original sequencing-based method placed sections on arrays of positionally barcoded primers and kept two-dimensional position (Ståhl and colleagues, 2016); a capture spot is a positional barcode and can span several cells. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) system, with two main classes of peptide-display molecule. Classical class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) has a heavy chain, beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a bound peptide, is found on most nucleated cells, usually displays peptides from proteins made inside the cell and is read by CD8 T cells. Class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) has alpha and beta chains with a bound peptide, is mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (expression can be induced elsewhere), usually displays proteins processed in vesicles, often acquired from outside, and is read by CD4 T cells. These are common routes, not exclusive lists: cross-presentation puts externally acquired antigen on class I without making it class II, and a CD4 response is not proof of matching class I tumour display. CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors and usual recognition partners, not guarantees of cell function. Structural work shows the T-cell receptor lying across the peptide and HLA together (Garboczi et al., 1996), CD8 contacting the class I alpha2 and alpha3 domains and B2M (Gao et al., 1997) and CD4 engaging a separate class II region (Yin et al., 2012); these constructs do not define universal angles or functions.

HLA alleles are shared across people, and a person inherits a combination that is not necessarily unique. Each person inherits two copies each of HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C, so a cell can display up to six classical class I variants at once. The IPD-IMGT/HLA statistics page read on 9 November 2026 listed 46,146 HLA alleles, 31,311 class I and 14,835 class II (9,457 HLA-A, 11,328 HLA-B and 9,580 HLA-C alleles). Binding predictors estimate whether a peptide can fit a specified allele's groove, but processing, transport, loading and surface expression decide whether it is displayed. Sarkizova et al. (2020) profiled more than 185,000 peptides eluted from 95 mono-allelic cell lines to learn allele-specific motifs and build prediction models; that is allele-level data, not proof of any cell's display. Kaur et al. (2017) showed that HLA-C surface expression varies across individuals in an allele-specific manner, influenced by the structure of the peptide-binding cleft and peptide diversity; Apps and colleagues found lower HLA-C than HLA-A/B in the analysed healthy-donor peripheral blood lymphocytes with the A*02:01/B*44:02/C*05:01 haplotype; the magnitude differed between flow cytometry and mass spectrometry. This is a defined comparison, not a universal hierarchy. The small HLA-C peptide share observed by Schellens and colleagues in four B lymphoblastoid cell lines was also affected by their assignment method, which gave HLA-A/B precedence; it is not a universal biological fraction.

In cancer, class I HLA shows peptides to CD8 T cells and is also the main ligand for inhibitory receptors on natural killer cells, so losing it can hide a tumour from T cells while removing a brake on NK cells. HLA-E and HLA-G are nonclassical and vary little between people; HLA-E presents leader peptides from other class I molecules and binds the NK receptor CD94/NKG2A (Braud et al., 1998, with HLA-E tetramers). Tumours can lose a presenting allele (HLA loss of heterozygosity), alter processing or reduce expression, and allele-specific loss differs from complete loss of conventional class I display; targets on retained alleles may remain possible. Tran et al. (2016) documented a colorectal cancer lesion that progressed after T-cell therapy against mutant KRAS G12D, which had lost the chromosome 6 haplotype encoding the restricting HLA-C*08:02; this shows escape in one patient, not a rate. Typing, protein expression, recovered peptide, recognition and killing are different observations, and a conventional surface-target engager avoids peptide-HLA dependence while a peptide-HLA-directed engager keeps it.

B2M is the light chain of classical class I and does not span the membrane; class II contains no B2M, so CD4 T-cell recognition can remain when B2M is lost. B2M also partners other class I-like molecules: UniProt records heterotrimers with HLA-E, HLA-G, HLA-F and MR1 and lists CD1 interactions, and a B2M mutation caused deficiency of the neonatal Fc receptor FcRn in two siblings (Wani et al., 2006), so complete B2M loss can remove more than classical class I. Loss of one HLA allele can leave other presenting alleles usable, whereas loss of functional B2M impairs many class I targets at once, so several peptides on different alleles are not independent protection. A B2M variant, low RNA, absent surface class I and a blood B2M concentration are different observations: one variant does not show complete functional loss, and blood B2M does not count tumour peptide-HLA complexes. Zaretsky et al. (2016) linked a truncating B2M mutation to lost surface class I in one melanoma relapse after PD-1 blockade, which is a mechanism in that setting, not a frequency. Reduced class I display does not guarantee NK-cell killing, because activating signals are still needed.
evidence.explanation: Peptide-HLA recognition and natural display are specified; intact-protein detection is not universal immune recognition or killing. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) system, with two main classes of peptide-display molecule. Classical class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) has a heavy chain, beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a bound peptide, is found on most nucleated cells, usually displays peptides from proteins made inside the cell and is read by CD8 T cells. Class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) has alpha and beta chains with a bound peptide, is mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (expression can be induced elsewhere), usually displays proteins processed in vesicles, often acquired from outside, and is read by CD4 T cells. These are common routes, not exclusive lists: cross-presentation puts externally acquired antigen on class I without making it class II, and a CD4 response is not proof of matching class I tumour display. CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors and usual recognition partners, not guarantees of cell function. Structural work shows the T-cell receptor lying across the peptide and HLA together (Garboczi et al., 1996), CD8 contacting the class I alpha2 and alpha3 domains and B2M (Gao et al., 1997) and CD4 engaging a separate class II region (Yin et al., 2012); these constructs do not define universal angles or functions.

HLA alleles are shared across people, and a person inherits a combination that is not necessarily unique. Each person inherits two copies each of HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C, so a cell can display up to six classical class I variants at once. The IPD-IMGT/HLA statistics page read on 9 November 2026 listed 46,146 HLA alleles, 31,311 class I and 14,835 class II (9,457 HLA-A, 11,328 HLA-B and 9,580 HLA-C alleles). Binding predictors estimate whether a peptide can fit a specified allele's groove, but processing, transport, loading and surface expression decide whether it is displayed. Sarkizova et al. (2020) profiled more than 185,000 peptides eluted from 95 mono-allelic cell lines to learn allele-specific motifs and build prediction models; that is allele-level data, not proof of any cell's display. Kaur et al. (2017) showed that HLA-C surface expression varies across individuals in an allele-specific manner, influenced by the structure of the peptide-binding cleft and peptide diversity; Apps and colleagues found lower HLA-C than HLA-A/B in the analysed healthy-donor peripheral blood lymphocytes with the A*02:01/B*44:02/C*05:01 haplotype; the magnitude differed between flow cytometry and mass spectrometry. This is a defined comparison, not a universal hierarchy. The small HLA-C peptide share observed by Schellens and colleagues in four B lymphoblastoid cell lines was also affected by their assignment method, which gave HLA-A/B precedence; it is not a universal biological fraction.

In cancer, class I HLA shows peptides to CD8 T cells and is also the main ligand for inhibitory receptors on natural killer cells, so losing it can hide a tumour from T cells while removing a brake on NK cells. HLA-E and HLA-G are nonclassical and vary little between people; HLA-E presents leader peptides from other class I molecules and binds the NK receptor CD94/NKG2A (Braud et al., 1998, with HLA-E tetramers). Tumours can lose a presenting allele (HLA loss of heterozygosity), alter processing or reduce expression, and allele-specific loss differs from complete loss of conventional class I display; targets on retained alleles may remain possible. Tran et al. (2016) documented a colorectal cancer lesion that progressed after T-cell therapy against mutant KRAS G12D, which had lost the chromosome 6 haplotype encoding the restricting HLA-C*08:02; this shows escape in one patient, not a rate. Typing, protein expression, recovered peptide, recognition and killing are different observations, and a conventional surface-target engager avoids peptide-HLA dependence while a peptide-HLA-directed engager keeps it.

B2M is the light chain of classical class I and does not span the membrane; class II contains no B2M, so CD4 T-cell recognition can remain when B2M is lost. B2M also partners other class I-like molecules: UniProt records heterotrimers with HLA-E, HLA-G, HLA-F and MR1 and lists CD1 interactions, and a B2M mutation caused deficiency of the neonatal Fc receptor FcRn in two siblings (Wani et al., 2006), so complete B2M loss can remove more than classical class I. Loss of one HLA allele can leave other presenting alleles usable, whereas loss of functional B2M impairs many class I targets at once, so several peptides on different alleles are not independent protection. A B2M variant, low RNA, absent surface class I and a blood B2M concentration are different observations: one variant does not show complete functional loss, and blood B2M does not count tumour peptide-HLA complexes. Zaretsky et al. (2016) linked a truncating B2M mutation to lost surface class I in one melanoma relapse after PD-1 blockade, which is a mechanism in that setting, not a frequency. Reduced class I display does not guarantee NK-cell killing, because activating signals are still needed.
evidence.explanation: Peptide-HLA recognition and natural display are specified; intact-protein detection is not universal immune recognition or killing. points.requirement: The protein-coding route does not require every RNA to be translated, and a nucleus-office analogy omits other genomic and cellular compartments.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: RNA, short for ribonucleic acid, uses ribose and usually uracil in place of DNA’s thymine. It is often single-stranded but can fold through internal pairing. Messenger RNA carries a coding template; ribosomal RNA contributes to ribosome structure and catalysis; transfer RNA brings amino acids; regulatory RNAs influence other molecules. Many nuclear messages receive a 5-prime cap and poly(A) tail and have introns removed by splicing before translation, but these features are not universal to all RNAs. Ribosomes read a coding sequence in codons to produce a polypeptide; processing, folding and localization follow.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Residual tumour here means cancer remaining in the sampled tissue after treatment. For residual-tumour research, first support malignant-cell identity, then ask which recovered states, target messages and immune profiles are present. A stress programme does not establish a genetic clone or explain survival. In Kim and colleagues' twenty-person triple-negative breast-cancer study, longitudinal exome data and single-cell DNA/RNA data in eight participants supported selection of pre-existing genotypes alongside expression reprogramming under the studied treatment. This is not a universal resistance mechanism. Compare the sampled region, time, preparation, recovery and analysis before attributing a difference to treatment; a missing cluster need not have been eliminated. In a separate fictional calculation, an input suspension truly containing 4 percent malignant nuclei gives an expectation of 240 among 6,000 retained profiles only if malignant and other nuclei have equal inclusion through recovery, capture and quality filtering. Tissue-area cellularity is a different denominator. The calculation is neither a yield forecast nor an adequacy cutoff.

points.requirement: LC3 carrier flux, delivery to an acidic compartment and actual selected-cargo breakdown are related but distinct measurements requiring suitable controls.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.
evidence.explanation: The guideline-derived note explicitly separates LC3 carrier and selected-cargo flux, reporter limitations and complementary measurements. points.requirement: Autophagy initiation differs from completed lysosomal degradation. A change in mTOR-associated restraint or autophagosome abundance does not establish complete flux.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. PTEN, phosphatase and tensin homolog, removes a phosphate from a PI3K-generated lipid signal. These protein and lipid reactions need their own readouts. Ibrahim 2012 found that PI3K inhibition reduced BRCA1/2 expression and increased PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the BRCA-proficient triple-negative breast cancer models studied. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. Releasing an initiation brake does not establish completed cargo degradation or protective recycling. The two branches can change together without revealing the net survival effect. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.
evidence.explanation: Changing initiation restraint and establishing completed cargo handling are separate outputs. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

points.requirement: More death after a valid perturbation can support a protective role in that system, while less drug-induced death can support a contribution to that response. Neither observation alone identifies a perfectly selective mechanism.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Breast-cancer studies illustrate the conditional direction. Bellare 2021 reported that genetic disruption or chloroquine increased talazoparib sensitivity in the tested HR-proficient cells and xenografts. Arun 2015 found that ATG5 reduction partly reduced olaparib-induced apoptosis in BRCA2-mutant HCC-1428 cells, an oestrogen-receptor-positive line rather than a triple-negative model. These different drugs, models and perturbations do not define one protective or death-promoting label for all tumours. Bellare's 2025 correction replaced representative MCF7 images in Figure 5c as well as a liver-histology image in Figure 6f. The authors stated that replicate-based quantification and interpretation were unchanged; that statement is theirs, not an independent validation of the replacement images.
evidence.explanation: The stated studies support different conditional directions, rather than a selective mechanism or a guaranteed treatment benefit. points.requirement: Cargo delivery, membrane fusion, breakdown and product return are separate steps. Reuse symbols are not proof of extracellular secretion or transport of every product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A completed macroautophagosome has separate inner and outer membranes, with space between them. When it fuses with a lysosome, the outer membrane joins the lysosomal boundary, while the inner membrane is degraded before enzymes gain access to the enclosed cargo. Itakura and colleagues located syntaxin 17 on completed autophagosomes, and Tsuboyama and colleagues found that loss of ATG conjugation systems markedly delayed inner-membrane degradation even when fusion occurred. A direct-fusion sketch omits intermediate endosomal interactions described in multicellular organisms; it is not the complete route taken by every compartment.
evidence.explanation: Fusion, inner-membrane breakdown and defined product export are separate steps; mammalian amino-acid and yeast evidence do not establish every transported product. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Product return has evidence in defined systems. In leucine-starved cultured human HEK-293T cells, Wyant and colleagues found that SLC38A9 was needed for leucine made by lysosomal protein breakdown to reach the cytosol; the response also depended on the autophagy protein ATG7. Abu-Remaileh and colleagues measured regulated lysosomal amino-acid exchange in mammalian cells. Yeast experiments identified Atg22, Avt3 and Avt4 as partially redundant vacuolar amino-acid exporters. These results support amino-acid recycling in those systems, without establishing transport of every breakdown product, secretion from the cell or guaranteed growth.

points.requirement: Literal toy data, renderer code, figure symbols and source hashes can be checked for identity and internal consistency without establishing empirical observations, historical authorship, expert approval or clinical validation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional two-drug table normalises remaining viability to vehicle at 100 per cent: A leaves 70, B leaves 80, and combination examples leave 56 or 30. Highest single agent uses the better single-drug effect, a 70 per cent remaining-viability reference here. Bliss independence predicts 0.70 times 0.80 = 0.56, or 56 per cent. Both combinations exceed the HSA effect; 56 matches Bliss while 30 exceeds it at that dose pair. A further combination leaving 65 exceeds HSA but not Bliss. Loewe additivity instead needs equivalent-dose information from suitable individual dose-response curves; this one-point table cannot establish it. Report the model, dose-pair pattern, uncertainty and schedule. Interaction relative to a reference does not identify a biological mechanism, tolerable human exposure or a treatment choice.
evidence.explanation: Literal renderer output, fixture hashes and fictional symbols establish source identity/internal consistency, rather than historical authorship, empirical observations or approval. At damaged DNA it can build signals on proteins from chains of the chemical unit ADP-ribose, called poly(ADP-ribose), or PAR. Catalytic inhibition reduces this output. Some inhibitors can also stabilise DNA-associated PARP complexes, often called trapping. A repair-worker analogy separates a reduced call for help from a worker remaining in a doorway; proteins and medicines have no purpose, and the cell has more than one response route.

points.requirement: Growth and nutrient regulation of PI3K/AKT/mTORC1 is a simplified network with distinct molecular and initiation outputs, not one universal linear route.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

points.requirement: PI3K, AKT and mTOR interventions are not interchangeable, and PI3K-alpha/PIK3CA is distinct from PIKFYVE.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Rapalogs, PI3K or AKT inhibitors and ATP-site mTOR kinase inhibitors are different interventions. In Rodrik-Outmezguine's 2011 models, inhibiting both mTOR complexes initially reduced AKT Ser473 and Thr308 phosphorylation, but relief of receptor feedback later restored Thr308 phosphorylation and AKT signalling while Ser473 remained suppressed. A Ser473 result therefore did not measure all AKT activity. O'Reilly's rapalog study and Harrington's IRS feedback work likewise explain why lower mTORC1 output can coexist with increased upstream signalling. These are measured responses in specified systems, not inevitable behaviour or a universal combination prescription.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K means phosphoinositide 3-kinase; AKT is also called protein kinase B. Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, mTORC1, integrates growth and nutrient inputs. A second branch concerns mTORC1 restraint of ULK1-associated autophagy initiation, studied by Kim 2011. A model already lacking the relevant repair function cannot be assumed to gain the same vulnerability as one in which that function is newly reduced; measure protein and repair function, flux and survival under the actual compound, dose and schedule.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: DNA contains nucleotide chains with a sugar–phosphate backbone and the bases A, T, C and G. Complementary A–T and C–G pairing joins antiparallel strands. Nuclear chromosomes contain DNA associated with proteins as chromatin; nucleosomes organize DNA around histones. Mitochondria carry a separate genome. A gene is a functional region within DNA, rather than an entire chromosome. Replication copies DNA, while transcription produces RNA from a selected template. Packaging and gene presence do not establish active transcription or a functional protein.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: RNA, short for ribonucleic acid, uses ribose and usually uracil in place of DNA’s thymine. It is often single-stranded but can fold through internal pairing. Messenger RNA carries a coding template; ribosomal RNA contributes to ribosome structure and catalysis; transfer RNA brings amino acids; regulatory RNAs influence other molecules. Many nuclear messages receive a 5-prime cap and poly(A) tail and have introns removed by splicing before translation, but these features are not universal to all RNAs. Ribosomes read a coding sequence in codons to produce a polypeptide; processing, folding and localization follow.

points.requirement: Conventional alpha-beta recognition depends on peptide presented in an appropriate HLA context; the drawing does not establish literal recognition of only one immutable peptide.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Conventional alpha-beta TCR-T introduces selected paired receptor-chain instructions into therapeutic T cells. The receptor recognizes a displayed peptide-HLA complex, rather than entering the tumor cell to bind the whole source protein. Natural processing, the required HLA allele, surface display, receptor expression and useful cell function remain different questions. This differs from administering a soluble TCR/CD3 protein that recruits other T cells.
evidence.explanation: Conventional peptide/HLA recognition is stated, with a cross-reactivity example that contradicts literal one-peptide-only wording. Source/depth references: scientific-authoring-bodies-13-2026-11-13/source-group-register.json#gamma-delta-recognition. Subset/receptor-specific recognition and a preclinical HLA-restricted counterexample; curated human ligand identities and targeted review stress-ligand passages. No universal HLA independence, no-GvHD, donor compatibility or clinical efficacy claim. Fictional counts/volumes and simplified shapes/ordered gates are not measured outcomes, personal decisions or a validated clinical algorithm. Personal-case material is excluded.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cameron investigated fatal cardiac toxicity with one affinity-enhanced MAGE-A3 receptor and identified a cross-reactive Titin peptide presented by HLA-A*01 as the most likely cause. points.requirement: Gamma-delta recognition varies by subset and receptor context; less classical peptide-HLA dependence must not be generalized to every gamma-delta cell.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Recognition differs by subset, and it is not always free of HLA. For the Vγ9Vδ2 subset, which responds to phosphoantigens (small phosphorylated metabolites produced by microbes and overexpressed by some cancers), butyrophilin 2A1 (BTN2A1) binds the Vγ9 chain of the receptor, associates with a second butyrophilin, BTN3A1, and the two act together to start the response; a second ligand, possibly BTN3A1, binds a separate region that includes the Vδ2 chain (Rigau et al., 2020). This is not a peptide sitting in an HLA groove. HLA independence is also not universal: one characterised Vγ5Vδ1 receptor was restricted by HLA-A*24:02 and depended on the CD8-alpha co-receptor, acting on blood-cancer and solid-tumour cells in vitro and in vivo while sparing healthy tissue in those models (Kierkels et al., 2019). That receptor's mechanism is not an eligibility rule for the family.
evidence.explanation: A specific HLA-restricted counterexample prevents extending one gamma-delta recognition mechanism to the family. points.requirement: Adding a CAR gives gamma-delta cells an engineered antigen-recognition route alongside their baseline biology, without proving both routes function in every product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: An engineered receptor is a separate recognition route. Adding a GD2-directed chimeric antigen receptor to expanded human Vδ1 and Vδ2 cells increased GD2-specific killing of GD2-expressing cancer cell lines, did not impair movement towards tumour cells in vitro, and expanded Vδ2 cells kept the ability to take up tumour antigen and cross-present it to alpha-beta T cells (Capsomidis et al., 2018). That is a preclinical result for that preparation, and it does not show that any gamma-delta product enters tumours, cross-presents usefully or prevents antigen escape in patients. An allogeneic gamma-delta product that the registry names HLA-G-CAR.BiTE allogeneic γδ T cells (NCT06150885, phase 1 and 2) was listed as recruiting when the registry record was read for this entry; the record describes the product and the study design and reports no efficacy. A receptor added to a cell needs its own target on the tumour, HLA-low does not mean target-positive, and avoiding peptide presentation is not the same as avoiding antigen escape. Cells are identified by flow cytometry and receptor sequencing, but a response against one target line does not establish tumour entry, persistence or benefit, and matched cells without the added receptor are needed to separate native from engineered recognition. Two cautions are OnCo's reasoning and not findings of the cited papers: a product made of many receptor clones is not automatically broader or more effective than one defined clone, and the name gamma-delta describes the receptor chains and not the cell source, so whether cells came from the patient or from a donor has to be stated separately.
evidence.explanation: Native and added recognition require matched controls; one product does not establish every preparation uses both routes. points.requirement: Reaching and entering tumour tissue is a separate barrier from antigen recognition.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rise in engineered cells in blood with few found in two tumour biopsies leaves distribution and infiltration unresolved. Blood abundance is not entry into a mass of tissue, and a biopsy represents its sampled place and time. If a receptor works in a simple culture but killing falls in a more complex model with the target still present, investigate access, cell state and the model’s other features with controlled perturbations. The contrast alone does not identify a macrophage, vessel or signalling pathway as the cause, or show that more expansion will solve it. Expression of PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3 or TIGIT, or a count of macrophages or suppressor cells, does not by itself establish which input caused the functional difference. Trafficking toward a site and infiltration into tissue are different steps, and vessel number does not measure perfusion. Chronic stimulation, low oxygen, limited nutrients and inhibitory signals are different hypotheses; exhaustion describes cell states rather than physical tiredness.

points.requirement: RNA, DNA and an unspecified carrier cargo are not interchangeable labels; no integration or clinical effect is inferred from the schematic.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rise in engineered cells in blood with few found in two tumour biopsies leaves distribution and infiltration unresolved. Blood abundance is not entry into a mass of tissue, and a biopsy represents its sampled place and time. If a receptor works in a simple culture but killing falls in a more complex model with the target still present, investigate access, cell state and the model’s other features with controlled perturbations. The contrast alone does not identify a macrophage, vessel or signalling pathway as the cause, or show that more expansion will solve it. Expression of PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3 or TIGIT, or a count of macrophages or suppressor cells, does not by itself establish which input caused the functional difference. Trafficking toward a site and infiltration into tissue are different steps, and vessel number does not measure perfusion. Chronic stimulation, low oxygen, limited nutrients and inhibitory signals are different hypotheses; exhaustion describes cell states rather than physical tiredness.

points.requirement: An intended diagnostic use binds the assay, specimen, result rule and corresponding treatment/use.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: FDA describes companion diagnostics as devices that supply essential information for a corresponding treatment. Their roles can include identifying likely benefit, increased risk of serious adverse effects or a specified monitoring need. The treatment label and diagnostic labeling retain the relevant disease, specimen, biomarker and decision rule. Some devices have documented group labeling for specified oncology therapies. Similar analyte names do not establish assay interchangeability, and a label-matched result does not guarantee individual benefit or complete clinical suitability.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Three examples separate intended uses. Validated ER immunohistochemistry in invasive breast cancer, with appropriate tissue handling, tumour-nucleus scoring and controls, has a marker-specific pathology and endocrine-treatment assessment role; it does not validate a new RNA score as a substitute. In a wholly fictional second example, assay T version 1 detects alteration M in fixed tumour tissue under rule R, and Drug A requires exactly that result in setting S. The stipulated match supplies that requirement within the exercise, without promising benefit; another specimen, result type or setting needs evidence for the changed use. A third fictional score Q combines RNA, spatial neighbourhoods and a derived culture response to propose Drug A. Reproducibility and biological support can justify research, but do not establish that Q-guided care improves outcomes against an appropriate comparator. A laboratory certificate does not supply that missing evidence. Useful research and an established clinical use can appear on different parts of one report.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: G1 prepares the cell, S copies DNA, and G2 precedes the mitotic phase. Mitosis separates nuclear chromosomes; cytokinesis separates cytoplasm into daughter cells. G0 describes a noncycling state, which need not mean death or loss of function. Cyclins, CDKs and checkpoints regulate transitions, and their alteration can contribute to cancer without making every checkpoint absent or guaranteeing error-free division. Cell-cycle checkpoints and immune checkpoints describe different biological processes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional comparison, two populations start at 1,000 cells and are counted at the same later time. The untreated population reaches 2,000 and the treated one 1,200: their net increases are 1,000 and 200. The 800-cell endpoint difference does not mean that treatment killed 800 cells. Production and loss were not measured separately, so slower division, greater loss or both remain possible explanations. These are arithmetic premises, not a measured drug result or patient-benefit estimate.

A genetic clone has shared ancestry and can be tracked through specified genomic features; an RNA cluster alone does not establish that ancestry. Stem cells can renew and generate descendants; progenitor potential is restricted by the biological context. Differentiation develops specialized properties without requiring every change of state to become a new lineage.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A nucleus has an inner and an outer membrane, pores and DNA associated with proteins as chromatin. Rough endoplasmic reticulum forms a membrane network with a lumen; its membrane connects with the outer nuclear membrane. The Golgi consists of flattened membrane sacs, while a lysosome encloses material for breakdown. A mitochondrion has outer and inner membranes; folds of the inner membrane are cristae, and the matrix lies inside it. Its genome is distinct from nuclear chromatin. This general description is not an inventory of every human cell subtype, nor proof that DNA can never occur elsewhere.

points.requirement: The schematic follows G1, S, G2 and M, with an optional G0 state and conditional return.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: G1 prepares the cell, S copies DNA, and G2 precedes the mitotic phase. Mitosis separates nuclear chromosomes; cytokinesis separates cytoplasm into daughter cells. G0 describes a noncycling state, which need not mean death or loss of function. Cyclins, CDKs and checkpoints regulate transitions, and their alteration can contribute to cancer without making every checkpoint absent or guaranteeing error-free division. Cell-cycle checkpoints and immune checkpoints describe different biological processes.

points.requirement: Individual cell membranes and the extracellular basement membrane are different boundaries; the extracellular stroma is not drawn as naked free nuclei.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Epithelium forms linings, coverings and glands; an epithelial cell is not necessarily malignant. The relevant compartments depend on the tissue and disease.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Support a malignant-cell assignment with tissue context, a coherent marker panel, suitable normal references and quality checks, rather than one marker or cluster name. In five primary glioblastomas, Patel and colleagues profiled 430 cells and inferred broad chromosome alterations by averaging RNA expression along chromosomes against normal reference profiles. This was RNA-based inference, not a direct DNA copy count or a breast diagnostic rule. A flat inferred profile can miss a malignant cell lacking a detectable broad change; focal alterations and point mutations can also be missed. points.requirement: A chemical mark on otherwise identical DNA sequence differs from a base substitution; DNA methylation and histone modifications affect different substrates.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: DNA methylation changes a base’s chemical state without substituting the underlying sequence letter. Much human methylation analysis concerns 5-methylcytosine at CpG sites. Histone modifications affect DNA-associated proteins and are distinct from marks on DNA itself. Some regulatory states persist through division; epigenetic does not mean every mark is permanent or transmitted between generations. Promoter methylation can participate in reduced transcription, while patterns elsewhere need their own interpretation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In an invented sequence example, AACGT can carry a methyl group on its C while the underlying base order remains AACGT. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Consider an invented internal coding-DNA window, read from the 5-prime to the 3-prime end with the same left-hand frame: ATG GAA TCC GCT AAC GGT, 18 bases. Changing A to C at reference position 5 gives ATG GCA TCC GCT AAC GGT and preserves the grouping. Deleting positions 4 to 6, GAA, gives ATG TCC GCT AAC GGT, 15 bases. Deleting only G at position 4 instead gives ATG AAT CCG CTA ACG GT, 17 bases, with changed downstream grouping. The final GT is an incomplete part of a continuing window, not a stop codon. These predictions assume the specified coding transcript and unchanged splicing; neither RNA processing nor translation was measured.

Keep that biological comparison separate from an assay that chemically converts bases: standard bisulfite treatment can change the readout without establishing that the original DNA carried a C-to-T variant. Read the conversion chemistry, locus and cell context before interpreting a methylation call.
