evidence.supportingExcerpt: Immunity and capacity also limit what a lot can do. In a phase 1/2 study in seven people with severe haemophilia B, an AAV2 factor IX vector infused through the hepatic artery reached therapeutic levels at the highest dose but expression lasted about 8 weeks; the authors' further studies suggested that cell-mediated immunity against capsid antigens destroyed transduced hepatocytes (Manno and colleagues). Neutralising antibodies against the capsid are why re-dosing is hard: a review notes that systemic AAV dosing needs patient stratification by antibody level and that re-administration then becomes very difficult (Naso and colleagues), and a 2024 mouse study, which opens by noting that AAV typically induces long-lasting neutralising antibodies that prevent re-administration, found that transient B-cell depletion (anti-CD20 with anti-BAFF) before hepatic AAV8 delivery allowed effective re-administration (Rana and colleagues). evidence.supportingExcerpt: A typical RNA-delivery lipid nanoparticle combines an ionisable lipid, a phospholipid, cholesterol and a polyethylene glycol lipid around the RNA; the proportions, lipid identities and preparation change behaviour, so the label LNP alone does not name a product. points.requirement: Particle or fluorescent-lipid signal does not by itself establish intact RNA in the cytosol, encoded protein or useful function.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Where particles go depends on formulation and route. In female BALB/c mice given luciferase-mRNA LNPs by intramuscular, subcutaneous or intravenous injection, some intramuscular particles reached the liver and spleen, smaller particles more than larger ones, bigger particles tended to stay at the injection site, and liver expression was the most prominent; exposure and expression were not linearly related (Di and colleagues). Mouse distribution is not another product's distribution in people, and local injection does not establish local delivery. Readouts answer different questions: particle size, RNA integrity and encapsulated fraction describe the product; a labelled lipid or labelled RNA shows where a label went, not that intact RNA arrived or was released; and protein per identified live cell shows expression. In the mouse study a lipid label (DiR or deuterium-labelled cholesterol) and luciferase activity were measured separately and did not track each other linearly, and every figure needs its denominator (all cells, live cells or expressing cells). Uptake and protein are different fractions: in the six-formulation study the formulation with the highest eGFP expression had only moderate uptake, so a formulation that takes up in more cells can still make protein in fewer. Message and effect also run on separate clocks: in cultured mouse T cells CAR expression from LNP mRNA peaked at 24 hours and fell over the next days (Rurik and colleagues), and the same RNA in particles of different size or by a different route distributed differently, so the same RNA is not the same product.

points.requirement: Start context crosses the untranslated/coding boundary; it is not an extra inserted segment or a DNA transcription promoter. Untranslated regions can affect use of the message.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Start-codon context was tested by single-base substitutions around the AUG initiator in a cloned preproinsulin gene, where the best sequence identified changed proinsulin yield over a 20-fold range (Kozak). The interaction of the cap and the poly(A) tail was tested with luciferase mRNAs delivered by electroporation into tobacco protoplasts, Chinese hamster ovary cells and yeast, where the tail's effect depended on the cap (Gallie). A textbook describes the 5' cap, 5' and 3' untranslated regions that regulate translation initiation and mRNA stability, a poly-A tail of about 200 A residues added by poly-A polymerase to cellular mRNA, and a ribosome that moves from the cap to the AUG, with Kozak's rules describing the sequence around it (OpenStax Biology 2e). The cellular tail length is not a rule for engineered constructs: one dendritic-cell study found that a 120-nucleotide tail, an unmasked tail end and two 3' untranslated regions each improved stability and translation, and it measured transcript amount by RT-PCR, protein by eGFP, peptide-MHC density and T-cell stimulation separately (Holtkamp and colleagues), so a doubled reporter signal after a 3' change is one measurement, not a different antigen or a clinical benefit. These are tested constructs and cell systems, not one best sequence for a clinical product.

points.requirement: A pairing-antibody assay detects structures within its characterised length/chemistry/matrix scope; a lower or undetected signal proves neither zero impurity nor all product-quality attributes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: One documented origin is T7 polymerase initiating transcription from a promoter-less DNA end, producing an antisense strand and long double-stranded RNA that activated the sensor MDA5 (Mu and colleagues). In purification studies, unmodified mRNAs were translated better after HPLC purification but still induced high levels of cytokine secretion (Karikó and colleagues). A cellulose method removed at least 90 per cent of double-stranded RNA with over 65 per cent recovery regardless of mRNA length, coding sequence or nucleoside composition and increased translation in mice, and agarose gels showed that the purified mRNA stayed intact, but it removed duplexes of 30 base pairs or longer efficiently while most of a 21 base-pair duplex remained (Baiersdörfer and colleagues). Detection has its own scope: that paper notes an earlier report that about 40 base pairs of duplex are needed for detection by the J2 antibody, and a review of mRNA analytics lists immunoblot or ELISA for double-stranded RNA alongside separate integrity assays (Losada and colleagues). A lower dsRNA signal with worse fragmentation or recovery therefore does not show a better product. Method performance in those systems is not a clinical impurity limit.

evidence.explanation: Semantic comparison at stated source or fictional-premise scope; hash and containment checks are separate from entailment.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The limit of blank describes an upper background response at a specified probability. A limit of detection concerns an amount that can be detected under stated false-call and detection-probability conditions; LoD95 specifies 95 per cent detection in the tested workflow. It is not a line above which every repeat must be positive, nor 95 per cent certainty that a person has disease. A limit of quantitation requires stated quantitative accuracy, including bias and imprecision goals. The limits answer different questions and have no universal spacing; they may coincide under a particular method and its criteria.

A predictive biomarker concerns the effect of a named treatment relative to a comparator: compare those treatment effects across marker groups, with an explicit effect scale and uncertainty. A marker can serve both roles. Prespecified groups and randomized treatment assignment support this comparison, although the actual design, missing specimens and applicability still matter. Keep the assay, specimen timing, population, care, endpoint and horizon with either claim.

points.requirement: LoB concerns the background-response distribution at a specified probability, not itself a reliably detected amount; repeated representative blanks and conditions matter.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The limit of blank describes an upper background response at a specified probability. A limit of detection concerns an amount that can be detected under stated false-call and detection-probability conditions; LoD95 specifies 95 per cent detection in the tested workflow. It is not a line above which every repeat must be positive, nor 95 per cent certainty that a person has disease. A limit of quantitation requires stated quantitative accuracy, including bias and imprecision goals. The limits answer different questions and have no universal spacing; they may coincide under a particular method and its criteria.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Evaluate repeated blanks and low-level specimens across the conditions the claim covers. Each finite set of repeats needs representative clinical specimens or suitably equivalent reference inputs. Record the analyte, amount or concentration units, specimen matrix, input, workflow boundary, assay version and acceptable false-positive, false-negative and quantitative-error rates. Matrix means the material surrounding the analyte; reference material with a known added analyte amount needs justified equivalence to the clinical specimen. A limit measured on purified material is not automatically a collection-to-report limit. Contamination, nonspecific signal, calibration bias, poor recovery, unrepresentative targets, different lots or operators and inadequate input can change performance. Calibration-slope sensitivity, analytical detection capability and clinical sensitivity are different uses of the same word.

points.requirement: Nonsignificance does not establish no effect. A wide interval can leave important benefit and harm unresolved; the later-only event-information/power clause stays distinct from the original version.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Read the effect estimate and confidence interval together. Too few events can leave a study with low power and an interval compatible with meaningful benefit and harm. Precision concerns sampling uncertainty under the analysis; it does not remove bias. Evidence excluding a large effect need not exclude a smaller one, and an unresolved effect is neither evidence of benefit nor proof of exactly zero effect. Equivalence testing asks whether an effect lies within justified lower and upper bounds, preferably specified before seeing results, using an appropriate analysis. Non-inferiority instead asks whether a treatment is worse than its comparator by more than a prespecified margin. Neither question is settled by failing to reject a zero difference, and meaningful margins depend on the outcome and setting.

points.requirement: Frequentist confidence level concerns repeated valid method coverage under assumptions; the normal construction is approximate, and an observed interval is not a posterior probability or a range containing 95 percent of patients.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A frequentist confidence interval describes estimation precision using a procedure with a stated coverage rate under its assumptions. Across repeated valid applications, a 95% procedure would include the fixed true parameter in 95% of its intervals. This does not assign a 95% probability to that parameter being inside one interval after it has been calculated, or describe a range containing 95% of patients. The result depends on the data structure, estimator, confidence level, model and calculation method, including adjustment, missing-data handling and multiplicity. More observations often improve precision but do not remove biased measurement, confounding or a wrong model.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: For a fictional binary outcome in 50 of 100 independent people, the normal-approximation standard error is sqrt(0.50 × 0.50/100) = 0.05. The approximate 95% interval is 0.50 ± 1.96 × 0.05, or 40.2% to 59.8%. With 5,000 of 10,000 people, the proportion stays 50% but the standard error becomes 0.005 and the interval 49.02% to 50.98%. Small counts, proportions near zero or one, clustering and incomplete outcomes may require other methods. A hand-picked set of ten such intervals, nine containing a fixed 50% truth and one missing it, illustrates coverage but does not measure a procedure's coverage rate. A 95% method need not cover in exactly 95% of a small set. Narrower bounds indicate greater sampling precision, not less bias.

points.requirement: A hazard is an instantaneous event rate conditional on remaining at risk for a specified endpoint, with comparator direction and rate units stated.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A hazard is an instantaneous event rate among people still at risk, rather than the fraction of everyone enrolled who has had an event by a date. A hazard ratio divides one group's hazard by its reference group's hazard for a defined endpoint. It does not mean 30 percentage points fewer events, 30% longer survival or a 30% reduction in each person's probability. Reversing the comparison gives 1/0.70, about 1.43. Zero counts can make a raw odds ratio zero, infinite or undefined; estimation method and uncertainty matter. Reversing the comparison takes the reciprocal. For another fictional example, 20 adverse events among 100 people versus 10 among 100 gives a risk ratio of 2 but an odds ratio of (20/80)/(10/90) = 2.25. A response odds ratio is also different from a survival hazard ratio. An assay-based association with response does not quantify the benefit of acting on a biomarker; its model, endpoint and treatment comparison need their own evidence. All counts here are invented.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: An odds ratio divides the odds of an event in one group by the odds in a reference group. Its interpretation depends on outcome coding, the comparison, follow-up and model adjustment; a case-control sample does not reveal population prevalence from its case fraction.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Probability counts events among everyone; odds count events relative to non-events. points.requirement: A p-value conditions on the null and other analysis assumptions; it is not the probability the null is true, an individual finding is false, or a clinically important benefit exists.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A p-value is calculated for a specified null hypothesis and analysis. Assuming that null model and the other analysis assumptions are true, it is the probability of a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed. A small value indicates poor fit to that model; it is not the probability that the hypothesis is true, that the result occurred “by chance”, or that the selected finding is false. In particular, p = 0.03 does not mean a 97% probability of benefit. Omics analyses may test thousands of genes or pathways, and reporting only the most striking result hides the search. A selected small value can generate a hypothesis without establishing a drug dependency or clinical benefit. Error control cannot repair biased measurement or an irrelevant comparison, and prespecification reduces analytical flexibility without guaranteeing a sound design.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A surrogate is a measured outcome used in place of a direct clinical-benefit outcome, with evidence needed for that substitution in the intended setting. Two relationships must be separated: people with a favourable marker may have better outcomes, while treatments that improve that marker may or may not improve the outcome. The first is a prognostic association; the second concerns agreement between treatment effects across suitable randomised comparisons. A treatment can change another pathway, later disease or toxicity as well as the marker. Validation is specific to disease, treatment context and intended outcome. An early measure is not automatically validated, and regulatory acceptance in one programme does not transfer to another. “Validated” and “reasonably likely to predict benefit” carry different evidence claims. Even a pathology or imaging response does not capture every benefit and harm.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A confidence interval for the mean effect differs from a prediction interval for an underlying effect in another comparable study under the model. Neither is a personal prognosis interval. I-squared estimates the proportion of variability in study estimates associated with heterogeneity rather than sampling error; it is neither the percentage of people helped nor the percentage of studies that are wrong. Tau-squared is between-study effect variance on the chosen scale, such as squared score points or squared log risk ratios. These estimates can be uncertain, especially with few studies, and no I-squared cutoff alone makes pooling safe.

points.requirement: Vehicle and untreated controls ask different questions when the carrier or solvent can affect the assay.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. Slower growth, death and a molecular change require their own readouts; direct death or recovery measurements could address further questions. points.requirement: I-squared describes estimated heterogeneity relative to sampling variation, not people helped or studies wrong. Tau-squared is a between-study variance on the named effect scale; both estimates can be uncertain with few studies.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A confidence interval for the mean effect differs from a prediction interval for an underlying effect in another comparable study under the model. Neither is a personal prognosis interval. I-squared estimates the proportion of variability in study estimates associated with heterogeneity rather than sampling error; it is neither the percentage of people helped nor the percentage of studies that are wrong. Tau-squared is between-study effect variance on the chosen scale, such as squared score points or squared log risk ratios. These estimates can be uncertain, especially with few studies, and no I-squared cutoff alone makes pooling safe.

points.requirement: Keep the separate five-study day-30, 0-to-100 symptom-score example, A minus control: estimates -8,-6,-4,-2,0 with standard error 2 each, Q10, df4, DL tau-squared6 and I-squared60%.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional forest example: five studies compare treatment A minus control on the same 0 to 100 symptom scale at day 30. Their effects are -8, -6, -4, -2 and 0 points, each with standard error 2 and weight 20 per cent, so the square areas are equal. The mean is -4.0 points. With a classical moment variance estimate, Q = 10, I-squared = 60 per cent and tau-squared = 6 squared score points. A normal 95 per cent mean interval is about -6.8 to -1.2; the stated 2009 prediction method, using a t distribution with three degrees of freedom, gives about -13.0 to +5.0. The study intervals, mean diamond and wider prediction interval answer different questions. Five studies are few and these intervals are approximate; a negative mean does not imply a negative effect in every setting.

A post-hoc analysis can generate useful hypotheses, but choosing a favourable result and then calling it prespecified or independently validated does not provide confirmation.

points.requirement: Phases 1 to 4 describe development purposes, with overlap and actual protocol context. They are not a benefit ladder, fixed sample-size rule, guarantee of safety, efficacy or approval for every investigated use.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Clinical-trial phases describe development purposes rather than a fixed sample size, assignment method or promise of benefit. Phase 1 studies administration, exposure, safety and dosage, sometimes with early activity measures. Phase 2 asks whether activity and safety support further study in a specified population. Phase 3 compares with a defined alternative and can provide evidence for an approval decision; a phase 3 label is not itself approval. FDA's patient overview illustrates phase 3 with hundreds to thousands of participants, while the actual size follows the protocol's question and information requirements. Phase 4 studies an approved treatment in broader use. Read the protocol because phases can overlap or be combined.

A single-arm study has one intervention group; identify its actual external comparison, if any, and endpoint.

points.requirement: Chance assignment can reduce selection choices and help balance measured or unmeasured factors but can leave imbalances. Random assignment differs from random population sampling and does not guarantee transportability.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A randomized trial assigns eligible consenting participants to interventions by chance. Concealing the next assignment protects enrolment against foreknowledge; blinding concerns awareness after assignment. These are different design features. Randomization reduces treatment-selection confounding but leaves possible chance imbalance, missing outcomes and limits on applicability. The comparator, endpoint, analysis and conduct determine what the comparison establishes.

points.requirement: Separate the biological unit of inference, independently assigned experimental unit and measured observational unit; treating correlated subsamples as independent is pseudoreplication.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Name the intervention, control, outcome and units before counting replication. The biological unit is the entity about which conclusions are sought, such as a donor. The experimental unit receives an independently assigned intervention; the observational unit is measured. A cage assigned together or a preparation treated before being split can make the animals or wells subsamples. More measured cells do not become more assigned mice. Biological and technical replicate labels vary, so inspect sampling, preparation, allocation and measurement. Repeating runs tests consistency without adding donor identities. Analysing correlated subsamples as independent replicates is pseudoreplication.

evidence.explanation: Semantic comparison at stated source or fictional-premise scope; hash and containment checks are separate from entailment. Rebound to the expanded current root field with all three earlier notes preserved byte-exactly. No earlier scientific or visual acceptance is upgraded.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Separate the index-test result from a defined reference condition. Sensitivity is TP/(TP+FN), the positive fraction among reference cases; specificity is TN/(TN+FP), the negative fraction among reference non-cases. PPV is TP/(TP+FP), the reference-case fraction among positive calls; NPV is TN/(TN+FN), the reference-noncase fraction among negative calls. Base rate means prevalence of that reference condition in the intended tested population. Regrouping the same people by positive calls changes a denominator without adding participants.

At 10 per cent prevalence there are TP 80, FN 20, FP 90 and TN 810: PPV is 80/170, about 47.1 per cent, and NPV 810/830, about 97.6 per cent. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Separate the index-test result from a defined reference condition. Sensitivity is TP/(TP+FN), the positive fraction among reference cases; specificity is TN/(TN+FP), the negative fraction among reference non-cases. PPV is TP/(TP+FP), the reference-case fraction among positive calls; NPV is TN/(TN+FN), the reference-noncase fraction among negative calls. Base rate means prevalence of that reference condition in the intended tested population. Regrouping the same people by positive calls changes a denominator without adding participants.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Antigen-processing machinery (APM) is the set of proteins that generate, transport and load peptides onto HLA. A common class I route has five steps. (1) The proteasome cuts intracellular proteins into fragments, which can create a useful peptide or destroy it. (2) The transporter associated with antigen processing, TAP1 with TAP2, moves peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum; Shepherd et al. (1993) showed in a cell-free system that TAP1 is part of an ATP-dependent, sequence-selective peptide translocator. (3) ERAP1 and ERAP2 trim amino acids from the front end. York et al. (2002) found that ERAP1 can enhance or limit presentation by trimming epitopes to 8 to 9 residues, and Saveanu et al. (2005) found complementary human ERAP1 and ERAP2 activity, so more expression does not universally improve display. A class I HLA heavy chain assembles with beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a peptide, with helpers such as tapasin. (4) Stable peptide-HLA complexes reach the surface; the peptide stays held by HLA. (5) A compatible T-cell receptor on a conventional CD8 T cell may recognise the pair; recognition is a separate gate and display alone does not show killing.

Class II HLA commonly loads peptides in vesicles that process acquired proteins. An invariant chain protects the new groove and directs it there; after cutting, a remaining fragment is exchanged for other peptides with help from HLA-DM, and conventional CD4 T cells inspect these displays. Cross-presentation lets externally acquired material reach class I. The scheme is a common route, not a rule for every peptide.

A cancer cell may keep an altered protein and still show little of its peptide, and a shared processing defect can affect several targets at once, so adding candidate peptides does not bypass the bottleneck. Low expression, gene loss and a functional defect are different findings: a weak RNA signal does not prove deletion. Interferon gamma can increase presentation machinery when its signalling pathway and the required genes are intact, and cannot replace a deleted B2M or HLA gene. Sucker et al. (2017) described melanoma lesions in which JAK1 or JAK2 defects gave interferon-gamma resistance and evolved into HLA class I negative, T-cell-resistant lesions with antigen-presentation genes silenced and no longer inducible. Zaretsky et al. (2016) found, in biopsies from patients with acquired resistance to PD-1 blockade, JAK1 or JAK2 loss of function in two of four patients and a truncating B2M mutation with lost surface class I in a third. These are melanoma observations, not treatment-benefit evidence.

Evidence layers differ. DNA sequence and copy number show gene retention or alteration but not expression or function; RNA shows sampled gene activity but not protein, assembly or display; protein staining or flow cytometry detects protein but not which peptide is shown; HLA-associated peptide recovery shows a peptide was recovered with HLA in that preparation but not its cell of origin or recognition; controlled T-cell recognition shows function against tested targets. Peptide loading can bypass processing, so rescue by supplied peptide supports a bottleneck under those conditions only. Binding prediction is not presentation, and CD4 help is not proof of CD8 tumour recognition.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. CDR3 is an informative variable region, but neither a beta-chain sequence nor CDR3 alone specifies the complete paired receptor or its function.

Particular receptors can cross-react across peptide and HLA contexts; that does not establish a universal cross-reactivity rate. Paired receptor identity, binding, activation, target-cell death and clinical benefit require different evidence. A response by one reconstructed pair to peptide-loaded cells does not establish that another alpha-chain pairing recognises the same target, or that either kills naturally presenting tumour cells. Use irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls. Peptide loading can bypass natural processing, and contact diagrams are not healthy-tissue safety tests.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Interpret30CD8/100lymphocytes as30% of counted lymphocytes; neither denominator is all tumor cells or tumor specificity.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional section, 0.4 square millimetres of mononuclear infiltrate within 2 square millimetres of eligible stroma gives 20% by area. Separately, 30 CD8 cells among 100 counted lymphocytes gives 30% of those counted lymphocytes. Neither is the fraction of all tumour cells, a measure of cancer specificity or evidence of useful killing. One occupied unit among five equal eligible stromal-area units also gives 20%; the drawing illustrates a denominator rather than prescribing pixel counting for semiquantitative breast scoring.

points.requirement: Explain IFNg-receptor/JAK1/JAK2/STAT response and distinguish inducibility from baseline display.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Explain IFNg-receptor/JAK1/JAK2/STAT response and distinguish inducibility from baseline display.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: In Zaretsky’s selected four-person melanoma relapse series, two cases had JAK1 or JAK2 loss-of-function changes with loss of the normal allele and another had a truncating B2M change. The JAK2-deficient relapse cells failed to increase interferon-gamma signalling, PD-L1 and class I while retaining interferon-alfa/beta responsiveness. Engineered JAK1- or JAK2-deficient melanoma cells were still recognized by the tested NY-ESO-1-specific T cells. Baseline display, inducibility, recognition and killing are separate dependencies; neither a JAK variant nor detectable HLA alone answers all of them.

points.requirement: Define inflamed, excluded and desert from specified immune-cell locations; state the inconsistent desert-or-excluded use of cold.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Define inflamed, excluded and desert from specified immune-cell locations; state the inconsistent desert-or-excluded use of cold.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: An inflamed or hot pattern has specified immune cells within sampled tumour regions. In an excluded pattern, cells concentrate in surrounding stroma or at a boundary with less entry into malignant nests. A desert has few relevant cells in the examined regions. Cold is used for desert alone or for both desert and excluded patterns, so state the definition. A macrophage-rich sample is not automatically T-cell inflamed.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Measure local shrinkage, antigen-reactive immunity, distant response and long-term clinical benefit separately.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Intratumoral immunotherapy describes a delivery route and treatment purpose; in-situ vaccination describes a proposed learning strategy. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Added peptide can bypass natural processing. evidence.supportingExcerpt: The room-echo analogy explains the observation: a beam travels into tissue and returns from boundaries. A selected image plane is neither a histological section nor a survey of the whole body. Grayscale images primarily describe echo patterns; Doppler uses frequency changes from movement to describe blood-flow direction or speed. Its displayed colours depend on the mode and settings, rather than staining malignant cells. Flow is not itself proof of malignant activity.

points.requirement: A shared beta chain can hide different alpha chains (figure, common confusions)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: A shared beta chain can hide different alpha chains (figure, common confusions) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Beta match, alpha hidden, fictional: three cells carry beta chains B, B and C, so a bulk beta-chain view lists B, B, C and loses the alpha chains. The paired view keeps alpha X with beta B, alpha Y with beta B and alpha Z with beta C, so the shared beta B does not make alpha X and alpha Y equal. Single-cell methods that sequence the alpha and beta genes of individual T cells retain each pair and can be combined with function-related gene expression, and the same TCR sequence can sit in functionally different cells (Han 2014). A bulk method profiles a mixed sample, often one chain, whereas TIRTL-seq generates paired alpha and beta repertoire data at cohort scale and is distinguished from bulk single-chain data and from single-cell throughput limits (Pogorelyy 2026). Paired identity plus an expression program is more context and is still not evidence of the receptor's antigen.

points.requirement: Density separation, interface, incomplete recovery and contamination; PBMC label is not purity (figure)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Density separation, interface, incomplete recovery and contamination; PBMC label is not purity (figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: What the fraction is: peripheral blood mononuclear cells are circulating white blood cells with a single unsegmented nucleus, mainly lymphocytes and monocytes, with T, B and natural killer cells among them, isolated by layering anticoagulated blood over a density-separation medium and collecting the interface. Most conventional granulocytes and red cells separate elsewhere, but recovery is incomplete, so platelets, red cells or low-density granulocytes can contaminate a preparation, and the label PBMC does not guarantee purity. The classic density-gradient method dates from 1968 (Boyum 1968). Isolation selects a recoverable blood fraction and does not sample tumour or give a complete immune census.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Density separation, interface, incomplete recovery and contamination; PBMC label is not purity (figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The usable input for a downstream assay is the recovered viable cell preparation, not simply the volume of blood drawn. Fresh isolation, freezing, thawing, washing and any rest period define a sequence of selections, so record recovery, population composition and purity as well as viability. The Cytiva density-separation handbook describes the mononuclear interface, platelet carryover and possible immature-granulocyte contamination in pathological blood. That manufacturer method source does not validate every cancer assay, and an inadequate number of the relevant cells can make a rare-response experiment uninformative.

points.requirement: Multivalent avidity on a labelled scaffold (figure); tetramer as one format

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Multivalent avidity on a labelled scaffold (figure); tetramer as one format Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: What the evidence shows: in the original report, tetramers of HLA-A2 with two HIV-derived peptides or an influenza A matrix peptide bound peptide-specific cytotoxic T cells in vitro and T cells from the blood of HIV-infected people, and binding in general correlated well with cytotoxicity assays (Altman 1996). That is a correlation in those systems and not a rule that binding equals killing for an arbitrary tumour peptide. Tetramers are made by mixing biotinylated MHC with fluorescent streptavidin, and a later method made them with small-molecule fluorophores (Ramachandiran 2007), so reagent preparation is a source of variation. An observed stain shows binding under the tested conditions and does not show natural processing and display of that pair by a tumour.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Multivalent avidity on a labelled scaffold (figure); tetramer as one format Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Avidity describes the combined strength of multiple contacts. Multimerising peptide-HLA ligands can make binding detectable when an individual receptor-ligand contact is weak; the 2021 guidelines also caution that more multimerisation does not always improve detection. The measured output is a gate-defined binding fraction or, with a suitable counting method, a count. Reagent, viability and background controls support that binding measurement, which still requires separate validation before use for treatment selection.

points.requirement: Stimulus types, transport inhibition window, fixation and permeabilisation, viability stain before fixation (Mermaid, figure)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Stimulus types, transport inhibition window, fixation and permeabilisation, viability stain before fixation (Mermaid, figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: cytokines retained inside cells during a defined assay, so a response can be assigned to stained cell populations. How: cells get a defined stimulus, a protein-transport inhibitor is present for a stated window so newly made cytokines accumulate, the cells are fixed and made permeable, and flow cytometry reads cytokine stains beside population markers, with a viability stain applied before fixation. Input: viable blood or tissue cells, with separate aliquots per stimulus, and fixed cells cannot go on to living-cell assays. Output: percent cytokine-positive cells within a named parent population, or percent with stated cytokine combinations. Controls: unstimulated or vehicle, a positive stimulation, viability and recovery, single-stain and staining-boundary controls. It cannot tell natural tumour presentation, direct target-cell killing, receptor sequence identity or clinical benefit.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Stimulus types, transport inhibition window, fixation and permeabilisation, viability stain before fixation (Mermaid, figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The stimulus changes the question. Added peptide can bypass some processing steps; whole protein needs suitable antigen-presenting cells and processing, while broad stimulation tests responsiveness without identifying the intended antigen. The 2021 flow-cytometry guidelines describe brefeldin A and monensin as transport inhibitors and explain that their choice and exposure window can affect what is measured. Intracellular accumulation after inhibition is not a measurement of how much cytokine reached the surrounding medium.

points.requirement: Relative enrichment versus absolute expansion: 30 of 100 to 30 of 50 (figure); richness is not evenness; a shared sequence is not proven cancer specificity; one number is not the whole repertoire

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Relative enrichment versus absolute expansion: 30 of 100 to 30 of 50 (figure); richness is not evenness; a shared sequence is not proven cancer specificity; one number is not the whole repertoire Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Share against count, fictional: clonotype A is 30 of 100 measured molecules, 30%, and later 30 of 50, 60%. Its measured count did not rise, the total fell, and its relative frequency doubled, so relative enrichment is not absolute expansion and the molecule counts are not blood cell counts. In a published analysis pipeline, clonality was identified as a robust key metric and first choice for measuring TCR repertoire diversity, and in prostate cancer patients given sipuleucel-T the pipeline detected changes in sequence frequency and diversity in blood and prostate tissue (Zhang 2017); that is a methods and example study and sets no response threshold. A diversity-analysis software suite reports repertoire comparison and diversity outputs (Shugay 2015), and formulas, software settings and subsampling depth have to be stated.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Relative enrichment versus absolute expansion: 30 of 100 to 30 of 50 (figure); richness is not evenness; a shared sequence is not proven cancer specificity; one number is not the whole repertoire Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Frequency arithmetic, fictional: clonotype A is 10 of 10,000 sampled receptor units at baseline (0.1%) and 20 of 1,000 later (2%). The measured relative frequency rose twentyfold, but these are sampled receptor units and not a census of cells, and other populations contracting, different sampling and method effects can change frequency. Read counts are not always cell counts, because preparation, amplification and transcript abundance can change them, and absolute expansion needs compatible cell-number evidence. A sequence overlap between blood and tumour is detected overlap under a clonotype definition and is not a target, and antigen specificity needs a matching controlled recognition experiment.

points.requirement: Compare four equal versus four uneven clonotypes and a separate two-equal-clonotype sample to distinguish richness from evenness; the counts are fictional measured molecules, not body-wide cells.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Compare four equal versus four uneven clonotypes and a separate two-equal-clonotype sample to distinguish richness from evenness; the counts are fictional measured molecules, not body-wide cells. Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Metrics and arithmetic, fictional: with natural logarithms Shannon entropy is H = minus the sum of p times ln p, and one normalised clonality convention is 1 minus H / ln K for K observed clonotypes greater than one. Four clonotypes at 25, 25, 25 and 25 of 100 measured molecules give H = ln 4 = 1.386 and clonality 0. The same four at 70, 10, 10 and 10 give H = 0.940, clonality 1 minus 0.940 / 1.386 = 0.32, and an effective number of clonotypes exp(H) = 2.56. Richness is four in both, so many identities can coexist with strong dominance. Software may report Shannon entropy, its exponential or a normalised score, and these are not interchangeable: in the VDJtools documentation the Shannon-Wiener index returns the exponent of the entropy and the normalised index returns the entropy divided by the log of the clonotype count, which is evenness and not 1 minus that ratio, so a clonality built as 1 minus normalised entropy is a different number from either.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Compare four equal versus four uneven clonotypes and a separate two-equal-clonotype sample to distinguish richness from evenness; the counts are fictional measured molecules, not body-wide cells. Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Effective-diversity measures weight a distribution differently. For the inverse-Simpson convention, define D as the sum of squared clonotype fractions and report 1 / D: four equal fractions of 0.25 give 4, whereas 0.70, 0.10, 0.10 and 0.10 give 1 / 0.52, about 1.92. This differs from the Shannon effective diversity of about 2.56 for the same uneven distribution. A fictional sample containing only A and B at 50 molecules each has richness 2 and equal weights; low richness does not imply unequal weights.

points.requirement: SFU per million arithmetic: (30 minus 5) x 10 = 250; not a cutoff or a subset frequency (figure)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: SFU per million arithmetic: (30 minus 5) x 10 = 250; not a cutoff or a subset frequency (figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional arithmetic: wells with 100,000 input cells give 30 spots after peptide stimulation and 5 spots with vehicle. Background-subtracted, that is 30 minus 5 = 25 spots per 100,000 cells, or 250 spot-forming units per million input cells. This is an arithmetic summary and not a positivity cut-off, replicates, positive controls and a prespecified response rule still apply, and in mixed PBMCs it is not the frequency of a particular T-cell subset. If the cells came from an expanded culture, the number describes the cultured cells and not the responding fraction of the original blood draw.

points.requirement: Background arithmetic: 40% raw death minus 30% target-only = 10 percentage points excess (figure)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Background arithmetic: 40% raw death minus 30% target-only = 10 percentage points excess (figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Background arithmetic, fictional: matched wells of 100 identifiable targets show 30% death without effectors and 40% with them at the same 2-hour endpoint. Raw death is 40%, but 30% occurs without effectors, so the excess is 40 minus 30 = 10 percentage points. That excess is associated with the tested condition and does not identify which deaths the effectors caused, and calling the result 40% immune killing is not justified. A control-normalised specific-lysis formula gives a different quantity from an excess-death calculation, so the method has to be named, and a high baseline death can make the experiment unsuitable.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Following a blood test from body to result separates biological availability, inclusion in the evaluated aliquot, recovery through processing, and the final calling rule. Low shedding, handling losses, background or a failed quality criterion can interrupt different steps. Repeated draws observe different times, but tumour biology and handling can make their errors correlated; they are not automatically independent repeats. points.requirement: Figure and Mermaid: marker selection, recovered versus unselected cells and free DNA; blood volume to validated interpretation

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Figure and Mermaid: marker selection, recovered versus unselected cells and free DNA; blood volume to validated interpretation Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: A count is a recovery under rules: enrichment concentrates candidate cells before identification, and each method selects. One established epithelial method captures with EpCAM, then checks cell shape, a nucleus, cytokeratin and absence of CD45, which is one operational definition and not a universal rule for all circulating tumour cells or tumour types. Physical methods select by size or deformability and remove or retain different cells, so marker independence is not unbiased recovery. A negative capture, such as zero qualifying cells in 7.5 mL, does not show that no tumour cells circulate and does not predict a ctDNA result, because free DNA fragments are a separate analyte.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Figure and Mermaid: marker selection, recovered versus unselected cells and free DNA; blood volume to validated interpretation Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: A recovered candidate cell needs identification under the assay rules before it becomes a reported count. Record the blood volume, collection time relative to treatment, processing time, tube and transport conditions, recovery and staining controls, and how ambiguous images or failed preparations were handled. As a reading rule, a cell counted after fixation is not thereby shown to be alive or capable of forming a metastasis. Protein staining, RNA or DNA analysis, and culture are separate downstream measurements with their own material requirements; a count does not automatically supply a genome, a viable culture, the lesion that shed the cell or evidence that changing treatment helps.

points.requirement: Measured features then reference and model then source estimate; inference is not a cell census (figure and Mermaid)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Measured features then reference and model then source estimate; inference is not a cell census (figure and Mermaid) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Measure, then infer: the measured features are fragment length, end sequences, genomic positions and chemical marks. A reference or trained model then turns them into a source estimate or a score, so the output is an inference and not a cell census, and no single fragment carries a cancer address. Tumour fragments are shorter on average, but most short fragments in a sample still come from normal cells because normal DNA outnumbers tumour DNA when the tumour fraction is low. These features can complement mutation tracking when few informative mutations are sampled, and neither a source estimate nor a score by itself establishes tumour location, stage, a resistance mechanism or benefit from acting on a result.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Measured features then reference and model then source estimate; inference is not a cell census (figure and Mermaid) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: DNA extraction and analysis use a finite plasma aliquot, and the amount recovered differs from the amount drawn. A predefined detector need not build a patient-specific tumour reference, but the actual method's tissue and input requirements still need checking. Collection-to-separation time, storage and timing relative to treatment belong with the specimen. Validation has to follow the measured feature: retain collection and processing dates, reference mixtures and process controls, batch checks, and the population, assay version and cut-off used to develop and evaluate the model. A satisfactory DNA yield or size distribution does not validate fragment-end patterns. Analytical reproducibility of a feature is separate from cancer detection, prognosis and benefit from acting on the score.

As a model-reading rule, a source absent from the reference set cannot be assumed absent from the specimen: the model may leave it unresolved or attribute it imperfectly to represented sources. Keep the methylated-site fraction, estimated source fraction and classifier score distinct. Known-source mixtures, process and batch controls, and evaluation in the intended specimen and population test different parts of that inference.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Attribution rule: matched white-blood-cell sequencing is the standard comparison, but its gene coverage, depth and detection rules matter, a clone below its sensitivity can stay unseen, and subtracting every blood match is not a complete method because a variant can be present in blood and tumour. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional sTIL estimate of 30% means that the defined mononuclear infiltrate occupies about 30% of eligible stromal area. Additional stains change the measurement rather than silently changing its denominator.

points.requirement: Top panel ten numbered tumours with A/AB/B/none badges; lower panel HSA 30%, Bliss 44%, observed 40% at one dose pair (A 20%, B 30%), 72 h, vehicle-normalised viable-cell endpoint, no uncertainty/test; Loewe needs dose-response curves.

evidence.explanation: The responder union is 6 of 10; the separate 72-hour viable-count example exceeds HSA but not Bliss and supplies no uncertainty or Loewe curves.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The two fictional comparisons use different units of inference. In a ten-tumour better-component model, A covers tumours 1 to 4 and B covers 3 to 6: 4 + 4 - 2 = 6 in the union, with four in neither group. There is no extra within-tumour interaction or added toxicity in that counting model. Separately, one cultured-cell experiment at 72 hours gives 20%, 30% and 40% inhibition for A, B and the pair at one fixed dose pair. Inhibition here is a reduction in vehicle-normalised viable-cell count, not a direct death measurement. HSA expects 30% and Bliss 44%, so 40% exceeds the first and falls below the second. points.requirement: Four panels: purified binding, engagement in relevant cell, effect measurement, benefit and harm evidence; reaching the compartment alone is insufficient; molecular shapes schematic.

evidence.explanation: Purified binding, relevant-system engagement, functional effects and clinical outcomes form separate evidence layers.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Target engagement and the evidence ladder. Target engagement asks whether a compound interacts with its intended target in the relevant system. Binding to a purified protein does not show that the compound enters the cell or reaches its target in a tumour, and engagement is also not a change in the target's function, a downstream effect or clinical benefit. Each question needs its own measurement: engagement first, then a measured biological effect, then a check of the causal explanation with controls, then clinical evidence.

evidence.explanation: Purified binding, relevant-system engagement, functional effects and clinical outcomes form separate evidence layers.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading a thermal-shift result. The cellular thermal shift assay was introduced to evaluate drug binding to target proteins in cells and tissue samples through ligand-induced thermal stabilisation (Martinez Molina et al. 2013). The readout is the soluble target signal remaining after heating, plotted either against temperature at a fixed compound concentration or against concentration at a fixed temperature, so degrees Celsius and concentration units sit on different axes and the two designs ask different bounded questions. A shift of the compound curve against a matched control supports engagement under those conditions; indirect stability or protein-complex effects can also change the signal, so it is not an inhibition or occupancy percentage, and no universal shift cut-off is given here. The heated aliquots are consumed, so a record should carry the compound, concentration, exposure time, temperature series, cell or tissue system and controls. In an isothermal-shift study with a pan-kinase inhibitor, a large share of non-kinase proteins shifted in cells, which the authors read as in-cell profiling being more likely than lysate profiling to identify indirect binding targets; they recommend lysate profiling to identify targets and in-cell profiling to verify intracellular engagement (Ball et al. 2020).

evidence.explanation: Purified binding, relevant-system engagement, functional effects and clinical outcomes form separate evidence layers.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The last step is clinical. Mechanistic plausibility does not show benefit, because the target may also be present in healthy tissue and the useful margin depends on achieved benefit and harm in a stated disease, treatment setting, product and outcome. The National Cancer Institute adds that cancer cells can become resistant to targeted therapy when the target itself changes so the drug can no longer interact with it, or when cells find new ways to grow that do not depend on the target.

Atezolizumab instead binds PD-L1 and blocks its PD-1 and B7.1 interactions; directly blocking PD-L1 does not directly block the separate PD-1/PD-L2 contact. These target-specific descriptions are more precise than treating all checkpoint drugs as one switch.

Atezolizumab also binds the PD-L1/B7.1 interaction; no universal antibody interaction is invented. points.requirement: Read both complete receiver/exposure figures: the same cytokine can meet different receptors and states, and a local origin can yield distant exposure if signal reaches circulation and persists.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Circulating protein, local formulations and engineered cytokine-producing cells are different exposure strategies. A local origin does not guarantee local confinement: the signal can reach the circulation and persist elsewhere. In Zhang's 2015 dose-escalation study, 33 people with metastatic melanoma received transferred tumour-infiltrating cells engineered with inducible IL-12. Higher cell doses were associated with high serum IL-12 and interferon gamma and serious liver, fever and circulatory toxicities. The finding concerns that construct and regimen; it does not establish the safety or harm of every armoured cell product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A cytokine is a signalling protein, and cytokine treatment supplies the protein or causes cells to produce it. The response depends on the molecule, the receiving receptor system, the cell's previous state and its exposure. A neighbourhood-message analogy is useful only to this extent: receiving a signal does not give a cell the correct cancer target or a literal instruction to fight it. IL-2 can influence lymphocyte growth and activity; interferons have different receptors and effects, so one cytokine name cannot stand for every immune signal.
evidence.explanation: The receiver/state and local-origin/distant-exposure panels are represented together; secretion location is not evidence of confinement. evidence.supportingExcerpt: IL-2 can support regulatory T cells as well as other responding lymphocytes. Boyman and colleagues showed in mice that different IL-2-antibody complexes preferentially expanded different T-cell populations, including CD8 cells or CD4 regulatory T cells. The formulation changed the biological effect. Receptor composition, sensitivity and cell state therefore matter when studying a cytokine design; these mouse experiments do not establish human cancer benefit from every complex or from a larger dose.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: EGFR, also called HER1 or ERBB1, is a receptor tyrosine kinase. Ligand binding outside the cell can change receptor arrangement and the activity of phosphate-transfer machinery inside. Cetuximab binds the extracellular region, whereas an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor acts at the intracellular kinase. An antibody conjugate instead adds a cargo-delivery job to target recognition. Its mechanism and evidence need separate assessment, including any antibody-mediated immune effects. A schematic contact or cargo arrow is not a molecular map of receptor processing, and delivery to a recognised target does not by itself establish dependence on the receptor kinase.

points.requirement: Interpret membrane PI3K conversion of PIP2 to PIP3, PTEN opposition, AKT recruitment and indirect mTORC1 connection, with the dashed feedback brake indirect and not every branch.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K, AKT and mTOR name different parts of a signalling network. In the selected membrane route, PI3K adds a phosphate to the lipid PIP2 to make PIP3; PTEN removes the relevant phosphate and opposes that lipid signal. PIP3 helps recruit proteins including AKT to the membrane. AKT, also called protein kinase B, phosphorylates proteins, and its connection to mTORC1 includes intermediate regulators. mTOR participates in the distinct mTORC1 and mTORC2 complexes. A diagram showing this route leaves other branches out.
evidence.explanation: The membrane lipid conversion, PTEN opposition, AKT recruitment, indirect mTORC1 coupling and nonexhaustive diagram scope are explicit. evidence.supportingExcerpt: O'Reilly and colleagues found that mTOR inhibition relieved feedback inhibition and increased AKT activation in studied cancer cell lines and patient tumour samples. The indirect return path in a network sketch represents a feedback brake, not a direct physical wire or every branch. In a fictional experiment, reduced downstream output with a higher AKT phosphosite signal is compatible with network compensation. Those two measurements alone do not prove that this loop caused the change, that every tumour rebounds or that the drug missed its target; they also do not measure net survival benefit.

points.requirement: CAR T/target/macrophage signalling; vessel cutaway with dashed arrows to blood-pressure and oxygenation; clinical attribution and named ASTCT version supply grade, cytokine concentration does not; no management algorithm.

evidence.explanation: Multicellular inflammatory signalling is interpreted through clinical attribution, competing causes, treated denominator and product-specific observation, not a cytokine curve.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cytokine release syndrome can follow activation by engineered immune cells or T-cell-engaging treatments. Signals from several cell types can contribute to fever, hypotension, hypoxia and other organ effects. Infection or other conditions can produce similar findings or coexist with the syndrome.

evidence.explanation: Multicellular inflammatory signalling is interpreted through clinical attribution, competing causes, treated denominator and product-specific observation, not a cytokine curve.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading CRS without over-reading a cytokine level. CRS is a clinical syndrome, graded from attributed findings and not from a cytokine concentration. In a mouse model of CD19 CAR T-cell CRS, severity was mediated not by CAR T-cell-derived cytokines but by IL-6, IL-1 and nitric oxide from the recipient's macrophages, and IL-1 blockade abated it (Giavridis et al.); that supports a multicell amplification mechanism and does not show the same sources or shares in every human product. Infection and other conditions can cause or accompany the same findings, so the cause of a fever cannot be read from timing alone. A comparable report gives its grading version, observation window and treated denominator, with onset, maximum grade, interventions and resolution. Safety belongs to the product, disease, tumour burden and preparation, so experience with one blood-cancer product does not supply a solid-tumour product's rate, and no severe CRS in a small early study does not rule out uncommon events. CRS is a different problem from injury to healthy tissue that carries the target (on-target, off-tumour) and from neurotoxicity (ICANS). The treatment need not carry a cytokine payload to trigger endogenous inflammatory signalling. Tumour response does not establish acceptable inflammatory risk, and mild CRS does not establish lack of anticancer activity. Stopping a treatment input does not guarantee immediate removal of released signals or established injury. In a fictional early study, no severe CRS and a modest cytokine rise would not make every fever harmless CRS: attribution, clinical findings, a named grading framework, treated denominator and observation window are still needed.

points.requirement: Three panels: gut-brain nerve signalling plus blood-borne and learned inputs; reporting windows 0-24 h and beyond 24 h with overlap; nausea and vomiting as separate outcomes; no vomiting does not establish no nausea.

evidence.explanation: Separate gut/brain and learned pathways support overlapping timing categories; nausea and vomiting remain distinct outcomes.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Nausea and vomiting are different outcomes. Nausea is the sensation and vomiting the expulsion; they often occur together but one can occur without the other. Serotonin acting at 5-HT3 receptors and substance P acting at NK1 receptors contribute with other transmitters, and in two phase II cisplatin studies serotonin appeared to dominate early vomiting and substance P the later phase, with overlap (Hesketh et al.), so acute and delayed are reporting windows and not sealed pathways. The NCI PDQ classes are acute (the first 24 hours after chemotherapy), delayed, anticipatory, breakthrough, refractory and chronic; anticipatory nausea was reported in about 29 per cent of patients and anticipatory vomiting in 11 per cent, with prevalence varying with definitions and methods. It lists other causes too, such as fluid and electrolyte imbalance including hypercalcaemia or volume depletion, and tells clinicians to consider all potential causes when people receive several treatments, so new nausea needs a cause assessment.

evidence.explanation: Separate gut/brain and learned pathways support overlapping timing categories; nausea and vomiting remain distinct outcomes.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Gut-to-brain nerve signalling, blood-borne inputs and learned associations can contribute, so one blocked route does not account for every symptom. The timing terms organise observations. Acute commonly refers to the first 24 hours, delayed to symptoms beyond 24 hours, anticipatory to symptoms before treatment associated with previous experiences, and breakthrough to symptoms despite prevention. Learned symptoms are real; delayed does not mean mild, and early and later responses can overlap with multiday treatment. Prevention and treatment of symptoms that have appeared are different questions. In a fictional trial, no vomiting and no rescue medicine can meet its complete-response endpoint while the participant still reports nausea. Relief of either symptom does not measure tumour response.

points.requirement: Sam: no vomiting, persistent nausea, met endpoint no vomiting/no rescue -> not "no symptoms"; report separately, check window; emetic-risk class != individual certainty.

evidence.explanation: The named Navari regimen and endpoint definitions show why no vomiting/no rescue does not mean no nausea; patient reporting and alternative causes remain visible.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading antiemetic trials. In Navari et al. (380 evaluable chemotherapy-naive adults given cisplatin at 70 mg per square metre or more, or cyclophosphamide-doxorubicin, all with dexamethasone, an NK1 antagonist and a 5-HT3 antagonist), nausea prevention was the primary endpoint and complete response (no emesis and no rescue medication) a secondary one. No nausea in the first 24 hours was 74 per cent with olanzapine against 45 per cent with placebo, while complete response was 86 per cent against 65 per cent, so a complete response does not mean no nausea, and a person with no vomiting can still have persistent nausea. MASCC and ESMO updated their regimen-specific guideline in 2023 (Herrstedt et al., published 2024). Read patient-reported nausea severity, vomiting episodes, rescue-medication use and the observation window together with the preventive regimen and adherence; symptoms that limit drinking or eating warrant prompt contact with the care team. This describes how to read endpoints, not a medicine schedule.

points.requirement: Blood-side signals vs vascular lining/brain side with dashed arrow; ICE and broader domains feed clinical assessment; separate fictional CRS and neurologic timelines with no typical order/duration.

evidence.explanation: Neurologic findings and their timing are assessed separately from CRS, with vascular associations scoped to the Gust cohort and competing causes retained.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, or ICANS, is a neurologic syndrome associated with immune-effector-cell therapy. Changes in language, attention, handwriting or awareness and more severe findings such as seizures need assessment against baseline and alternative explanations. An immune-marker plot does not establish the syndrome.

evidence.explanation: Neurologic findings and their timing are assessed separately from CRS, with vascular associations scoped to the Gust cohort and competing causes retained.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: What is known about mechanism, timing and attribution. In 133 adults given CD19 CAR T cells, Gust et al. found that those with severe neurotoxicity had endothelial activation (disseminated intravascular coagulation, capillary leak) and increased blood-brain barrier permeability, and that the permeable barrier failed to protect the cerebrospinal fluid from high systemic cytokine concentrations including interferon-gamma. Higher risk went with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, high marrow CD19-positive burden, high CAR T-cell dose, CRS and pre-existing neurological disease, and markers of endothelial activation before lymphodepletion were higher in people who later had grade 4 or worse neurotoxicity. That is an association in one product class and population, not a complete mechanism for every treatment. ICANS can accompany CRS or follow its own timetable, and neurotoxicity after CRS is scored separately, so recovery of blood pressure and oxygen does not show neurological recovery. If a person is confused while taking a sedating medicine and the ICE score falls, the grading rule requires that sedation be excluded, so the fall calls for clinical assessment, neither ignored nor diagnosed from the score alone. Clinical assessment also considers infection, metabolic disturbances, medicines and pre-existing neurologic disease. A safety report should retain onset, severity, attributed cause, interventions, duration, recovery and how many people were adequately observed. Separate fictional CRS and neurologic timelines can end at different times; they do not specify a typical order or duration. Stopping an engineered input does not guarantee immediate reversal of established neurologic injury.

points.requirement: Three locations (no depicted effect, gene interruption, regulatory insertion) then fictional clone descendants without assuming cancer; nonviral systems can integrate.

evidence.explanation: Site, vector-copy, expression and pathology measurements have sampling limits; the fictional expanding clone does not itself establish cancer.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: To attribute a malignancy after engineered-cell therapy, investigators ask whether the therapeutic sequence is present in the malignant cells, where the integrations are, whether they alter relevant genes, whether related clones were detectable earlier, and what prior therapy, underlying disease and pre-existing genetic changes contribute. Integration-site sequencing maps insertion locations, quantitative DNA assays estimate vector copies per cell, and flow cytometry, gene-expression measurement and pathology answer different questions about identity, function and malignancy; the sample is consumed by testing. Average vector copy number cannot show the position or effect of each insertion, a clone's frequency depends on the sampled cells, assay sensitivity and time, and blood may not represent every tissue. This record gives no copy-number or clone-frequency threshold because none of the sources read sets one. Messenger RNA delivery that does not integrate does not use genomic insertion as its route, which does not remove its other risks.

evidence.explanation: Site, vector-copy, expression and pathology measurements have sampling limits; the fictional expanding clone does not itself establish cancer.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional follow-up example, an engineered-cell clone becomes more common but no new malignancy has been established. The observation prompts examination of the clone, insertion sites, gene effects and clinical findings. A growth pattern, a malignant diagnosis and an insertion-driven mechanism are separate claims. An insertion that leaves no demonstrated gene effect, one that interrupts a gene and one that alters nearby regulation are different possibilities; none of those schematic locations assigns an incidence or time to cancer. A CAR-positive malignancy can establish product ancestry without identifying which change drove it.

evidence.explanation: Site, vector-copy, expression and pathology measurements have sampling limits; the fictional expanding clone does not itself establish cancer.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

points.requirement: Two fictional ANC curves share day 3 = 0.5 x10^9/L; A brief dip, B days 2-4 at 0.5; no infection probability or G-CSF threshold; same number does not establish same risk.

evidence.explanation: ANC units, depth, duration, timing and fever definition are retained; equal day-three values do not give equal course or infection probability.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading a neutrophil count. The absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is the number of neutrophils per volume of blood, written as cells per microlitre or as times 10 to the ninth per litre; it is more specific than the total white cell count, which includes other cell types. One ANC is a snapshot. Two invented curves make the point: both read 0.5 times 10 to the ninth per litre on day 3, but in one the count dips briefly and recovers, while in the other it stays at that level from day 2 to day 4. The matching number does not mean matching risk, because depth, duration and trend matter, and a count alone neither establishes nor excludes infection. Keep the sampling date, units, the laboratory's reference range and the place in the treatment cycle with the number. NCI patient guidance lists a temperature of 38 degrees Celsius or higher among the signs of infection to report promptly, whatever an earlier count showed. Better counts and fewer infections are related but separate outcomes, and neither is tumour response.

evidence.explanation: ANC units, depth, duration, timing and fever definition are retained; equal day-three values do not give equal course or infection probability.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: For a prevention study, retain the actual anticancer regimen, risk factors, comparator, fever-and-count definition and observation window. A toxicity report needs its count threshold and grading version. The same ANC on one date can conceal different durations of low counts, and an earlier reassuring count does not dismiss new fever or other infection symptoms. Supportive-care benefit, such as fewer infections, is distinct from cancer control.

evidence.explanation: ANC units, depth, duration, timing and fever definition are retained; equal day-three values do not give equal course or infection probability.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fever with neutropenia is defined by a stated temperature and a stated neutrophil threshold, which a trial or guideline should name. A low count alone does not establish infection, and infection can occur without neutropenia, so the count and the fever are separate findings that together define the syndrome and prompt assessment before any source of infection is found.

points.requirement: A DNA-template-based in-vitro transcription route makes RNA, with capping and polyA strategy belonging to the specified process rather than a universal single operation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: An RNA vaccine starts with an approved sequence and product specification.
